title: Publish native entry/return cost per mechanism against Linux syscall and io_uring
justification: Synthesis freeze discipline requires every L1 decision to cite a benchmark report; V0 benchmark gates are publish-only, so the harness runs in CI and publishes numbers without a target.

title: Generate the C header, snapshot, docs and fuzz descriptions from the ABI definition
justification: BLD's syzkaller adaptation (GAP-0127/0548, V0.5) and DOC's IDL-to-docs (V1) both need a single machine-readable Layer 1 definition; ABI owns that source of truth.

title: Reserve the ComputeDevice object type and Operation slots in the Layer 1 ABI
justification: §65 rule 8 and INV-0701: the shape must exist before freeze candidates are named so V2 ComputeDevice dispatch (HET) needs no ABI break; depends on HET's V0 enumeration adr.

title: Run reference, conformance and compatibility suites on the 1.0 candidate and publish
justification: 1.0 exit: ABI reference, conformance suite and compatibility suite pass; compatibility-proof demo of a V4-built native application running unmodified on 1.0.

title: Build the ABI conformance suite with one test per prototyped Layer 1 entry point
justification: BLD's INV-1282 runs an ABI conformance suite in CI; ABI owns its content. Needed before the first ABI revision so v0-to-v0.1 compatibility is proven, not assumed.

title: Extend the conformance suite to every entry point plus cross-version binary runs
justification: V1 SDK compatibility test suite gate needs Layer 1 coverage: binaries built against v0.x run on v1 and vice versa where promised.

title: Build tooling that detects use of deprecated ABI entry points and interfaces in Packages
justification: The deprecation process is unenforceable without detection at build and install; runs in SDK build and PKG install paths from V2.

title: Select Native ABI or Linux ABI execution world per Component or process at entry
justification: Phase B dual personality is needed once the Wayland bridge runs Linux GUI apps beside native apps (V0.5 gate); the world tag lives in the entry layer.

title: Run the conformance suite against wrapper and native implementations during Phase C
justification: Phase C replaces Linux wrappers with native code under a stable ABI; the suite must pass on both implementations for every migrated primitive.

title: Implement the native ABI entry layer in the Linux-derived kernel
justification: Every V0 primitive test reaches the kernel through this layer; implements the chosen entry mechanism and dispatch; Linux syscall path left untouched for the L0 corpus gate.

title: Add build and lint rules forbidding native crates from linking Linux personality or libc
justification: Enforces the §3 compatibility firewall and the §57 non-goals (no POSIX, no Linux syscalls, no Wasm as native ABI) as a lint that runs on every native crate from V0.

title: Review every Layer 1 entry point and mark freeze candidates in the surfaces register
justification: Ladder: L1 freeze candidates at V1 with SDK v1; each candidate must cite its spike, adr and benchmark report per the synthesis freeze discipline.

title: Build the golden binary compatibility suite proving RC1 binaries run on every beta build
justification: V4 exit: a compatibility suite proves binaries built against the freeze candidate run on every subsequent beta build; also the V4 compatibility demo.

title: Exercise Layer 1 evolution: add an Operation, keep the v0 binary running, retain the test
justification: Mirrors the V0.5 UI-protocol v0-to-v0.1 exit criterion at Layer 1 so negotiation is proven against a real change before freeze candidates are named at V1.

title: Implement the Layer 1 version handshake and its forward/backward compatibility test
justification: Critique #12: the V0 negotiation test must be a Layer 1 handshake test, not only an IDL message test; the test is retained permanently as the first ABI conformance case.

title: Implement the Object<T> typed registry with type identifier checked on every Operation
justification: V0 exit: forged handle and wrong-type operations fail with a typed error; depends on decide-handle-encoding and decide-object-residency.

title: Remove deprecated Layer 1 entry points before the freeze candidate
justification: V4 scope: 'Layer 1 ABI freeze candidate: final review, removal of deprecated entry points'; follows the V2 deprecation process and detector results.

title: Institute the ABI review gate checklist enforcing the §65 rules on every L1 change
justification: Critique: constraints become one review-gate task, not a task per rule; the checklist rejects POSIX/Linux/Windows-justified interfaces, flags x86-64 and page-table assumptions, blocks exposed kernel internals and requires a deprecation and shim plan per L1 change.

title: Add CI golden ABI snapshot diff that fails unless the change links an accepted ADR
justification: Makes accidental Layer 1 changes mechanically impossible from the first prototype; snapshot is generated from a machine-readable ABI definition covering entry points, object types and message layouts.

title: Classify public symbols into stability layers and enforce policy in CI
justification: Classifying every public symbol into L1–L4 and enforcing the layer policy is ABI surfaces-register work. build-firewall-lint rejects POSIX names; decide-layer1-scope enumerates L1 versus L2; neither is the classifier. BLD only runs the resulting check. V0.5 with the first immutable packages, not V0.

title: Enforce that native Components cannot invoke Linux syscalls, with a filter test
justification: Phase B verification: once the personality is a product at V1, native components must be shown to run with the Linux syscall world closed; test retained in CI.

title: Classify every public symbol into a stability layer
justification: Surfaces register plus a lint that rejects POSIX-shaped names, Linux syscall numbers and Wayland objects on native surfaces unless an accepted Decision exempts them.

title: Decide the 1.x stability declaration superseding the freeze ADR with 'stable for 1.x'
justification: 1.0 exit: the ABI freeze ADR is amended to 'stable for 1.x' and a public policy states Layer 1 changes require a major version; decisions are immutable so this is a superseding adr.

title: Decide the binding substrate: C-compatible ABI header plus IDL-generated language stubs
justification: Language neutrality (§50) must be fixed before the Rust runtime and C header are built; options include header-only, IDL-only and Rust-native ABI.

title: Decide the Layer 1 and platform deprecation process: announcement, overlap, detection
justification: Store client and third-party packages arrive at V2, so retiring an entry point needs an agreed process before the V4 removal of deprecated entry points.

title: Decide the native ABI entry mechanism and the maximum count of kernel entry points
justification: V0 exit requires accepted ADRs for every architectural choice; bounds the L1 surface per §65 rule 1. Depends on spike-entry-mechanism and bench-entry-overhead. Surface state prototyped, not frozen.

title: Decide the Operation result error model: typed enum per kind or uniform error object
justification: V0 exit requires typed errors for forged handles, denied derivation and Timeout; the error model is one of the five ABI-shape decisions split out of INV-1279 per the critique's hub-splitting advice.

title: Decide Capability handle representation: dense index, sparse id or sealed value
justification: V0 exit names handle representation as a required ADR; options must record CHERI/tagged-memory implications per §8. Takes CAP's GAP-0483 prototype as its spike input. Surface prototyped in V0.

title: Decide whether ABI headers carry a syscall-note-style exception for native programs
justification: Must be accepted alongside SDK's V0.5 licence adr (GAP-0006) before the first third-party native application is built against the header; GOV's licence firewall (GAP-0004) is the input.

title: Decide the Layer 1 freeze: accept the freeze ADR over the reviewed candidate set
justification: V4 exit: 'the freeze ADR is accepted'; critique forbids any L1 freeze before V4; options include freezing the full candidate set, a reduced core, or deferring to 1.0.

title: Decide Layer 1 scope: enumerate L1 primitives and place every concept in L1 or L2
justification: V0 scope requires a stability-layer declaration; answers the L1-vs-L2 question (compositor protocol, package format, ResourceDomain policy) so downstream workstreams know which surfaces are L1.

title: Decide whether Layer 2 interface stability applies at V1 or only at 1.0
justification: SDK v1 and IPC's frozen L2 evolution rules at V1 need this answered so developers know which interfaces may still break before 1.0.

title: Decide object-operation dispatch with async-only submission and move semantics
justification: Fixes how Operations are invoked on typed handles, that no blocking entry exists other than wait-for-completion (rule 4) and how Capability and MemoryObject arguments move (rule 5); depends on the entry, handle and error adrs.

title: Decide which Object<T> types live in the kernel and the kernel-residency criteria
justification: Fixes §65 rule 2 (high-level semantics in user services) as a written criterion so V0 object types are placed deliberately; depends on spike-zircon-object-model.

title: Decide whether the Operation kind set is a closed kernel enum or extensible registry
justification: Operation submission is a V0 exit criterion; the kind set's extensibility rule is an ABI stability property that must precede the entry layer build.

title: Decide how user space identifies an Operation: Capability, ring index or opaque handle
justification: V0 cancellation and deadline exit criteria need a stable way to reference in-flight Operations; coordinated with TSK's completion-delivery adr.

title: Decide the Layer 1 version identification and feature-negotiation scheme
justification: §65 rule 6 requires versioning from V0 and critique contradiction #12 requires a Layer 1 handshake test at V0; this adr defines what the handshake negotiates.

title: Write the normative, versioned native ABI specification v0 defining every entry point
justification: V0 scope 'Native ABI v0 ... stability-layer declaration'; the spec enumerates and bounds the surface and records every surface as prototyped.

title: Revise the ABI specification to v1 with freeze-candidate marking and full semantics
justification: SDK v1 and DOC's IDL-to-docs generation at V1 need a complete normative spec; the entry-point bound from decide-entry-mechanism is re-verified here.

title: Draft the ABI stability statement for RFC review
justification: V4 exit: support policy documents including the ABI stability statement drafted, reviewed via RFC, and accepted.

title: Publish Layer 1 change control: mandatory RFC, compatibility review, per-milestone policy
justification: Heightened change control is needed once the ABI has consumers beyond the V0 demo (four V0.5 apps); complements the mechanical snapshot check with the formal evolution process of §65 rule 10.

title: Publish the deprecation policy per stability layer with notice periods and overlap
justification: V1 exit requires an accepted SDK stability policy; the per-layer policy is its Layer 1 and Layer 2 half and refines GOV's INV-1288 with concrete windows.

title: Review ABI, MemoryObject, ComputeDevice and Capability shapes against future hardware
justification: §70 defining constraint: the 1.0 gate includes a fossilization review against CXL, CHERI, NPU and disaggregated-memory scenarios; findings feed the 2.0 RFC.

title: Define the Layer 1 freeze gate: compat suite, fuzz corpus, semantics, add-vs-change policy
justification: Freeze candidates are named at V1; without a written gate the V4 freeze and the V1 'stable SDK' claim have no verifiable meaning.

title: Complete the Layer 1 reference: documented semantics for 100% of entry points
justification: V3 exit: 100% of Layer 1 entry points have reference pages; ABI authors the normative semantics, DOC generates and publishes.

title: Map every Linux and Windows personality object onto its native Object<T> terminus
justification: Tracks the §4 invariant that all three application paths end in native kernel objects as Phase C translation begins; reviewed with LNX and WIN at each milestone.

title: Lint native surfaces against POSIX-shaped names and Linux syscall numbers
justification: §57/§65: native ABI entries must not exist because POSIX or Linux has an equivalent. ABI lint; BLD would only execute it.

title: Prototype syscall-per-Operation, shared submission page and vDSO trampoline entry
justification: Critique freeze-before-spike rule: the entry-mechanism decision needs a prototype of each option before the adr; produces the three prototypes measured by bench-entry-overhead.

title: Catalogue ABI assumptions that break on CHERI, tagged memory and future architectures
justification: Must precede freeze-candidate review so each candidate carries its escape-hatch analysis; complements CAP's CHERI emulator validation (GAP-0487).

title: Study NT object manager, handles, access masks and I/O request packets
justification: Critique moves non-V0-gating research studies to V0.5; informs the DeviceOperation shape and the WIN personality bring-up planned non-gated at V1.

title: Study Zircon handles, rights, VMOs, channels, FIDL and component framework
justification: Critique keeps the Zircon/Fuchsia study among the six V0 research spikes that inform L1 surfaces; report feeds decide-handle-encoding, decide-object-residency and decide-object-dispatch.

title: Route accessibility actions from AT clients to widgets through the tree
justification: Implements activate, focus, set-value, scroll, expand/collapse and custom actions on tree nodes per the one-tree adr, with round-trip tests; needed before any AT client (V2 screen reader) can act.

title: Implement the Capability<AccessibilityTree> broker with secure-field redaction
justification: Implements the V1 adr: grant issuance via consent, per-app scoping, revocation through SEC's Permissions UI v1, and tree filtering that redacts secure nodes for AT without an elevated grant; tests prove a non-elevated AT cannot read a password field.

title: Extend the assistive-technology script to 50 tasks across shell and every native app
justification: Verifies the V4 gate: 50-task script completes 100% with the screen reader across shell, settings and every shipped native application; also runs under magnifier and high contrast.

title: Write the assistive-technology task script for the four apps and shell settings
justification: Verifies the V2 gate 'task completion script passes 100%' using the tree test driver plus speech capture; seeds the V4 50-task script.

title: Run and report an assistive-technology user study on daily tasks
justification: V4 demo 'an assistive-technology user completes daily tasks across the shell and native apps'; a moderated study with blind and low-vision participants produces a report feeding the RC fix list and the 1.0 evidence dossier.

title: Bridge AT-SPI2 trees of Linux-personality applications into the native tree
justification: Screen reader reads and activates L2/L3 corpus GUI apps through an AT-SPI2 consumer contained in the Linux personality (D-Bus stays inside LNX's bridge); includes AT-SPI2 export of the native tree if decide-at-protocol chose 'both'. §49 requires compat apps to integrate with accessibility.

title: Benchmark focus-change to speech-onset and tree update latency
justification: BEN's anti-fake-claim policy requires any responsiveness statement about the screen reader to live in the register with a method; harness measures focus change to AT notification and to first audio, published beside Orca on Linux on the same hardware, no target claimed.

title: Add braille display output with BRLTTY-equivalent drivers to the screen reader
justification: Braille mode of the screen reader over USB/Bluetooth braille displays; V2 gate needs speech only, so braille lands at V3 to derisk the V4 gate and allow LAB to procure a braille display.

title: Add accessibility scoring to L5 and W3 corpus integration checks
justification: The 1.0 compatibility gate requires 'accessibility where the toolkit exposes it' for every passing Linux and Windows entry; adds a screen-reader read-and-activate check to LNX/WIN scenario scoring using the bridges.

title: Audit shell, installer, greeter, lock screen and every native app against the checklist
justification: Runs the V3 checklist over every first-party surface, tracks fixes to closure, and verifies keyboard-only operation of the entire shell and high-contrast rendering across shell and apps as the V4 exit requires.

title: Author the EN 301 549 / WCAG 2.2 AA checklist and assess EU Accessibility Act duties
justification: Defines the checklist every first-party surface is audited against and, with GOV, maps the EU Accessibility Act obligations for operating systems to the conformity evidence 1.0 must publish. V3 scopes out conformance claims, so this is the internal instrument, not a claim.

title: Publish the accessibility conformity evidence and hold V4 gates on the release build
justification: 1.0 exit requires the V4 accessibility gates to hold on the release build and GAP-0077 requires conformity evidence at 1.0: re-run the 50-task script and keyboard-only verification, then publish the EN 301 549 conformance report and EU Accessibility Act evidence with GOV.

title: Decide assistive-technology access as Capability<AccessibilityTree> with redaction
justification: Decides one thing: AT reach the tree only through a consent-scoped Capability, with password/secure fields redacted unless an elevated grant is held. Options: per-app grants; session-wide grant with secure-field redaction; ambient bus (rejected per §9). Includes the AT keylogging/screen-scraping threat analysis as an addendum to SEC's threat model. Must precede the V2 broker and screen reader.

title: Decide the assistive-technology protocol: AT-SPI compatible, native, or both
justification: Decides one thing: how AT clients reach the tree (native typed Channel only, AT-SPI2 export, or both). Options enumerated per GAP-0554. Separate from the schema decision; must land before the V1 UI protocol freeze candidates and drives the V3 bridge design.

title: Decide whether semantic actions and accessibility actions share one tree
justification: Answers the §42 question with options: single tree with actions typed by the semantic registry; two trees with a consistency contract; a11y tree as a projection of the semantic tree. Must precede action-dispatch and the V1 L2 freeze candidates; needs SEM's V1 registry design as input.

title: Decide the accessibility tree model shared by the toolkit and semantic interfaces
justification: Decides one thing: the tree contract (roles, states, properties, actions, live regions, text ranges) and whether AccessKit is the schema. Options: adopt AccessKit; native schema with AccessKit export; native only. Critique ordering fix requires acceptance before the UI protocol L2 freeze; V0.5 emission gate depends on it.

title: Decide the text-to-speech engine for the native screen reader
justification: Decides one thing: the speech engine (options: espeak-ng, Piper, vendor voices, pluggable with a default). Scheduled at V1 so the V2 speech service can be built on it; GOV licence policy is an input.

title: Publish accessibility guidelines for native application developers
justification: SDK v1 ships at V1; developers need labelling, role, focus, contrast and reduced-motion guidance so third-party apps meet the V3 checklist. Content owned by ACC, published through DOC's pipeline.

title: Define and implement the focus order and keyboard traversal contract
justification: Required by the V4 gate 'keyboard-only operation of the entire shell verified' and the V2 screen reader prototype, which tracks focus; focus order is derived from the tree, focus-visible indication is mandatory, and traversal rules are testable. ACC scope: keyboard-only.

title: Add sticky, slow and bounce keys, mouse keys and dwell click to input routing
justification: Keyboard and pointer accommodations implemented in UIP's input routing layer under ACC's settings so they apply to native, Linux and Windows windows alike; required by the V3 checklist and V4 script.

title: Add os inspect accessibility tree dump and the four-app tree dump test
justification: Verifies the V0.5 gate: role/name/state for every widget inspectable via os inspect, with a CI tree-dump test on Terminal, File Browser, Text Editor and Image Viewer.

title: Make installer, greeter, lock screen and recovery operable by the screen reader
justification: GAP-0266 requires the screen reader from the first installer screen; the graphical installer, greeter and recovery environment arrive at V3, so the speech service and reader must be present in the live image and start on a keystroke, with INS and APP.

title: Build the screen magnifier with focus and caret tracking
justification: Compositor-level magnification (with GFX) driven by focus and caret positions from the tree; V4 gate lists the magnifier and the V3 checklist requires it.

title: Build the native screen reader: focus tracking, navigation modes, review cursor
justification: First AT client consuming the tree through the Capability broker: announces focus and state changes, live regions, text ranges in the editor, browse/focus modes and a review cursor. Verified by the V2 exit criterion that it reads and activates every widget in the four apps and shell settings.

title: Make the screen reader an accessibility client of semantic interfaces
justification: Uses SEM's V1 registry so the screen reader can list and invoke semantic actions (e.g. Editor.open, Terminal.run) without simulating input, proving §42's accessibility consumer; depends on the V1 semantic interface v0.

title: Build the speech Component with voice selection, queueing and interruption
justification: Text-to-speech service on the decided engine, exposed as a typed interface; utterance queue, priority interruption, rate/pitch/voice settings. Required by the V2 screen reader prototype gate.

title: Evaluate AccessKit as accessibility tree schema and bridge against a native schema
justification: Prototype derives role/name/state for the V0.5 toolkit widgets through AccessKit and through a hand-rolled schema, measuring schema fit, licence, Rust maturity and bridge coverage; must precede decide-tree-schema and decide-at-protocol (critique: a11y adr before the UI protocol L2 freeze).

title: Prototype consuming AT-SPI2 and Wine UIA/MSAA trees into the native tree
justification: Feasibility on one GTK app and one Wine app: node mapping fidelity, event latency, D-Bus containment inside the Linux personality, and the security boundary between compat trees and the Capability broker; precedes the V3 bridge builds.

title: Measure espeak-ng, Piper and vendor voices for latency, quality, footprint, licence
justification: Prototype each engine as a sandboxed Component and publish time-to-first-audio, CPU/memory, voice quality and licence findings; must precede decide-tts-engine.

title: Complete tree derivation: properties, text ranges, live regions, incremental diffs
justification: Extends automatic derivation beyond role/name/state to the full schema and ships incremental update notifications so AT clients are not re-sent whole trees; prerequisite for the V2 screen reader reading the Text Editor.

title: Build the accessibility tree crate and derive it from the declarative UI tree
justification: Implements the accepted schema as the crate the UIP toolkit emits through, deriving role/name/state automatically from the declarative widget tree so apps need no per-widget work; required for the V0.5 exit criterion that every widget emits metadata. Widget-side wiring stays in UIP.

title: Build a scripted test driver that operates applications through the tree
justification: GAP-0261 rationale names testing as a tree consumer; the V2 'task completion script' and V4 50-task script need a driver that navigates and activates via the accessibility tree rather than synthetic input. Also lets APP acceptance scenarios exercise a11y for free.

title: Bridge UI Automation and MSAA exposed by Wine into the native tree
justification: Screen reader reads W2 corpus applications via Wine's UIA/MSAA implementation mapped into the native schema; coordinated with WIN, gated on the V3 W2 integration checks.

title: Enforce high contrast, large text, reduced motion, colour filters and cursor size
justification: Accessibility settings service stored via SVC settings storage, surfaced in the V2 Settings app and enforced by the toolkit theme tokens so every native app complies without per-app work; prerequisite for the V3 checklist and the V4 'high contrast across shell and native apps' gate.

title: Prototype voice control and switch access over semantic actions
justification: Parking rung for alternative input modalities not in the 1.0 definition; they build on semantic actions and the tree test driver rather than synthetic input, so they are cheap once SEM and ACC infrastructure exists.

title: Add CI lint failing on unlabelled or roleless interactive widgets
justification: Turns the standing rule that every UI element carries accessibility metadata into an enforced gate at SDK v1: toolkit and first-party apps fail CI on missing role, name or state.

title: Publish warm and cold startup for the four native applications
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate measures native application warm and cold startup (B-016, B-017) for each of the four apps and publishes; APP owns the per-app harness, BEN owns methodology.

title: Publish notification, lock and launcher latencies against desktop baselines
justification: V2 benchmark gates: application warm startup for all shipped native apps (B-016) and unlock-to-interactive-desktop (B-033). BEN GAP-0319 names notification post-to-display and lock-to-unlock; APP instruments the shell.

title: Build the Settings About panel with notices and license texts
justification: GAP-0279 About panel. INS GAP-0014 requires an About/licenses view exposing license texts and the GPL written offer; APP hosts that panel in Settings.

title: Polish the desktop shell and applications for external alpha users
justification: V3 §63 polished desktop ready for external users (enthusiasts, developers, researchers). Closes remaining P0/P1 in shell and first-party apps on Tier 1.

title: Build the automation-rule editor over Semantic interfaces
justification: §45 user-facing automation editor. Depends on done SEM registry and rules engine (V2); no AI broker. Users create and inspect rules without GUI scraping.

title: Build the backup and restore UI over snapshot-based user-data backup
justification: Critique missing requirement 35: user-data backup to external or network targets as STO/APP at V3. APP owns schedule/progress/restore UI; STO owns encrypted snapshot backup.

title: Integrate the default browser with URL dispatch, downloads and chooser
justification: V2 browser integration: default-browser registration, URL dispatch, downloads into capability-scoped locations, WebRTC camera/microphone through native capabilities, file-chooser portal. Widevine CDM is MED/LNX.

title: Build the OS-owned file chooser UI minting UserSelected capabilities
justification: V0.5 gate: Image Viewer opens a user-chosen image via UserSelected and cannot enumerate the directory. APP owns the privileged chooser UI; STO owns UserSelected authority minting (§25).

title: Build clipboard history with sensitive-item exclusion
justification: V2 clipboard history as a privileged shell feature; sources mark entries ephemeral and excluded from history and sync. UIP owns clipboard Capability policy.

title: Integrate Linux personality Git, browser and IDE into launcher and chooser
justification: V1 scope: Git and a browser via the Linux personality integrated into launcher, clipboard and file chooser (APP, LNX). Availability is LNX; this is the APP integration half.

title: Build the trusted consent prompt UI for Capability requests
justification: Workstreams.md Applications sub-scope: consent UI (policy in SEC). V2 gate and demo: permissions prompt for camera/microphone/files/network/screen capture, deny without crash. GFX GAP-0228 protects the trusted Surface.

title: Build the default-application picker over the system registry
justification: GAP-0279 default-apps panel. SVC owns the headless default-application registry (GAP-0280 reassigned from PKG); APP owns the picker that grants a Capability to just the opened object.

title: Build the demo native Text Editor
justification: V0.5 exit and §60 demo require a native Text Editor with declarative UI, a11y metadata, and scripted acceptance; kernel-scale editing is V1.

title: Build the demo native Terminal on the system text stack
justification: V0.5 exit requires a demo native Terminal that passes scripted scenarios. Daily-driving feature bar (tabs, splits, OSC 8, Sixel/Kitty) waits for V1.

title: Build the demo Image Viewer with an isolated decoder Component
justification: V0.5 gate: Image Viewer starts with UI and GPU capabilities only, opens a UserSelected image, and decodes in an isolated Component (§11, §60).

title: Build desktop search as a Background-intent Component
justification: Critique: desktop search/indexing is APP with STO. Background-intent Component over storage capabilities powers launcher search without ambient home access. STO GAP-0315 is the store-side index service.

title: Extend Text Editor for kernel and platform development on the OS
justification: V1 exit: editor/IDE usable for kernel and platform development on the OS. Native Text Editor must open the OS tree, search, and jump to diagnostics; Linux personality IDEs are LNX.

title: Build the emoji picker as an input-method protocol client
justification: V2 emoji and special-character picker invoked by a global shortcut, committing text through the same input-method protocol. TXT owns IME protocol; this is the system picker client.

title: Freeze remaining native application and shell features for 1.0
justification: V4 feature freeze after RC1: every APP feature in the 1.0 definition is done; no new shell or first-party application features after freeze.

title: Build the privileged File Browser that hands out storage capabilities
justification: V0.5 demo native File Browser using capability-based storage objects (§60). The browser is a privileged holder of user storage authority and can hand Capabilities to other apps; UIP owns drag/drop protocol.

title: Implement the native first-party applications selected by the set Decision
justification: GAP-0318 ADR at V2 selects which of viewer/player/archive/calculator/camera/disk utility/system monitor are native. V3 public alpha needs that native subset shipped; compat-bundled remainder is LNX/WIN.

title: Build a grant log viewer for Capability audit events
justification: V1 scope out says permissions UI beyond a log viewer; the log viewer itself is in. Full revoke/expiry/timeline Settings surface is V2 GAP-0229.

title: Build the Settings grant surface with revocation, expiry and timeline
justification: V2 permissions UI v1: list every persistent Capability grant per application with revocation, expiry and usage timeline from the audit trail. Policy is SEC; this is the user-facing surface.

title: Build the login greeter UI over the identity service
justification: Workstreams.md Shell sub-scope includes greeter. GAP-0283 session management; SEC GAP-0215 owns identity/password/FIDO2. APP owns the compositor-integrated greeter chrome.

title: Hold shell and native application quality through the 1.0 soak
justification: 1.0 exit: V4 a11y and localisation gates hold on the release build; 30-day soak with zero open P0/P1 on Tier 1 includes shell and first-party apps. Compatibility integration (launcher, taskbar, notifications, file chooser) still holds.

title: Build persistent in-use indicators for camera, microphone and screen share
justification: V2 gate: screen sharing shows a persistent indicator; MED camera service requires a shell in-use indicator. APP owns the shell chrome; GFX/SEC own the screen-capture Capability.

title: Localize the shell and shipped native applications to ten languages
justification: V4 exit: 10 languages at ≥ 95% string coverage for shell and native apps. TXT owns the localisation pipeline; APP ships translations for every first-party surface.

title: Extend the launcher with search and Personality icons
justification: V2 shell: launcher with search. Windows and Linux apps appear with extracted icons (PE resources, .desktop icons) and no separate desktop (§49).

title: Build the native launcher importing Linux personality .desktop entries
justification: V1 scope: Git and a browser integrated into the launcher. Import .desktop entries so Linux packages appear as launchable native-chrome apps. Search and Personality icon polish are V2.

title: Build the compositor-enforced lock screen UI
justification: V2 lock screen: idle-triggered, lock-before-suspend, notification privacy, authentication via SEC identity. GFX GAP-0216 owns compositor enforcement that no app Surface renders above the lock.

title: Build the media session shell controls bound to media keys
justification: V2 shell media session (play/pause/next, now-playing) bound to hardware media keys and Bluetooth AVRCP. MPRIS bridge is LNX; AVRCP is HW/AUD; APP owns the shell surface.

title: Build the migration assistant UI over the installer import engine
justification: Workstreams.md Applications sub-scope and critique MIG split: APP owns migration assistant UI; INS GAP-0414/0415 own Windows-profile and Linux-home import engines.

title: Build multi-user session switching with separate Capability stores
justification: V3 exit: two users with separate sessions, Capability stores and encrypted data; switching preserves state. SEC owns session objects; APP owns switcher/greeter chrome for the second session.

title: Build the Notify service with Capability-gated posting and history
justification: V1 daily-driving and L2 integration need notifications. Typed Notify interface requires Capability<Notifications>, semantic actions, do-not-disturb, persistent history, and survival across compositor restart. LNX owns compat bridges.

title: Build power and battery UX mapped to ResourceDomain energy policy
justification: V2 laptop gate judged through this UI: battery estimates, power profiles mapped to ResourceDomain energy policy, per-application energy attribution, low-battery actions, lid-close, charge limits. PWR owns the mechanisms.

title: Build the OS-owned print dialog minting per-job print capabilities
justification: Critique PRT split: APP owns the print dialog that grants Capability<PrintJob> for a single job the way the file chooser grants file authority. HW GAP-0268 owns discovery (IPP/eSCL/USB).

title: Build quick settings and status indicators
justification: GAP-0282 and workstreams.md Shell sub-scope: quick settings and status indicators (network, battery, volume, Bluetooth, input method) for the V2 polished shell.

title: Build the safe-mode recovery shell with settings, logs and restore
justification: Critique missing requirement 16 and workstreams.md: when shell or compositor exhausts its restart budget, SVC starts a minimal recovery shell. APP owns that recovery UI (settings, log export, os restore).

title: Build screenshot and screen-recording UI over screen-capture Capability
justification: V2 screen sharing and recording as explicit capabilities with indicator. APP owns the user-facing capture UI; GFX/SEC own the Capability; MED owns encode.

title: Expose Semantic interfaces for Terminal.run and Editor.open
justification: V1 gate: an automation script invokes Terminal.run and Editor.open through typed interfaces without GUI input. SEM owns registry and IDL; APP implements the two proof interfaces.

title: Build logout, shutdown, inhibitors, auto-login and session restore
justification: V2 session management: logout/shutdown/reboot with inhibitors, session restore, optional auto-login, fast user switching. Identity and FDE are SEC; generation restore UX is INS.

title: Build a minimal session host that launches the four demo applications
justification: V0.5 demo boots to a native desktop showing Terminal, File Browser, Text Editor and Image Viewer. Critique warns against a full shell here; this is a session host, not panel/launcher/lock.

title: Build the Settings application chassis as per-panel Components
justification: V2 Settings application composed of per-panel Components each holding only that panel's capabilities (§11). Chassis plus appearance, keyboard, region, date/time, about; device panels are a sibling task.

title: Build Settings panels for displays, network, Bluetooth, sound and printers
justification: GAP-0279 remaining panels that consume GFX/NET/HW/AUD device services. Each panel is a Component with only its panel's capabilities; discovery stacks stay in those prefixes.

title: Build on-screen display overlays for volume, brightness and lock
justification: V2 polished shell (workstreams.md Shell sub-scope, §62): hardware volume/brightness/lock keys must show OSD overlays without granting apps a global overlay Capability.

title: Build the desktop panel and taskbar with Personality integration
justification: V2 polished shell (§62): panel/taskbar. Windows and Linux applications must integrate with the native taskbar (§49). Sibling tasks cover launcher, workspaces, quick settings and tray.

title: Build the Settings UI for named global shortcut bindings
justification: UIP GAP-0286: apps request named actions bound by the user in Settings and never receive raw global key grabs. APP owns the Settings binding UI for the V2 shell (media, screenshots, picker).

title: Build the store client with install-time Capability review
justification: V2 gate: native repository/app store client; capability requests shown and deniable at install, app still launches degraded when optional. Workstreams.md Applications sub-scope. REL/PKG own repository and packages (INV-1228).

title: Extend Terminal for daily development with tabs, splits and graphics
justification: V1 self-hosted terminal for daily development. Feature bar (GPU text, tabs/splits, OSC 8, Sixel/Kitty, true colour, PTY bridge) is the V1 daily-driving gate, not the V0.5 demo.

title: Build a thin panel with a running-application list for daily driving
justification: V1 scope sentence requires a shell mature enough for daily work. This is a running-app list, not the V2 polished panel with status indicators.

title: Build the status-tray host according to the tray Decision
justification: Implements decide-status-tray. Linux and Windows tray clients must either appear in the native host or be explicitly denied; the Decision is accepted before this ships.

title: Build the running-application update prompt for generation switches
justification: Critique missing requirement 17 and PKG EXTRA-017: when a Package is replaced by a new SystemGeneration, APP shows the restart/defer prompt so no running Component observes a mixed-version tree.

title: Run the 40-scenario desktop UX script on the three target machines
justification: V2 exit: desktop shell passes the 40-scenario UX script (launch, switch, notify, settings, lock, unlock, external display, scaling) on all three target machines with zero P0/P1. Verifies the polished shell (§62).

title: Build the sandboxed native WebView Component
justification: GAP-0307 native sandboxed WebView for apps, after the V1 browser ADR and spike-webview. Not a native browser; in-app web content as a Capability-scoped Component.

title: Build a window switcher usable for daily development
justification: V1 scope: Terminal, editor and shell mature enough for daily work; L2 integration check includes the task switcher. Full workspaces and overview wait for V2.

title: Build virtual workspaces, overview and window layout
justification: GAP-0282 enumerates virtual workspaces, window switcher and overview as V2 shell parts; V2 40-scenario UX script includes launch and switch on three target machines.

title: Decide browser strategy for 1.0 and the native WebView Component
justification: §56.5 makes a browser existential; V1 daily-driving needs one. Options: Chromium and/or Firefox through the Linux personality, a native port, or both, plus whether apps get a sandboxed WebView. 1.0 does not promise a native browser.

title: Decide the first-party application set native versus bundled at 1.0
justification: Must precede V3 native first-party builds. Options: native versus bundled compat for document/PDF viewer, media player, archive manager, calculator, camera, disk utility, system monitor. Native subset must stay splittable.

title: Decide which foreign package formats map to Personality launches
justification: V2 gate: double-click a Windows .exe from File Browser and it launches with native chrome. ADR maps .exe, .msi, .AppImage, .deb, .rpm, Flatpak to Personality launches with no compatibility wizard (§49).

title: Decide IDE strategy for 1.0 and the criteria for a native port
justification: Answers INV-1106: VS Code/JetBrains through the Linux personality versus a native editor/IDE, and switch criteria. V1 needs a usable IDE for self-hosting; 1.0 does not promise a native IDE.

title: Decide the shared PDF renderer for viewer, thumbnails and print preview
justification: pdfium, poppler or a Rust renderer used by document viewer, file-browser thumbnails and print preview. APP owns those surfaces; the library choice is one Decision.

title: Decide status-tray policy: StatusNotifierItem compatibility versus none
justification: GAP-0282 requires a status-tray policy ADR (StatusNotifierItem compat versus none) before the V2 shell ships; the Decision precedes tray-host and Linux/Windows tray integration.

title: Document first-party applications as Component graphs
justification: Workstreams.md Applications sub-scope and §11 require first-party apps to be Component graphs (isolated decoder, chooser, PTY). Written so V0.5 apps dogfood the model instead of becoming monoliths.

title: Publish 1.0 non-goals for accounts, parental controls and dictation
justification: GAP-0321 nongoal: online-account integration, parental controls and speech dictation are out of 1.0 with only Semantic-interface hooks reserved. Collapses the nongoal into the published 1.0 non-promise list.

title: Publish post-1.0 non-goals for casting, NFC, WWAN and MIDI
justification: Critique missing requirement 37 and ladder LATER parking: casting (Miracast/Chromecast/AirPlay), NFC, WWAN/eSIM and MIDI/pro-audio appear in the published non-goal list. AUD/HW own any later mechanism work.

title: Prototype a PTY bridge that scopes Linux personality tools to Terminal
justification: V0.5 Terminal must host Linux CLI tools inside a native window without giving the Terminal ambient filesystem or network authority; LNX GAP-0311 decides the V1 policy, this spike feeds the demo Terminal.

title: Prototype capability-scoped desktop search without ambient home access
justification: Critique assigns desktop search to APP with STO. An indexer with ambient home-directory access would violate §9; this spike bounds what EXTRA-044 may index before the search Component is built. STO GAP-0315 is the store-side index.

title: Prototype session restore of application windows from system history
justification: GAP-0283 session restore and PKG GAP-0544 (application-state restore vs 1.0 non-goal) need a measured prototype before session-flows commits to reopening windows from history.

title: Prototype a sandboxed native WebView Component for in-app web content
justification: GAP-0307 requires the browser ADR to choose a native sandboxed WebView versus personality-only web content; the spike must precede the ADR at the same V1 rung.

title: Apply ducking and exclusive-mode audio focus
justification: V2 desktop preview and L3 conferencing need interruption policy on the mixer: duck, pause and exclusive LowLatency for games and calls. APP media-session UI consumes this; AUD enforces it on AudioStream.

title: Ship PipeWire and PulseAudio compatibility on AudioStream
justification: §47 and V1 scope require PulseAudio and PipeWire compatibility with a PipeWire server on native audio objects. Shape follows the object-model adr: either PipeWire is native and exports AudioStream, or a PipeWire/Pulse server is a personality client of the native service. LNX owns personality product wiring; this task is the AUD-side bridge.

title: Decide native AudioStream service versus PipeWire-as-native
justification: V1 gates require an accepted audio object-model adr and Object<AudioStream> (§7). Options are at least (1) PipeWire as the native server wrapping AudioStream and (2) a native AudioStream service with PipeWire as a Linux personality client; the spike's B-028 comparison is an input. This is the baseline-gap scope adr for AUD (§22, §32, §47).

title: Decide which audio device classes run in user space
justification: INV-0616 is evaluate-then-implement. Record which classes (USB, HDMI, Bluetooth offload, onboard) stay on retained ALSA versus a user-space driver hosted by SVC, using the spike report. Options must include keep-in-kernel for 1.0 and user-space USB.

title: Document native and personality audio mapping
justification: V3 public documentation includes the compatibility guide. AUD writes how AudioStream, PipeWire/PulseAudio and WASAPI map, which grants are required, and how restart/rebind behaves. DOC/SDK own publishing and IDL pages.

title: Deny microphone use without an explicit Capability
justification: INV-0205 is the §9.1 no-ambient-authority invariant for microphone access. Collapse it into a grant test: a native component with no capture Capability receives Error::Rights, allocates no stream, and appears in the audit log. Prompt UI remains SEC/APP.

title: Ship AudioStream conformance tests for the freeze
justification: V4 freezes Layer 1 and locks Layer 2 interface versions. AudioStream is a §7 kernel object explored by the V1 spike/adr; this task is the conformance suite for rights, rebind, mixer and personality bridges. ABI/IPC own the freeze adr; AUD owns the audio cases.

title: Build audio round-trip latency and glitch harness
justification: V1 benchmark gate for B-028 (bench:audio-roundtrip): loopback round trip and a ten-minute glitch run on the native path, published beside PipeWire on Linux on the same hardware. BEN owns the register; AUD owns this harness.

title: Measure Bluetooth audio latency on the native path
justification: V2 benchmark gate for B-029 audio latency (pairing cycles stay with HW). Loopback latency per negotiated codec on the Intel and AMD laptops; publish beside BlueZ plus PipeWire on Linux.

title: Implement restartable audio server with stream rebind
justification: §32 names the audio server as a critical restartable service. AUD implements the server as a supervised component whose clients disconnect, rebind and restore streams without ending the session; SVC owns the supervisor. B-024 remains BEN's harness; this task supplies the audio rebind path the V1 daily-driving gate needs.

title: Host USB audio in user space within the latency budget
justification: INV-0616 implement-where-acceptable clause. If the adr accepts user-space USB audio, ship it as a capability-scoped component on the V2 machines and keep B-028 inside the budget the adr records. If the adr rejects it, this task drops with that reason.

title: Implement Object<AudioStream> with play and capture rights
justification: V1 scope is native audio objects. After the object-model adr, ship Object<AudioStream> and Capability rights for playback, capture and route so native components hold typed streams rather than ALSA or PipeWire handles. os inspect must show live streams, devices and holders.

title: Implement the LowLatency capture-to-playback audio path
justification: V1 scope and the V1 functional gate require a native low-latency path distinct from the compatibility server. Bind AudioStream callbacks to LowLatency intent (§22); SCH owns the scheduler class. Needed before the B-028 harness can run.

title: Isolate audio routing per login session
justification: V3 multi-user gate: two sessions with separate capability stores must not share capture or playback. Route AudioStream and the mixer per login session; SEC owns identity, AUD owns the graph.

title: Measure native AudioStream versus PipeWire round-trip latency
justification: GAP-0539 requires a latency measurement before choosing PipeWire as the native audio server or as a personality client of a native AudioStream service. V0.5 scopes audio out and V0 is capped at zero AUD tasks, so this L1-object spike sits at V1 with the object-model adr. Report compares both topologies on the reference desktop using the B-028 method; cite the B-ID, never a number.

title: Measure user-space audio-driver latency against ALSA
justification: INV-0616 and §33 require a measured latency budget before moving audio devices out of the kernel. Compare user-space USB audio against in-kernel ALSA on B-028; HW's USB-driver spike is the sibling, not a substitute.

title: Implement per-application volume mixer
justification: EXTRA-022 and the AUD workstream mixer sentence. Per-application gain on AudioStream, inspectable and overridable from settings UI (APP owns the widget). Include a mix-monitor stream so later screen-recording and echo-cancellation can take a far-end reference.

title: Park MIDI and pro-audio until after 1.0
justification: Critique missing requirement 37: MIDI and pro-audio are explicit 1.0 non-goals so they appear on the published non-goal list. APP EXTRA-038 covers the combined declaration; this parks the AUD-owned remainder (MIDI ports, Jack/pro-audio graphs) on LATER.

title: Provide echo-cancellation and noise-suppression pipeline
justification: Critique missing requirement 23 and EXTRA-023: conferencing in the L3 corpus needs AEC and noise suppression shared with MED. AUD owns the capture/playback graph and mix-monitor reference; MED owns video encode and the camera service.

title: Ship native playback and capture on reference hardware
justification: INV-1204 and the V1 developer-preview gate require audio output and input for native applications on the AMD desktop and Intel laptop. Uses retained kernel ALSA devices (KRN inventory) behind AudioStream; does not expose ALSA as a native API.

title: Publish audio round-trip versus Linux, Windows and macOS
justification: 1.0 requires every §54 metric published on Tier 1 against Linux, Windows and macOS. Re-run B-028 (and B-029 audio latency) with the existing harnesses; no superiority claim without the report.

title: Convert sample rate, format and channel layout on mix
justification: V1 native-plus-PipeWire simultaneous playback cannot hold a single hardware format without resampling and channel mapping in the mixer. Required plumbing for the V1 functional audio gate, not a new codec framework (MED).

title: Restore playback and capture after suspend and resume
justification: V1 exit requires audio functional after 200 laptop and 100 desktop suspend cycles. AUD reopens devices and rebinds streams; PWR owns the suspend cycle. No new device stack.

title: Route Bluetooth audio with per-device codec selection
justification: V2 scope is Bluetooth audio via the user-space stack (HW owns BlueZ/native placement and pairing). AUD routes A2DP and HFP onto AudioStream and exposes codec selection (SBC, AAC, aptX, LDAC, LC3) from EXTRA-022. Headset reconnect is a V2 Bluetooth gate.

title: Score audio integration on L5 and W3 corpus entries
justification: 1.0 compatibility gate requires audio in the integration score for every passing Linux and Windows entry. AUD supplies native-object probes used by LNX/WIN scenario scripts.

title: Serve native AudioStream to the Windows personality
justification: INV-0925 and §49: Windows applications integrate with native audio. AUD exposes AudioStream so WIN can map WASAPI/XAudio2 (INV-1075 stays in WIN). Needed for W1 integration scoring and the V2 gaming proof.

title: Switch default device on jack, display and USB hot-plug
justification: Critique missing requirement 22 and EXTRA-022: headphone jack, HDMI/DP and USB hot-plug must retarget the default route without restarting clients. Bluetooth codec selection waits for V2 because V1 scopes Bluetooth out. Needed for Intel-laptop daily-driving with USB-C displays.

title: Verify Linux GUI applications play through native AudioStream
justification: INV-0881 and the V1 gate that native and PipeWire streams play together without glitches. Script L2 GUI entries so audio is scored through native AudioStream, not a leftover Linux-only path from V0.5.

title: Verify audio on every V4 Tier 1 machine
justification: V4 hardware gate: the full suite including audio on at least ten Tier 1 machines each RC. Extends the V3 matrix across two GPU generations and NVIDIA HDMI audio; no new architecture.

title: Verify playback and capture on every V3 Tier 1 machine
justification: V3 hardware breadth and the public-alpha demo (Bluetooth headset, video call) require jack, HDMI/DP, USB and Bluetooth audio on all six Tier 1 machines, including the NVIDIA desktop. Probe output feeds REL's HCL.

title: Publish 1.0 cross-OS comparison on every Tier 1 machine
justification: 1.0 exit and definition: every §54 metric published for every Tier 1 machine against Linux, Windows where dual-boot exists, and macOS where a comparable class exists, including L5 and W3 overhead and energy.

title: Verify no V4 benchmark regression at 1.0
justification: 1.0 benchmark gate: no regression beyond the register band versus V4 final on any tracked benchmark on any Tier 1 machine; any exception is an accepted Decision referenced in the release notes. Harness B-051.

title: Publish native application startup and input-to-photon
justification: V0.5 gates for warm and cold launch of Terminal, Editor, Image Viewer and the SDK sample, plus input-to-photon on the four demo apps, using the visible-UI boundary. Publish-only; V1 sets the B-016 absolute. Harnesses B-016, B-017 and B-020 on the demo set.

title: Publish boot time to login on every Tier 1 machine
justification: V3 gate: boot time to login on each of the six Tier 1 machines beside a mainline Linux distribution and Windows where dual-boot exists. Extends B-032 from V0.5/V2 hardware.

title: Publish boot-to-login and unlock-to-desktop latency
justification: Verity, measured boot and encryption add boot cost; §54 requires the claim be measured. Harnesses B-032 and B-033 on V2 target machines beside Linux and Windows where dual-boot exists. Numbers live only in the register.

title: Publish full-image build time on the OS versus Linux
justification: V1 benchmark gate and self-hosting exit: clean and incremental full-image build time inside os env versus Linux on the same hardware. Harness B-039.

title: Publish compositor frame and input-to-photon latency
justification: V0.5 gates for commit-to-scanout latency, deadline behaviour and photodiode input-to-photon beside a Linux Wayland desktop on the same machine. Consumes LAB's V0 rig. Harnesses B-018 and B-020.

title: Publish ComputeDevice dispatch overhead
justification: V2 ComputeDevice demo must not ship an unmeasured dispatch path. Harness B-048 versus direct Vulkan compute and a native thread pool.

title: Publish crash-free session rate from opt-in telemetry
justification: V3 gate: crash-free session rate from opt-in telemetry over the stated window and fleet size. Harness B-041; OBS/REL collect, BEN publishes against the register target.

title: Publish compositor frame-deadline miss rate
justification: V2 benchmark gate: deadline misses under a scripted mixed desktop workload at 60 Hz. Harness B-019; target lives only in the register.

title: Publish desktop-essentials latency suite
justification: V2 desktop preview: keystroke-to-glyph through the IME path, notification post-to-display, lock-to-unlock, Wi-Fi reconnect after resume, Bluetooth audio connect and camera cold start. Harness B-045.

title: Publish energy use on the Intel laptop
justification: V1 battery gate: idle, video, compile and browsing watt-hours on the Intel laptop beside a mainline Linux distribution on the same machine, using spike-energy-method and LAB meters. Harness B-031; no superiority claim.

title: Publish energy use on both V2 laptops
justification: V2 gates: idle desktop energy and mixed-workload battery runtime on both laptops beside mainline Linux and Windows where dual-boot exists. Extends B-031 from the V1 Intel laptop.

title: Publish os env startup against Docker Compose
justification: V1 gate and §35: cached os env enter versus docker compose up for the reference stack, with cold published separately. Harness B-025.

title: Publish disk-encryption overhead on NVMe
justification: Encryption by default is only defensible if sequential and random NVMe cost is measured. Harness B-038 versus LUKS2 and BitLocker on the same drive; V2 publish, later rungs per Tier 1.

title: Publish the gaming benchmark suite on the AMD desktop
justification: §56.2/V2 gaming proof: frame-time distribution, input latency, load time and stutter for W1 Gold titles on the AMD desktop versus Windows and Proton-on-Linux. Complements B-027 with the stutter/load suite.

title: Publish SystemGeneration creation time and disk overhead
justification: V0.5 generation-switch gate needs creation time and per-generation store growth as standing metrics. Harness B-022; PKG owns switch and rollback segments.

title: Track kernel image size and boot time to first frame
justification: Cheap isolation and fast startup degrade through bloat unless image size and boot-to-first-frame are watched with regression alerts. Harnesses B-044 and B-032; V0.5 publish, later rungs regress.

title: Publish interoperability path throughput and import time
justification: V3 migration/interop: NTFS and exFAT throughput, SMB client throughput, VM-guest launch time and GPU fraction, and migration import time per 100 GB with verification, versus Linux and Windows on the same hardware. Harness B-049.

title: Publish native isolation cost against OCI containers
justification: §36/§53: native ResourceDomain plus Component plus capabilities must be published beside OCI creation latency and memory on the same hardware. Standing B-015 using the V0 spike's baseline images.

title: Publish Linux personality overhead against upstream Linux
justification: V1 gate: syscall latency and L2 corpus workload throughput versus upstream Linux on the same hardware. Personality productisation is V1; V0 measured only fork syscall overhead. Harness B-026.

title: Publish security-mitigation overhead
justification: V4 benchmark gate: relative cost of shipped kernel and runtime mitigations on versus off for B-001, B-004, B-016 and B-026. Harness B-040.

title: Publish developer onboarding time
justification: V1 daily-driving and SDK v1 make time-to-hello-Component a tracked claim. Harness B-050: SDK download to running hello, and fresh clone to booted QEMU CI image.

title: Publish kernel panic rate from opt-in telemetry
justification: V3 gate: kernel panics per machine-day from opt-in telemetry, published monthly. Harness B-042; V4/1.0 add the absolute ceiling in the register.

title: Publish Task baselines against Tokio, Go and BEAM
justification: §54 language-runtime comparison for Task creation, Operation cost and message passing against Tokio tasks, Go goroutines and Erlang/BEAM processes on the same hardware. Standing baseline for B-002, B-003, B-009 and B-014.

title: Publish snapshot creation and restore time
justification: V2 benchmark gate: snapshot creation and restore from the settings UI on a fixed user-data set. Harness B-036; STO/PKG own the mechanism.

title: Publish storage-object access against Linux file I/O
justification: §54 filesystem/object access through Capability-scoped storage objects versus direct Linux file I/O on NVMe. Harness B-037; STO owns the service under test.

title: Publish update success rate
justification: V3 updater gate and later 1.0 update-success guarantee: fraction of update attempts that boot the new SystemGeneration without automatic rollback. Harness B-043.

title: Publish V0 Component, Task and ResourceDomain cost benchmarks
justification: V0 benchmark gates for Component creation, Task creation, idle memory, context-switch behaviour and related §10/§20/§22/§23 costs are publish-only. Wires CMP, TSK and SCH harnesses through the BEN runner for B-001, B-002, B-003, B-008, B-009, B-010, B-011 and B-014 including 500,000 concurrent Tasks.

title: Publish V0 demo pipeline latency, copies and memory
justification: §59 measured list and the V0 demo: end-to-end latency, copies per stage, memory per Component and Channel, creation cost, native handoff versus Linux switch, and cross-core plus cross-NUMA placement of A to Channel to B to MemoryObject. Harness B-013.

title: Publish V0 IPC, MemoryObject and syscall-overhead benchmarks
justification: V0 gates for same-core and cross-core IPC, throughput, MemoryObject transfer versus memcpy, tracing overhead on the IPC path, and fork syscall microbenchmarks versus the pinned upstream kernel. Publish-only; V1 sets absolute IPC targets. Covers B-004, B-005, B-006, B-007, B-012 and B-026's syscall microbench.

title: Verify no V0 benchmark regression at V0.5
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate: all V0 benchmarks re-run with no regression beyond the register band versus V0 without an accepted Decision. Harness B-051.

title: Verify V1 absolute targets and prior-rung regression
justification: V1 gates: all V0 and V0.5 benchmarks re-run on V1 hardware with no regression beyond the register band, plus first absolute B-001, B-004 and B-005 targets on the reference desktop. Harness B-051 plus the cited B-IDs.

title: Verify no V1 benchmark regression at V2
justification: V2 benchmark gate: all prior benchmarks re-run on all three target machines with no regression beyond the register band versus V1 without an accepted Decision. Harness B-051.

title: Verify no V2 benchmark regression at V3
justification: V3 benchmark gate: all prior benchmarks re-run across Tier 1 with no regression beyond the register band versus V2, with dashboards public. Harness B-051.

title: Publish V4 absolute targets for creation, IPC and startup
justification: V4 gates restated only by B-ID: Component creation, Task creation, same-core and cross-core IPC, Terminal/Editor warm startup, cached os env, input-to-photon and compositor deadline misses on the reference desktop and every Tier 1 machine.

title: Update public dashboards on every V4 release candidate
justification: V4 benchmark gate: public dashboards updated on every RC. Extends the V1 dashboard with RC snapshots and fleet-wide Tier 1 views.

title: Publish every tracked metric on every Tier 1 machine
justification: V4 gate: every §54 metric published for every Tier 1 machine with comparison to Linux and, where dual-boot exists, Windows; macOS comparison where a comparable class exists. Extends the V3 completeness proof across the ten-machine fleet.

title: Verify no V3 benchmark regression at V4
justification: V4 benchmark gate: all prior benchmarks re-run on all Tier 1 machines; regression beyond the tighter V4 band versus V3 blocks unless an accepted Decision explains it. Harness B-051.

title: Publish native warm startup against the V1 target
justification: V1 benchmark gate: Terminal and Editor warm startup against B-016 on V1 hardware. First absolute application-startup target; V0.5 was publish-only.

title: Publish Windows personality overhead against Proton and Windows
justification: V2 W1 gate: frame time and CPU overhead of Gold titles versus Linux plus Proton and versus native Windows on the same hardware. Harness B-027; no superiority claim. Wine bring-up stays non-gated in WIN at V1.

title: Publish zero-copy NIC-to-GPU copies per stage
justification: §17 path from NIC or storage through a decoder Component to GPU and scanout, with copies counted by physical-page identity where hardware permits. Harness B-046; V2 when the media path exists.

title: Enforce claim-to-benchmark lint and traceability matrix
justification: §53/§54/§57 invariants collapse into one lint: no performance claim without a named B-ID and a report from its harness, no rewrite-Linux-faster framing, and priorities tied to user-perceivable outcomes. The matrix lists every architectural claim against a B-ID; CI fails a docs or task change that cites a number or an unbacked superiority claim.

title: Build the shared benchmark runner and CI publication
justification: V0 scope requires a harness and CI on QEMU plus the reference desktop; the V0 gate publishes generated Markdown between markers on every merge. This is the shared runner, report skeleton, environment record and per-commit history; the public dashboard is V1.

title: Pin Linux comparison baseline images on reference hardware
justification: §54 requires every claim compared against Linux on identical hardware. Pins the upstream kernel version that was forked plus a mainstream distro userspace on the V0 desktop so V0 tables have a replayable baseline.

title: Pin macOS comparison baseline on comparable hardware
justification: §54 macOS comparison where a hardware-comparable class exists (input-to-photon, app startup, energy). Pins machine class, OS version and method so V4/1.0 cross-OS tables are replayable.

title: Publish the public per-commit benchmark dashboard
justification: Performance claims must be continuously measured and publicly visible. Dashboard fed by CI with per-commit history and regression alerting for every register metric. V3/V4 gates require this dashboard to stay public.

title: Store benchmark results with change-point detection
justification: §54 demands watched benchmarks. Time-series store with change-point detection, noise-calibrated thresholds from spike-noise-floor, and automatic bisection to the offending commit. Committed reports stay per-milestone; the TSDB holds the rest (critique structure weakness 8).

title: Pin Windows comparison baseline on reference hardware
justification: §54 Windows comparison for startup, input latency, gaming and energy needs a pinned Windows image on dual-boot reference hardware before W1 overhead is published.

title: Decide the blocking performance merge-gate policy
justification: V1 is the first rung with absolute targets. Options: block merge on a regression beyond the calibrated noise band on tier-one metrics (IPC round trip, Component creation, app startup, input-to-photon), nightly-only fail, or warn with a required Decision. BLD owns the CI job; this Decision is the policy.

title: Decide benchmark methodology and target-kind policy
justification: Critique contradiction 5 and structure weakness 2: V0 gates stay publish-only, numeric targets live only in the register with kinds publish, absolute, and regression-versus-prior-milestone, and the proposed sub-microsecond V0 IPC exit is deleted. Answers INV-1042 (hardware list, warm/cold, percentiles, iteration counts, frequency pinning, mitigations). Options include register target kinds, restating numbers in milestone files, or numeric V0 exits.

title: Decide the visible-UI measurement boundary
justification: V0.5 startup gates are incomparable unless 'visible UI' is fixed. Options include first compositor presentation of a non-blank frame, first client commit, or first photodiode edge. B-016 cites this Decision as Q-029.

title: Write the contributor guide for adding a benchmark
justification: Workstream scope: BEN owns the register, methodology and results. V1 self-hosting and SDK v1 mean other prefixes add B-IDs; the guide states how to register a metric, write a harness against the runner, and land a report.

title: Audit 1.0 claims against published benchmark reports
justification: 1.0 exit: the release announcement contains no performance claim without a link to the measurement. Checklist against build-claim-lint and the public reports; I-061 enforcement at ship time.

title: Prove every tracked metric has a public Tier 1 number
justification: V3 benchmark gate: the full §54 list has a public number for every item on at least one Tier 1 machine; any missing item blocks the gate. Produces the completeness matrix against the register.

title: Publish methodology, raw data and scripts for third parties
justification: 1.0 benchmark gate: methodology, raw data and scripts published so third parties can reproduce every number. Pairs with the reproducible-build story; BEN owns the measurement pack.

title: Measure native startup against traditional ELF load
justification: §53 startup comparison: map immutable objects and reuse verified pages versus lookup, shared-library load, reloc and constructors. Informs B-016/B-017 and the Package mapping path.

title: Define energy measurement methodology with external meters
justification: Critique ordering: energy methodology and LAB power meters precede the V1 battery gate. Protocol covers external meter versus battery gauge versus RAPL, drain workloads, and comparison OS images on the same laptop. B-031 stays unpublished until this report exists.

title: Measure filesystem candidates for snapshot and clone cost
justification: Informs the V0.5 STO filesystem Decision with snapshot creation, clone time, checksum overhead and dedup on a representative system image. Critique contradiction 4: ZFS is rejected on licence before measurement and is not a candidate.

title: Measure native IPC against Unix socket, pipe and D-Bus
justification: §53 IPC study: typed message plus ownership transfer plus scheduler-aware handoff versus serialize-syscall-copy-deserialize on Unix sockets, pipes and D-Bus. Informs V1 absolute B-004/B-005 targets; standing numbers live in bench-v0-ipc.

title: Measure native isolation against OCI container start
justification: §53 isolation comparison of the five-step native path against runtime-daemon, namespaces, overlay, cgroups and process start. Establishes the Docker/Podman runc and crun baseline on the same hardware. Publish-only at V0; V1 publishes the cheaper-than-OCI claim as B-015.

title: Profile the native application launch path
justification: Breaks launch into Component creation, capability attachment, mapping, runtime init and first frame so the B-016 budget is spent on a named stage rather than a single wall number. Precedes V1 absolute warm-startup checks.

title: Measure harness noise floor on QEMU versus hardware
justification: Critique: microsecond IPC and Component-creation numbers cannot be taken from shared or virtualised runners. Records QEMU versus reference-desktop noise so V1 blocking gates have a calibrated band and V0 publish-only reports stay labelled by environment.

title: Run accessibility-tree dump tests for the four V0.5 apps in CI
justification: V0.5 exit: every UI widget emits accessibility metadata inspectable via os inspect, verified by a tree dump on each of the four apps. UIP/ACC own metadata; BLD runs the dump in the GUI harness.

title: Run the ABI conformance and cross-version suite in CI
justification: Moved from V0: ABI owns suite content at V0.5 (no L1 freeze before V4). BLD wires the suite into post-merge CI once ABI-@build-conformance-suite-v0 exists.

title: Adapt syzkaller to the Native ABI with a capability-aware executor
justification: L1 spikes are V0; continuous native-ABI fuzzing starts from the first prototype (V0.5, not freeze). syzlang for handles, Channels, Operations and MemoryObjects; capability-aware executor; IDL-generated descriptions. IPC owns per-interface mutators.

title: Produce nightly images for the alpha channel
justification: V3 exit: updater delivers consecutive alpha releases. BLD produces the nightly SystemGeneration images REL promotes without rebuilding (GAP-0147).

title: Apply the chosen linker, LTO and PGO policy in CI profiles
justification: Implements decide-linker-lto-pgo in debug/release profiles and the double-build job so the V1 image is the policy, not a local override.

title: Keep an ARM64 kernel and userspace cross-build compiling in CI
justification: §38 forbids fossilising on x86-64. Standing compile-only ARM64 (and a Native ABI header plus smoke Component) without shipping or booting. KRN owns RISC-V build-only CI.

title: Automate CI-validated dependency update proposals
justification: Crates, C libraries, firmware, QEMU and upstream Linux updates as CI-validated changes with a documented review cadence so the fork and Rust tree do not rot during daily-driving.

title: Track build-time budgets on the reference runner
justification: Critique: every number lives in registers/benchmarks.md. Incremental kernel, incremental userspace and clean CI build times are measured and gated by B-IDs, not prose. V1 sets targets; V0 was publish-only.

title: Fail merges that regress beyond the calibrated performance band
justification: V0 executed the suite publish-only. V1 applies BEN's blocking gate (GAP-0137) on the quiet fleet: regressions outside the noise band block merge unless an adr-linked exception exists.

title: Rehearse disaster recovery of the CI and lab pipeline
justification: GAP-0108 is unproven until the pipeline is recreated from repository plus backups in a drill before public alpha depends on it.

title: Manage CI and lab infrastructure as code with disaster recovery
justification: V1 daily-driving depends on a recreatable pipeline from the repository plus backups. Lab machine definitions stay in LAB; BLD owns runner, cache, queue and secret layout.

title: Structure CI into tiers and enforce a merge queue
justification: V0 gate and bisection assume main is always green. Pre-merge lint/unit/QEMU smoke, post-merge full QEMU matrix, nightly sanitizers/fuzz/perf/lab, later release qualification; merge queue with no direct pushes.

title: Provide CI plumbing for compatibility-corpus jobs
justification: V0.5 L1 corpus gate and later L2–L5/W1–W3 jobs need a guest-agent path that runs corpus scenarios and records C-ID results. LNX and WIN own scenario content.

title: Run continuous Native ABI fuzzing with dedup, bisect and task filing
justification: syzbot-like infra on the V0.5 syzkaller port: crash dedup, repro minimisation, automatic bisection, tasks filed into the Markdown repository. Covers IDL deserialisers. V3/V4 crasher-age gates consume this.

title: Measure kernel and userspace coverage and gate security-critical paths
justification: kcov/gcov and Rust coverage with minimum gates on capability enforcement, ABI entry points and IDL-generated paths before SDK v1 freeze candidates.

title: Run SDK cross-version compatibility jobs in CI
justification: V1 exit: SDK v1 compatibility suite passes for apps built against v1.0.0 after each v1.x. SDK GAP-0100 owns the suite; BLD runs it on generated images.

title: Upload content-hashed debug symbols for every stripped generation
justification: V1 daily-driving and crash reports need symbols for immutable stripped binaries. OBS GAP-0151 operates debuginfod; BLD publishes the symbols-preserved profile by content hash.

title: Decide the top-level build orchestrator for kernel and userspace
justification: Kbuild-plus-Cargo versus Bazel/Buck2 versus a derivation-based builder aligned with the content-addressed store decides whether hermeticity and remote caching are native properties. Required before the one-command Linux-host build.

title: Decide the CI platform with self-hosted KVM runners
justification: Boot, graphics, performance and hardware jobs need nested virtualisation or lab devices. Hosted runners are allowed only for lint and unit tests. Precedes CI tiers and the QEMU harness.

title: Decide linker, LTO scope and PGO policy for kernel and userspace
justification: Depends on spike-linker-lto-pgo. Options must include refusing PGO where it breaks bit-for-bit SystemGeneration identity.

title: Decide LLVM/Clang as the sole C compiler and reject a custom compiler
justification: Rust-in-kernel needs bindgen against libclang; mixing GCC C with rustc doubles the matrix. Collapses the no-forked-LLVM nongoal into the same adr with upstream-bound patches as the accepted option.

title: Decide repository topology before a second repository exists
justification: Every CI, bisection and promotion design depends on whether one commit identifies the whole system; must precede any second repository. GOV GAP-0384 decides forge hosting; this adr decides monorepo versus pinned-manifest multi-repo.

title: Decide SBOM format for Packages and SystemGenerations
justification: GAP-0352 generator needs SPDX versus CycloneDX versus both decided before V2 store/repository SBOMs and V3 attestations (REL GAP-0095).

title: Decide a semantic-interface GUI test harness over pixel scripting
justification: V0.5 four apps and compositor-restart need an end-to-end GUI harness. Options: semantic interfaces plus accessibility tree, coordinate scripting, or pixel goldens. Pixel goldens stay reserved for compositor rendering (GFX).

title: Turn on deterministic compile and link flags for Packages
justification: V0.5 immutable Packages are content-addressed; path/timestamp/codegen-unit flags must be pinned before the V1 double-build gate (GAP-0094).

title: Eliminate artifact non-determinism and double-build on every merge
justification: V1 self-host gate requires bit-for-bit image identity across two machines. CI builds twice, diffs artifacts, and verifies Package hashes against the content-addressed store. STO owns addressing; BLD owns the rebuild check.

title: Build an embargoed private path for security-release compilation
justification: V3 security-response gate. Public CI leaks embargoed fixes; a private compile/sign/stage path is BLD infrastructure REL uses for advisories.

title: Build a fault-injection framework for service kill and kernel failures
justification: V0.5 compositor-restart gate and SVC supervision need CI that kills services and injects allocation/I/O failures and checks rebind. Pulled from V1 because the gate is V0.5.

title: Lock CI against new Layer 1 entry points after feature freeze
justification: V4 feature freeze after RC1 and no new Layer 1 ABI entry points. ABI owns the snapshot; BLD fails qualification if the snapshot grows without the freeze adr.

title: Eliminate flaky tests or expire their quarantine
justification: V4 scope: stability program including flaky-test elimination (OBS, BLD). Quarantine from GAP-0120 must be empty or expired at RC.

title: Publish a flaky-test policy and automate quarantine in CI
justification: Desktop and hardware jobs will flake. Policy: auto-quarantine, at most one retry, time-boxed deflake on the owning workstream, expiry deletes or fixes. V4 elimination depends on this existing.

title: Gate V4 on a clean Native ABI fuzz window
justification: V4 exit: kernel and IPC fuzzing have zero known open crashers for the consecutive window recorded in the gate before freeze.

title: Gate V3 on no known open Native ABI fuzzer crasher
justification: V3 exit: kernel and IPC fuzzing run continuously in CI with no known open crasher older than the register window. Enforces continuous-fuzzing-infra as a gate.

title: Fuzz userspace parsers of untrusted input with in-tree corpora
