justification: Userspace parser fuzzing (manifests, fonts, images, PE/ELF, capability serialisation) is distinct from Native ABI syzkaller (continuous-fuzzing-infra). cargo-fuzz corpora in the repository. Size L: many parsers across PKG, TXT, MED, LNX/WIN and CAP.

title: Generate an SBOM from the content-addressed dependency graph
justification: Critique: mechanised compliance is BLD CI; REL publishes. V2 native repository needs per-Package and per-SystemGeneration SBOMs from the build graph.

title: Extend the boot harness to SystemGeneration selection cycles
justification: V0.5 exit: selecting the previous generation at boot restores kernel, compositor and Packages, verified by an automated boot-menu test. V0 harness covered reboot/kexec only.

title: Build a guest-side test agent that reports structured results
justification: V0 Component/Channel/Capability/MemoryObject tests must run inside the booted image and map failures to task IDs over virtio-serial or vsock.

title: Run the 40-scenario desktop UX script in the GUI harness
justification: V2 exit: desktop shell passes the 40-scenario UX script on all three targets. APP owns scenarios; BLD runs them through the semantic harness on QEMU and lab.

title: Run the hardware regression matrix on QEMU and the reference machine
justification: Critique collapse of retain-Linux items: KRN owns the retained-mechanism inventory; BLD hosts the DRM/PCI/USB/NVMe/net/ACPI regression matrix on QEMU and the single V0 AMD desktop so native features cannot regress hardware support (§55).

title: Run hermetic builds inside native development environments
justification: GAP-0092 required the native environment primitive (§35) once it exists. V1 os env becomes the sandbox for self-hosted builds, replacing the Linux-host equivalent.

title: Verify reproducible builds with independent rebuilders
justification: V4 exit: 100% of SystemGeneration Packages reproduce on two independent builders and a public verifier exists. This task stands up the second builder and publishes per-generation status.

title: Migrate CI runners to bare-metal JakeOS
justification: Critique: full CI-on-JakeOS after installer/updater exist. Dogfoods unattended operation and remote management that desktop daily-driving never hits.

title: Document and CI-exercise the kernel debug workflow
justification: Critique extra: QEMU gdbstub, kgdb, early console and drgn crash-dump analysis in one page, exercised in CI so the fork is debuggable from the first boot.

title: Wire the hardware lab scheduler into nightly and post-merge CI
justification: V1 Intel-laptop gates (Wi-Fi, 200 suspend cycles, GPU-accelerated Linux apps) and the critique's lab-on-critical-path note. LAB owns LAVA-like scheduling; BLD submits jobs and consumes results.

title: Run licence compliance scanning in CI across kernel, crates and firmware
justification: SPDX and cargo-deny with a zero-unknown gate. GOV owns the allowlist Decision; BLD enforces it.

title: Produce milestone test images from the shared image builder
justification: Moved from V0: critique puts the image builder at V0.5 (INS EXTRA-070). Desktop test images must come from the same builder as shipped images. V0 continues to use the hermetic QEMU smoke image.

title: Provide a hermetic one-command Linux-host build and source mirror
justification: V0 exit boots from a CI-built image reproducible from a tagged commit; this is the contributor entry point. Hermetic sandbox, content-hash mirror, committed lockfiles and a containerised Linux env for non-Linux hosts (nongoal: no native Windows/macOS host builds before 1.0).

title: Run the core benchmark suite and V0 demos in CI
justification: V0 benchmark gates are publish-only (critique). BLD executes BEN harnesses on pinned QEMU and the reference desktop and records V0 demo runs. Numeric fail-on-regression is the V1 blocking hook; BEN owns methodology and the quiet fleet.

title: Stand up the quiet bare-metal performance CI fleet
justification: workstreams.md gives the perf-CI fleet to BLD. BEN consumes the machines; LAB is the physical site.

title: Pin the userspace rustc and rustup profile for self-host builds
justification: V1 self-host and SDK v1 need a pinned userspace rustc distinct from the kernel RfL pin (GAP-0089), with a next-candidate canary that does not block kernel builds.

title: Pin a reproducible userspace sysroot and toolchain artifacts
justification: V1 bit-for-bit self-host and later independent rebuilders need a content-addressed sysroot, not an ambient distro toolchain, while still carrying only upstream rustc/LLVM (GAP-0160).

title: Enforce license, provenance, unsafe and static-analysis merge gates
justification: Collapse of V0 invariants and lint deliverables: kernel license allowlist (no Apache-2.0-only/CDDL), SPDX headers, Signed-off-by and verified signatures, rustfmt/clippy -D warnings, sparse/smatch/checkpatch, cargo-deny, Miri where feasible, unsafe inventory. SDK forbid(unsafe_code) templates stay in SDK; GOV owns DCO policy.

title: Build release artifacts once and promote them across channels
justification: V3 release pipeline: build once, then promote identical artifacts through nightly, testing and stable. BLD must not rebuild per channel or qualification is void.

title: Publish public CI and benchmark dashboards
justification: V3 benchmark gates require public dashboards. BEN owns numbers; BLD publishes pass/fail, flake and BEN exports without leaking embargoed jobs.

title: Ship a public verifier for independent rebuilds
justification: V4 exit: a public verifier tool is available so reproducibility is not only the project's own pipeline.

title: Define the QEMU boot matrix, boot harness and kselftests
justification: V0 primary CI target is QEMU/KVM. Declares q35/OVMF/TPM/virtio/CPU/memory/NUMA axes, drives boot-complete over serial, detects panics, reboot and kexec. Nightly kselftests for every retained subsystem. Generation-selection cycles wait for V0.5.

title: Run a QEMU-hosted JakeOS CI runner as the self-host step
justification: Critique contradiction 8: migrating CI to JakeOS at V2 predates the installer. V2 step is a QEMU-hosted JakeOS runner; bare-metal migration waits for V3.

title: Stand up the quiet bare-metal performance CI fleet
justification: workstreams.md gives the quiet bare-metal perf-CI fleet to BLD; no existing BLD fleet-rack slug (perf-and-demo-ci runs V0 publish-only on QEMU plus the reference desktop). V1 with blocking-perf-ci-hook. Fixed frequency, disabled turbo/SMT, isolated from other CI load. BEN consumes the machines; LAB does not rack this fleet.

title: Run release-candidate soak matrices on the Tier 1 fleet
justification: V4 exit: two RC cycles each with soak on the full Tier 1 fleet and no P0. BLD owns the matrix jobs; LAB owns machine uptime.

title: Implement the release-qualification CI tier
justification: GAP-0109 named release qualification at V0 but public alpha is the first rung that ships channels. Mechanical checklist: gates green, reproducibility, Tier 1 pass, no unresolved BEN regressions. REL GAP-0148 consumes it.

title: Deploy a shared content-addressed remote build cache
justification: Pre-merge feedback stays usable only if compiler and artifact caches are shared and hits are checked against reproducible outputs (§27 cached build outputs).

title: Make every SystemGeneration Package reproduce bit-for-bit
justification: V4 reproducible-builds gate for the inherited Linux toolchain plus native Packages. 1.0 two-rebuilder-release reuses this as the remaining independent-party proof.

title: Establish pinned Rust-in-kernel toolchain and Kbuild integration
justification: V0 scope requires Rust-in-kernel so native subsystems can land. Pins rustc, allowed unstable features, RfL-tied upgrade cadence, bindgen/Kbuild, and a next-candidate toolchain canary. Kernel half of §50.

title: Define sanitizer debug and release build profiles and boot them nightly
justification: V0 memory-safety bugs in inherited C and unsafe Rust are caught only if lockdep/KASAN/KCSAN/UBSAN/KFENCE and Rust debug assertions actually boot. Release profile is LTO plus stripped; a symbols-preserved variant feeds later symbol upload.

title: Gate releases on complete SBOMs for every SystemGeneration
justification: 1.0 security posture and REL GAP-0095 need every shipped generation to have an SBOM. Turns generate-sbom-ci into a release-qualification failure.

title: Deliver Linux-host bootstrap and self-hosted full-system builds
justification: V1 exit: a clean checkout builds the full image on the OS inside os env and the image boots the V0/V0.5 suites. Documents a small contributor path on Linux and on JakeOS. ENV owns os env; BLD owns the build graph.

title: Build the semantic-interface and accessibility-tree GUI test harness
justification: Implements the harness so V0.5 scripted app scenarios and compositor-rebind run in QEMU CI without pixel scraping.

title: Run nightly CI on all six Tier 1 machines
justification: V3 hardware scope: six Tier 1 machines fully tested each release, including NVIDIA. BLD schedules the nightly matrix LAB hosts.

title: Emit SLSA-style build provenance from hermetic CI
justification: REL GAP-0095 publishes SBOM plus signed provenance; BLD emits the provenance from the hermetic, no-network-after-fetch builder so attestations match actual CI.

title: Run the 1.0 soak matrix on the Tier 1 fleet
justification: 1.0 exit: final RC soaked on the full Tier 1 fleet with zero open P0/P1. BLD keeps the qualification matrix green for the soak window; REL owns channel launch.

title: Spike Component and ResourceDomain isolation for parallel tests
justification: Once V0 primitives are stable, evaluate one Component per test as the isolation unit. Report must measure creation cost against BEN Component-creation B-IDs rather than claiming speedups.

title: Spike linker, LTO and PGO effects on binaries and benchmarks
justification: Must precede the linker adr. Measures lld versus mold, LTO scope and PGO against BEN §54 harnesses and bit-for-bit rebuilds so PGO cannot silently break reproducibility.

title: Run nightly CI on at least ten Tier 1 machines
justification: V4 hardware: at least ten named Tier 1 machines fully tested each RC. Extends six-machine-ci.

title: Deploy a per-commit test-results database and dashboard
justification: KernelCI-style history, flake rate and duration per commit, configuration and machine. BEN owns the performance TSDB; this is pass/fail/flake for functional jobs.

title: Run CI on the three V2 target machines
justification: V2 hardware scope is exactly three named machines. Extends lab-ci-integration so nightly and qualification jobs cover AMD desktop, Intel laptop and AMD laptop.

title: Reproduce the 1.0 image with two independent rebuilders
justification: 1.0 exit: 100% of 1.0 SystemGeneration Packages reproduce bit-for-bit on two independent builders and a third party has reproduced the release image with published matching checksums.

title: Run userspace sanitizer profiles for native Components in nightly CI
justification: V0 sanitizer profiles boot the kernel; V2 desktop code needs ASAN/LSAN/TSAN (or equivalent) on native Components in nightly CI without exploding the pre-merge budget.

title: Add virtio-gpu QEMU configurations to the compositor CI matrix
justification: V0.5 hardware scope: QEMU/KVM with virtio-gpu for compositor CI. Extends the V0 q35 matrix so GFX jobs have a GPU-less and virtio-gpu path.

title: Provision GPU-equipped nightly capacity for the W1 corpus
justification: V2 W1 gates need GPU lab jobs. WIN owns corpus and Wine suite; BLD sizes nightly GPU runners so those jobs are not starved by kernel QEMU.

title: Enforce the security-fix watermark in the bootloader per the anti-rollback decision
justification: Implements decide-anti-rollback: the signed manifest carries a watermark, the bootloader compares it against a monotonic counter, and behaviour follows the chosen policy with tests for each branch.

title: Build the harness measuring reboot-into-previous-generation time and publish results
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate 'generation switch and rollback time measured and published'; the boot-menu rollback segment is BOOT's metric (PKG owns the switch segment) and must live in the BEN register with a method.

title: Build the boot-to-login timing harness and publish results beside Linux and Windows
justification: V3 benchmark gate 'boot time to login on each Tier 1 machine measured and published'; critique #5 requires boot gap #74's numbers to live in the register with a method, so the harness exists from V1 on the desktop and Intel laptop.

title: Build the pre-boot unlock latency harness and publish results
justification: Critique #5: the '< 500 ms unlock' figure from boot gap #74 must be a registered B-ID with a harness, not a milestone claim; measured from unlock submission to root pivot on both V1 machines.

title: Expose SystemGenerations to foreign bootloaders via BLS entries and an os-release descriptor
justification: Coexistence is bidirectional: os-prober and systemd-boot on a co-installed distro must list JakeOS generations or users assume the install failed.

title: Close all High and Critical external-audit findings against the bootloader chain
justification: V4 exit: external security audit (GOV GAP-0240 names the bootloader chain) with all High/Critical fixed and re-verified by the auditor.

title: Implement boot counting, bad-generation marking and unattended fallback to last known-good
justification: §30 'if boot fails, boot the previous generation' needs a defined failure detector; includes the counter storage on the ESP/EFI variable and the capability-gated boot-success primitive that SVC's init reports through. Needed before V2's fault-injected rollback gate.

title: Define the on-disk boot-entry format mapping a menu entry to a SystemGeneration
justification: Fixed contract between bootloader (BOOT) and generation store (PKG): entry → generation ID, kernel image, verified store root hash, signed manifest; includes a Rust parser/writer crate and a golden-file compatibility test.

title: Fault-inject a broken SystemGeneration and verify unattended fallback on the three target machines
justification: V2 exit: a fault-injected broken update automatically boots the previous generation, tested on all three machines; adds the LAB-driven power-cycle harness reused by V3 and 1.0 gates.

title: Boot the forked kernel on QEMU/KVM under OVMF from a CI-built image
justification: V0 exit: kernel fork boots on QEMU/KVM from a CI-built image, reproducible from a tagged commit; QEMU/OVMF is the primary CI target.

title: Boot the forked kernel on the reference AMD desktop from the tagged CI image
justification: V0 exit and §59: boot on at least one physical reference machine; covers UEFI firmware quirks, serial console and power-cycle automation on the LAB rig.

title: Embed the kernel command line in the signed SystemGeneration and test that edits fail verification
justification: Invariant covered by a test gate: the command line is part of the signed image, the boot-time editor is disabled outside developer mode, and CI proves a modified command line is rejected.

title: Decide the anti-rollback policy for SystemGenerations older than a security watermark
justification: §30 first-class rollback and downgrade-attack protection are in direct tension; V3 public alpha exposes rollback to strangers. Options: block below watermark; allow with warning; allow only in developer mode.

title: Decide what 'boot succeeded' means and which Component may clear the boot counter
justification: Too early lets a broken desktop mark itself good, too late breaks headless and recovery boots; SVC's init is the reporter. Options: session manager reached greeter; user authenticated; per-boot-mode profile (headless/recovery/desktop).

title: Decide the bootloader: systemd-boot, GRUB or a native Rust UEFI stub
justification: V0.5 exit requires an accepted adr for the generation switching mechanism; generation selection, boot counting and PCR policy all depend on this choice. Options: systemd-boot; GRUB; native Rust UEFI stub.

title: Decide how early boot locates the content store and the selected SystemGeneration
justification: Generation booting only works if early boot finds immutable objects before trusting mutable state; pairs with SVC's early-userspace adr (GAP-0170). Options: initramfs-embedded locator; kernel command line parameters; bootloader-passed manifest.

title: Decide the trusted time source policy before network time is available
justification: Certificate and signature validity checks at early boot need a clock trust policy. Options: bootloader-persisted monotonic floor; build-timestamp floor of the booted generation; RTC trusted with TPM-backed clock attestation.

title: Decide ESP policy: reuse the existing OEM ESP or create a dedicated ESP for generation entries
justification: V2 target laptops ship Windows-created 100 MB ESPs and V3's dual-boot installer (INS) depends on the layout; decided at V2 so INS can build on it. Options: reuse existing ESP with compact entries; dedicated ESP; reuse with XBOOTLDR-style extended partition.

title: Decide atomicity of kernel, driver and firmware updates within a SystemGeneration
justification: §30 rollback conflicts with firmware that cannot be rolled back; the adr defines what a generation guarantees and what is recorded as irreversible in §31 history (cross-ref HW). Options: firmware outside generations; firmware staged with the generation and flagged irreversible; firmware applied only after boot-success.

title: Decide whether GPLv3 components may appear in the boot chain and how Installation Information is met
justification: Secure/measured boot plus GPLv3 (GRUB, gnupg) triggers anti-tivoization obligations; must be settled alongside decide-bootloader. Options: no GPLv3 in the boot chain; GPLv3 permitted with user-enrollable Secure Boot keys as Installation Information; GPLv3 only in developer mode images. The base-image half (coreutils, bash) is GOV licensing policy.

title: Decide Secure Boot distribution: Microsoft-signed shim, enrolled project keys, or both
justification: Most retail hardware ships only Microsoft keys and dual-boot machines must keep Windows Secure Boot and BitLocker functional; V3 exit requires Secure Boot on all Tier 1 machines so the strategy is fixed at V2. Options: shim + MOK; user-enrolled PK/KEK/db; both.

title: Decide UEFI-only boot on x86-64 with no legacy BIOS/CSM support through 1.0
justification: Standing non-goal covered by the adr that decides it; must precede the V0 reference-desktop boot so no BIOS path is ever built or tested. Options: UEFI-only; UEFI plus CSM; UEFI now with BIOS revisit at V3.

title: Decide whether each SystemGeneration boots as one signed UKI or separately verified parts
justification: The image format must be fixed before the generation store layout (PKG) and boot-entry format are frozen; determines Secure Boot signing units and PCR predictability. Options: single signed UKI; kernel + separately verified initramfs and command line; UKI with detached add-ons.

title: Decide V0 boots Linux init from a retained initramfs with native Components beside it
justification: Critique contradiction #2: the V0 exit 'boots to a native init' conflicts with §5.1 Phase A; the adr fixes V0 = retained Linux boot and initramfs handoff with native Components started beside init, native init deferred to V0.5 (SVC). Options: retained initramfs + Linux init; native init at V0; hybrid stub init.

title: Ship documented developer mode: own Secure Boot keys, self-built kernels, visible indicator
justification: V1 self-hosting requires booting self-built kernels; developer mode enrols owner keys, disables lockdown and exposes a non-suppressible state that APP's shell renders as a persistent indicator; includes the enrolment guide.

title: Mount the content store read-only in early boot and hand off to native init
justification: Implements decide-early-boot-store: early userspace locates the store and selected generation, mounts immutably, and hands off to SVC's native init so the cold-boot-to-native-desktop demo starts from a SystemGeneration.

title: Seed the kernel RNG at boot from TPM, CPU RNG and a bootloader-persisted seed
justification: First-boot disk unlock, TLS and signature checks depend on early entropy; the bootloader persists and refreshes a seed on the ESP and the kernel credits TPM and RDSEED sources.

title: Gate UEFI variable and firmware-settings access behind a Capability with no ambient efivarfs
justification: §9 no ambient authority; writable efivars can brick firmware or alter Secure Boot state; a typed firmware-variable service replaces ambient efivarfs for native Components and a denial test is added.

title: Make bootloader and ESP updates atomic with tested rollback of the bootloader itself
justification: An interrupted bootloader update is the one failure generations cannot roll back from; dual-slot or write-then-rename with a power-cut test in QEMU is required before the V1 signed-repository update path ships.

title: Manage ESP space so at least N previous SystemGeneration kernels stay bootable
justification: 1.0 definition (3) requires N ≥ 3 previous generations bootable and the V0.5 exit requires the previous kernel selectable at boot; per-generation kernel images on the ESP need retention, garbage collection and out-of-space handling.

title: Chain-load Windows Boot Manager and foreign Linux loaders and self-heal BootOrder
justification: V3 installer supports dual boot (INS GAP-0208); Windows updates rewrite BootOrder and bootx64.efi, so the boot chain must chain-load foreign loaders and repair its own entries on next boot.

title: Present previous SystemGenerations in the boot menu with automated boot-menu selection test
justification: V0.5 exit: selecting the previous generation at boot restores the previous kernel, compositor and packages, verified by an automated boot-menu test on QEMU (serial/firmware-driven selection) and the reference desktop.

title: Verify SystemGeneration images at boot against their content hashes via the boot-entry root
justification: §26 integrity verification and §27 content addressing: the verified store root hash in the boot entry drives dm-verity on the generation image; a tampered image must fail closed.

title: Retain the Linux initramfs handoff and launch native Components beside Linux init
justification: §5.1 preserve boot initially; implements decide-v0-boot-strategy so the V0 demos (Component A/B, busybox and L0 corpus side by side) start from one retained initramfs.

title: Design and build the integrity-failure experience with a guaranteed recovery path
justification: Verity, PCR or signature failures after firmware changes are inevitable; the user sees a diagnosis, can enter the recovery boot entry, and no path silently bypasses verification; INS owns the recovery environment itself.

title: Rehearse signing-key rotation and SBAT revocation through the boot chain on the testing channel
justification: V4 exit: signing key rotation drill executed on the testing channel without breaking updates; the bootloader must accept rotated db/MOK certificates and revoked SBAT generations while keeping previous generations bootable.

title: Extend kernel, command line, generation ID and verity root into TPM PCRs with signed PCR policies
justification: Without predictable PCR policy every update strands sealed disk keys; ships signed expected PCR values per generation so SEC's re-seal (GAP-0199) and TPM service (GAP-0192) can keep unlock working across updates.

title: Build the graphical DPI-aware pre-boot unlock UI
justification: GAP-0197 specifies graphical, DPI-aware unlock at V2 for the polished desktop on three target machines, including HiDPI laptop panels.

title: Build the text pre-boot unlock UI with passphrase, TPM+PIN, recovery key and layouts
justification: V1 scope allows manually configured encryption; unlock must work before the compositor exists with multiple enrolled slots and keyboard layout selection; consumes SEC's sealing design.

title: Make UKI and bootloader images reproduce bit-for-bit with deterministic signing layout
justification: V4 exit: 100% of system-generation packages reproduce on two independent builders; PE assembly and embedded Authenticode signatures need deterministic layout or detached verification for BLD's verifier to pass.

title: Verify the update and rollback guarantee by fault injection on every Tier 1 machine
justification: 1.0 exit: on every Tier 1 machine a fault-injected failing generation boots back automatically, N ≥ 3 generations remain bootable, and a power pull mid-update recovers; the release ceremony demo depends on it.

title: Document the Secure Boot key or shim path, developer mode and recovery for public alpha users
justification: V3 exit requires Secure Boot 'using the documented key or shim path' and public install documentation good enough for strangers; covers key enrolment, MOK prompts, developer mode and integrity-failure recovery.

title: Verify Secure Boot and measured-boot event-log recording on every Tier 1 machine
justification: V3 exit: all Tier 1 machines boot with Secure Boot on and measured boot records generation identity in the TPM event log, verified; the matrix extends to ten machines at V4 and is re-run each RC.

title: Integrate shim and MOK enrolment into the signed boot chain per the Secure Boot strategy
justification: V3 exit: Tier 1 machines boot with Secure Boot enabled using the documented shim or key path; wires shim, MOK enrolment of the project certificate and SBAT metadata into the bootloader and UKI build.

title: Plan the shim-review submission, legal applicant and re-signing process
justification: V3 risk 'shim requires an external review process with uncertain timelines'; the plan (applicant entity, review-board requirements, SBAT and re-signing per shim change) must exist at V2 so REL can run the submission (GAP-0180) in time for V3.

title: Verify the release-key signature of every SystemGeneration manifest before offering it
justification: Root of trust for the immutable generation model; V1 exit 'packages signed, verified before activation' and the V1 adr on package signing and trust roots; consumes REL's key hierarchy decision (GAP-0322, V0.5).

title: Prototype systemd-boot+UKI and a Rust UEFI stub booting a SystemGeneration from the store
justification: Precedes decide-bootloader; §57 forbids rewriting a mature piece without demonstrated benefit, so the adr needs measured evidence (generation selection, Secure Boot chain, PCR measurement, ESP footprint) from both candidates on QEMU/OVMF.

title: Stage UEFI capsule updates on the ESP within a generation transition with PCR re-seal hooks
justification: Boot-chain side of HW's firmware update service: capsules are staged on the ESP, applied by firmware at reboot, and the boot chain triggers SEC re-seal before and after; implements decide-firmware-update-atomicity.

title: Make AI action Capabilities revocable mid-run with a logged action graph
justification: V2 exit criterion: AI demo with the full action graph logged and one step revoked mid-run. Must depend on SEM's semantic registry task (§57: no AI before the semantic object model).

title: Lint native SDK and system Components for ambient authority and descriptor-shaped APIs
justification: Standing invariants enforced by a CI lint: no native SDK entry opens objects by ambient path or fd-shaped handle, no system Component is launched with a wildcard set; first matters when the four V0.5 apps and SDK expand.

title: Gate persistent background execution behind Capability<BackgroundExecution>
justification: §21: persistent background execution beyond the owning application requires an explicit capability; V0.5 introduces services and applications that outlive windows. TSK owns TaskGroup lifetime, CAP defines the type and check.

title: Benchmark Capability mint, derive, transfer and revocation cost
justification: BEN anti-fake-claim policy (§53): decide-revocation-semantics states cost bounds that must be measured in CI, and the V0.5 gate re-runs all benchmarks with regression checks; publish-only, no target.

title: Export Capability audit events for the permissions log viewer and os trace
justification: V1 scope excludes 'Permissions UI beyond a log viewer', so a log viewer is in scope and needs structured audit export; V1 exit requires `os trace` session export.

title: Record Capability grants, derivations, revocations and denials in the audit log
justification: V0 scope line 'Capability<T>: creation, derivation, attenuation, transfer over channels, revocation, audit log (CAP)' and the V0 isolation demo 'typed denial visible in the audit log'; §7 lists auditable as a Capability property.

title: Close external audit findings in Capability enforcement
justification: V4 exit criterion: external security audit of kernel capability enforcement with all High/Critical findings fixed and re-verified.

title: Complete conformance tests for every frozen Capability entry point
justification: V4 exit criterion: every L1 entry point has a conformance test and binaries built against the freeze candidate run on every subsequent build.

title: Declare Capability L1 surfaces freeze candidates with conformance tests
justification: Ladder V1: L1 freeze candidates with SDK v1; critique forbids freezing in V0 and requires spikes in the closure of every freeze. Depends on spike-cheri-abi-validation and formal-capability-model.

title: Re-validate the frozen Capability ABI on CHERI emulator and formal model
justification: V4 freezes L1; GAP-0487 demands validation of the frozen ABI on a CHERI emulator and GAP-0488 the formal model before freeze; this precedes the freeze ADR (ABI).

title: Add Capability forge, type-confusion and derivation fuzz targets
justification: V3 gate requires continuous kernel fuzzing with no crasher older than 14 days and V4 requires 30 days; capability-specific targets must be seasoned before V3, so they are added at V2 into BLD's fuzzing infrastructure.

title: Expose Capability type, rights and object identity to holders and os inspect
justification: V0 exit criterion requires `os inspect capability` to print state, ownership and relationships; OBS owns the CLI, CAP provides the query surface for a holder's own Capabilities.

title: Implement Capability mint and attenuating derive with rights monotonicity tests
justification: V0 exit criterion: Capability<File, ReadWrite> derives Capability<File, Read>; deriving Admin fails with a typed error; regression test retained permanently.

title: Write property-based tests for Capability unforgeability, typing and attenuation
justification: Standing invariants (unforgeable, typed, attenuation never widens, revocation complete, no ambient authority) enforced by one property/model-based suite rather than one task per rule; forged-handle test satisfies the V0 exit criterion.

title: Document every Capability object type and right for the Layer 1 reference
justification: V3 exit criterion: 100% of Layer 1 ABI entry points have reference pages; 1.0 definition requires every capability right documented. DOC owns generation, CAP authors the content via object-rights-registry.

title: Implement Capability revocation invalidating all derived Capabilities
justification: V0 exit criterion: revoking a Capability makes every derived Capability fail within one Operation at derivation depth 8. Depends on decide-revocation-semantics.

title: Publish the Capability model guarantees and non-promises for 1.0
justification: 1.0 exit criterion: ABI stability statement and explicit non-promises, including that CHERI-class hardware enforcement is not promised, only ABI room (ladder 1.0 scope out).

title: Implement the kernel Capability object and per-Component Capability table
justification: Kernel-owned enforcement: every object access resolves a typed handle through the holder's table, type mismatch fails at the kernel boundary with a typed error. Required by V0 exit criteria for Component creation with capabilities and forge/type failures.

title: Implement Capability transfer over Channels and at Component creation
justification: Crosses IPC (capability-carrying message slots) and CMP (explicit set attached at creation, native isolation path step 3). Required by the V0 §59 demo where B transfers a MemoryObject Capability back to A.

title: Model debugger attach, tracing and memory reading as explicit Capabilities
justification: V1 native debugger attaches to a Component and LNX ptrace-equivalent (critique: V1) must be gated by an explicit debug Capability rather than same-user checks; crosses SDK, OBS and LNX.

title: Decide Capability persistence across Component restart and reboot
justification: Single decision: sturdy references vs revocable persistent grant store vs re-prompt, and which object types may ever persist. Must precede the V1 persistent-grant-store and V2 grant continuity; depends on spike-capability-os-survey.

title: Decide how Capability unforgeability survives machine boundaries
justification: Answers the §43 question (cryptographic capabilities vs sturdy references vs proxies) so the ABI does not foreclose it; distributed interfaces themselves remain LATER and outside 1.0.

title: Decide explicit grant sources replacing ambient permissions
justification: Single decision: the sources of a Component's authority (creator at launch, user choice via chooser, Package manifest request) so V0 components receive exactly what they are handed. SEC's V0.5 grant-taxonomy ADR refines the taxonomy on top of this.

title: Decide the userspace Capability<T> handle representation and table design
justification: Single decision: how a Capability<T> is represented to userspace and laid out in the per-Component table, replacing file descriptors and reserving room for hardware enforcement. Depends on spike-handle-representation, spike-cheri-escape-hatches and spike-sel4-capability-study; the ABI shape ADR must depend on this. S-state prototyped only, no freeze in V0.

title: Decide the Capability<T> and MemoryObject mapping onto hardware capabilities
justification: Single decision recording the CHERI/Morello and tagged-memory findings as the mapping the ABI must remain compatible with; depends on the two V1 spikes.

title: Decide the ABI invariants required for hardware-assisted Capability enforcement
justification: Single decision: the list of ABI invariants (handle opacity, no pointer-derived identity, rights in the object not the handle, etc.) that keep application-visible Capabilities stable across kernel-metadata, page-table, tag or CHERI enforcement. Depends on spike-cheri-pointer-mapping and spike-cheri-escape-hatches.

title: Decide revocation semantics: eager vs lazy, in-flight Operations, cost bounds
justification: Answers the INV-0187 question and chooses the strategy from spike-revocation-strategies; the V0 exit criterion (depth-8 revocation within one Operation) cannot be implemented without it. Coordinates with TSK on cancelling in-flight Operations.

title: Decide rights and transfer-rights encoding including Admin authority
justification: Single decision: bitmask vs per-type typed rights vs rights objects, and how Admin and transfer/delegation rights are expressed. Required by the V0 exit criterion listing capability encoding among accepted ADRs; state prototyped per critique.

title: Decide how a Component obtains its initial and later Capabilities
justification: Namespace object vs broker Component vs manifest static wiring must be decided before SVC supervision and rebind (V0.5) so services do not invent bootstrap protocols; V0 demo rebinding to a restarted B exercises the initial handoff.

title: Implement the Capability discovery namespace decided in the service discovery ADR
justification: V0.5 native init and compositor crash-rebind (SVC) need a defined way for components to obtain later Capabilities; implements decide-service-discovery.

title: Abstract Capability enforcement behind a kernel backend interface
justification: Kernel-metadata backend today, hardware later; must exist before freeze candidates are declared so the abstraction is exercised by the conformance tests.

title: Build a machine-checked model of Capability derivation, transfer and revocation
justification: Formal model must exist before freeze candidates (V1) and is re-checked at the V4 freeze; depends on spike-formal-tooling; model checking runs in CI.

title: Key persistent grants on Package identity and publisher, revoke on publisher change
justification: Critique missing requirement 18; V2 store client and update flows would otherwise drop grants on every update. Depends on persistent-grant-store and PKG signing identity.

title: Lint Component graph descriptions for explicit per-Component Capability sets
justification: Standing invariant (§11) enforced by lint over CMP graph descriptions: every Component in a graph declares its Capability set and receives nothing else; first matters when component graphs arrive at V0.5.

title: Attach only the granted Capability set to a launched Component
justification: V0.5 exit criterion: Image Viewer starts with UI and GPU Capabilities only and cannot open other files. Implements decide-grant-sources at launch time over PKG's manifest and SEC's grant taxonomy; the launcher passes the resolved set to CMP creation.

title: Register typed rights and Admin authority for every kernel object type
justification: V1 introduces NetworkConnection, AudioStream, Surface and Device object types (NET, AUD, GFX, HW); §7 requires per-type rights and a lint fails when a new object type lacks a rights declaration, scaling decide-rights-encoding.

title: Implement one-time and time-bounded Capability grants with per-application history
justification: V3 scope: Permissions UI v2 including per-application audit history and one-time grants; V3 exit requires converting a grant to one-time.

title: Isolate persistent grant stores per user session
justification: V3 exit criterion: two users with separate sessions, separate capability stores and separate encrypted data.

title: Implement the revocable persistent grant store with user revocation
justification: V1 daily-driving requires editors to retain user-selected files across restarts; implements decide-capability-persistence including recent-files and revocation.

title: Test immediate revocation across camera, microphone, files, network and screen capture
justification: V2 exit criterion: Permissions UI revocation takes effect immediately, tested with camera, microphone, files, network and screen capture; CAP owns the cross-object-type revocation test matrix that SEC's UI drives.

title: Implement rights and transfer-rights checks on every Capability Operation
justification: Implements the decide-rights-encoding ADR: each Operation on an object checks the holder's rights and each transfer checks delegation rights. Depends on decide-rights-encoding.

title: Survey KeyKOS, EROS, CapROS, Capsicum, Barrelfish and Theseus Capability patterns
justification: Critique moves research studies not informing a V0 surface to V0.5 non-gating; this survey informs the V0.5 persistence ADR (KeyKOS/EROS persistence) and confinement patterns.

title: Validate Capability ABI freeze candidates on QEMU-CHERI
justification: Critique: no L1 freeze before V4, freeze candidates at V1; this validates the candidates so the promise of hardware readiness is tested before candidacy. Re-run on the frozen ABI in capability-freeze-verification at V4.

title: Study CHERI capability hardware for ABI escape hatches
justification: Critique names CHERI escape hatches as a V0 spike that must precede the handle-representation ADR so the ABI reserves a sealed-pointer layout (§8, §65 rule 8).

title: Prototype Capability<T> and MemoryObject mapping on a CHERI/Morello emulator
justification: Concrete mapping prototype preceding the V1 hardware mapping ADR and the freeze-candidate validation.

title: Document how Capability<T> maps onto CHERI-style capability pointers
justification: Feeds decide-hardware-readiness; establishes the mapping the readiness ADR lists as invariants.

title: Evaluate Kani, TLA+ and Alloy for modelling the Capability derivation core
justification: GAP-0131 asks for the tooling evaluation; it must precede the V1 machine-checked model (formal-capability-model) so the model targets a chosen tool.

title: Prototype dense index, sparse token and sealed-pointer Capability handle layouts
justification: GAP-0483 requires the representation ADR to be backed by a prototype of each option; the V0 exit criterion demands an accepted handle-representation ADR.

title: Study hardware provenance tracking for Capability audit
justification: §8 research item scheduled at its inventory rung; non-gating input to audit design.

title: Prototype and measure revocation strategies at one million derived Capabilities
justification: Derivation-tree walk, epoch indirection and lazy check-on-use must be measured before the revocation semantics ADR; results are published, not claimed.

title: Study seL4 CSpaces, derivation trees, revocation and verification for CAP
justification: Critique keeps the seL4 capability study among the six V0 research studies because it directly informs the V0 handle-representation and revocation ADRs.

title: Study tagged memory implications for MemoryObject and Capability storage
justification: Input to decide-hardware-capability-mapping; MEM consulted for MemoryObject implications.

title: Test that UserSelected<T> results carry authority with no path-based check
justification: Standing invariant enforced by a test gate: the chooser (STO) returns a Capability and no subsequent path permission check exists; verifies the V0.5 chooser exit criterion and demo audit line.

title: Map immutable package objects directly into the Component AddressSpace
justification: Workstream scope 'address space from packages': verified-once, shared, position-fixed package objects mapped without a loader stage so the Component launches immediately after mapping.

title: Benchmark native application cold startup
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate 'cold startup measured and published' is a distinct metric from warm startup and needs its own harness and register entry.

title: Benchmark Component creation latency p50/p99 on QEMU and reference hardware
justification: V0 benchmark gate: creation latency measured and published (publish-only in V0, register target p50 <= 200 us, conditional adr above 500 us); the harness is reused by V1 (<= 100 us), V4 and 1.0 gates and makes Principle 4 a tracked metric.

title: Benchmark resident memory overhead per idle Component
justification: V0 benchmark gate: memory overhead per idle Component measured and published; the register carries the per-component target (order of 512 KB) so component graphs with hundreds of Components remain viable.

title: Benchmark native application warm startup from click to first presented frame
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate: warm startup measured for each of the four apps and published (register target p50 <= 20 ms for the smallest, §34); workstream scope names warm start under CMP and the same harness serves V1, V2, V4 and 1.0 gates.

title: Map immutable executable objects as Component Code
justification: A Component contains Code as mapped immutable executable objects; in V0 the objects come from the retained initramfs (packages arrive at V0.5), mapped read-only and shared across instances.

title: Implement Component exit causes, teardown and the 100k leak test
justification: Delivers typed exit causes (panic, stack overflow, OOM, cancelled, exited) observable through the Component handle, full resource reclamation on destroy, and the V0 exit test creating and destroying 100,000 Components with kernel memory growth under 1%.

title: Bring the Component L1 surface to freeze-candidate state with tests
justification: Ladder: L1 surfaces become freeze candidates at V1 with SDK v1 and freeze only at V4; delivers the surface review and candidate conformance tests for Object<Component>, spawn, exit causes and code mapping under the ABI freeze process.

title: Add fuzz targets for the Component spawn, exit and code-mapping surface
justification: V3 scope introduces continuous fuzzing (BLD infrastructure); CMP supplies the fuzz targets for its ABI surface so the 1.0 'no known open fuzzer crasher for 30 days' criterion is measurable.

title: Ship the conformance suite for the frozen Component L1 surface
justification: V4 exit: L1 frozen with a conformance suite; no L1 freeze happens before V4 per the critique, so the freeze-time conformance suite for Object<Component>, spawn and exit causes lands here.

title: Publish reproducible Component creation, memory and startup metrics
justification: 1.0 benchmark gates require every §54 metric published against Linux, Windows and macOS with methodology, raw data and scripts; CMP delivers the reproducible package for its three metrics under BEN methodology.

title: Write the Component section of the ABI stability statement
justification: 1.0 exit publishes the ABI stability statement and explicit non-promises; the Component section states what is frozen, the status of the in-address-space class and what stays personality-only.

title: Implement Component creation as one kernel operation over Linux internals
justification: Phase C initial implementation: a single native operation creates the AddressSpace, capability set, owned TaskGroup and ResourceDomain membership by wrapping task_struct, mm_struct, namespaces and cgroups; verifies the V0 exit criterion that a Component can be created, granted capabilities, run code and be destroyed.

title: Verify the native isolation path needs no daemon, namespace, overlay or fork
justification: Acceptance suite over the package-based launch path proving the §53 native isolation path (create ResourceDomain, create Component, attach capabilities, map package, schedule) involves no runtime daemon, namespace setup, overlay mount, image layers or fork/exec.

title: Implement the Component creation fast path to the register target
justification: V1 benchmark gate sets creation p50 <= 100 us; implements the mechanism chosen by decide-wrapper-vs-native (prewarmed templates, cached page tables, batched capability-table setup) and verifies it with bench-component-creation.

title: Publish Component creation beside fork+exec, clone and podman run
justification: V1 benchmark gate requires creation latency published beside fork+exec, clone and container start on the same hardware; extends the V0 harness with the Linux baselines under BEN methodology, no superiority claim.

title: Decide whether every Component owns a hardware address space
justification: Determines whether an intra-address-space component class exists for plugins and decoders; V0 exit requires accepted adrs for all architectural choices and this one bounds isolation cost before applications are architected as component graphs. Depends on spike-in-address-space-isolation.

title: Decide what replaces PID, parent/child, exit status and process groups
justification: Component replaces process as the unit of isolation; this adr fixes the native replacements for process identity, lineage, exit status and grouping (options: Object<Component> handles only, handle plus kernel-visible lineage, opaque identity with supervisor-held lineage) that every V0 build task assumes.

title: Decide static manifest graphs versus dynamic child instantiation
justification: Decides whether component graphs are declared in the package manifest, instantiated dynamically by a parent, or both with constraints on dynamic children; moved to V0.5 per the critique and precedes graph-instantiation.

title: Decide Component plus ResourceDomain as the native isolation model
justification: Records that container-based isolation is replaced by Component + ResourceDomain and that OCI containers live in the Linux personality; the §53 non-goals (no daemon, no namespace step, no overlay mount, no image layers) become the standing rules this adr adopts and lint-no-process-shapes enforces.

title: Decide the order and equivalence tests for replacing the Component wrapper
justification: Phase C later: chooses which wrapper pieces (mm_struct, namespaces, cgroups, task_struct) are replaced first and the ABI-equivalence strategy; options include address-space-first, membership-first, and big-bang replacement.

title: Decide Component panic, abort and typed exit-cause semantics
justification: Critique EXTRA-004: a Rust panic aborts only its Component, stack overflow and OOM are typed exit causes reported to the supervisor, and no unwinding crosses the ABI; options are abort-only, unwind-to-component-boundary, and per-component policy. Required by the V0 fault demo.

title: Decide how personality processes map onto Components
justification: V1 daily-driving through the Linux personality and Wine bring-up require a decided mapping of Linux and Windows processes to Components (one Component per process, per process tree, or a personality ResourceDomain hosting plain tasks) and how PID and exit status surface through Object<Component>.

title: Decide the native Component spawn primitive that replaces fork and exec
justification: fork() has no native equivalent; the adr chooses between spawn-from-immutable-code-object, template-clone and builder-object-then-start shapes and records that Unix process startup is never the native creation mechanism.

title: Decide the Phase A Component implementation strategy
justification: V0 exit criteria name the wrapper-vs-native Component decision as a required accepted adr; options are thin wrapper, wrapper plus prewarmed templates, and early native object, chosen from spike-creation-strategies and spike-creation-cost-breakdown.

title: Launch Components in degraded mode when optional capabilities are denied
justification: V2 exit criterion: an application whose optional capability requests are denied at install still launches in a declared degraded mode; the launch path must distinguish required from optional declared capabilities.

title: Build the V0 demo: Component A requests, Component B returns a MemoryObject
justification: The §59 demo: A sends Channel<Request>, B returns a result by MemoryObject ownership transfer, shown with os trace; the same pair runs the fault demo where B panics and A observes a typed disconnect and rebinds to a restarted B.

title: Write the Component design guidelines for SDK v1
justification: V1 exit publishes SDK v1; developers need guidance on when to split an application into Components, graph patterns from §11, capability attenuation per child and panic/exit-cause handling.

title: Complete the Component L1 reference documentation
justification: V3 exit requires 100% L1 reference pages; DOC generates signatures from the IDL, CMP writes the lifecycle, exit-cause, graph and isolation semantics prose.

title: Enforce constraints on dynamically created child Components
justification: Implements the constraint half of decide-graph-declaration: children receive only attenuated parent capabilities, nest inside the parent's ResourceDomain, and are bounded by SCH kernel-object limits; tested with a child attempting to exceed its parent's authority.

title: Instantiate declared component graphs with attenuated per-child authority
justification: §11: applications are component graphs where each child gets only the authority it requires; the parent creates children per the accepted declaration model, wires Channels between Inputs and Outputs and attenuates capabilities per child.

title: Scale-test 500-Component graphs for creation, memory and teardown
justification: §11 browser-style graphs need hundreds of Components per application; verifies bounded per-component memory and creation latency under contention on all three V2 target machines.

title: Implement the in-address-space Component class if the adr adopts it
justification: Conditional on decide-address-space-model: gives fine-grained sandboxes (the V1 Wasm editor plugin demo) a kernel-visible Component identity, capability set and ResourceDomain membership without a hardware address space; WASM owns the runtime.

title: Bind Component Inputs<T> and Outputs<T> declarations to Channels at launch
justification: Critique ordering fix: the CMP Inputs/Outputs manifest belongs at V0.5; §10 lists Inputs<T> and Outputs<T> as Component contents and the V0.5 four apps need declared typed endpoints wired by the launch path rather than discovered ad hoc.

title: Close external audit findings against the Component isolation boundary
justification: V4 exit requires the external audit closed; findings against Component isolation, exit handling or code mapping are fixed with regression tests and re-verified by isolation-negative-tests.

title: Publish the Component isolation boundary assurance report
justification: Before daily-driving, enumerate every retained Linux kernel path reachable from a native Component and show each is gated by a capability or unreachable; feeds the SEC threat model and the V4 external audit.

title: Prove Component isolation with negative tests and the isolation demo
justification: Negative tests that a Component cannot reach memory, objects or capabilities it was not granted, cannot enter the Linux syscall ABI without a personality capability, and receives a typed denial visible in the audit log (V0 isolation demo).

title: Cache Component launch metadata across launches
justification: Warm start caches the Component graph, Capability set and relocation state. CMP owns launch; PKG supplies the store objects.

title: Add the ABI review gate rejecting process, thread and container shapes
justification: Critique: constraints become lint or review-gate tasks, not one task per rule; this gate fails CI when a native Component entry point exposes PID, fork/exec, process-group, namespace, overlay-mount, image-layer or daemon-dependent shapes.

title: Isolate Components across user sessions with negative tests
justification: V3 introduces multi-user; Components created in one user session inherit that session's ResourceDomain and identity, and negative tests show no cross-user reach to memory, objects or capabilities.

title: Show ResourceDomain plus capabilities subsume mount, pid, net, user and ipc namespaces
justification: Per-namespace mapping with tests: mount to capability-scoped storage, pid to Object<Component> handles, net to network capabilities, user to no ambient uid, ipc to Channels; proves native software needs no namespace setup step.

title: Implement the native AddressSpace object replacing mm_struct wrapping
justification: First step of the native Component implementation: page-table templates and prewarmed address spaces owned by the native object while the Component ABI stays unchanged.

title: Implement the native launch path from package entry to scheduled Component
justification: §34/§53: resolve the package generation entry, create ResourceDomain, create Component, attach declared capabilities, map immutable package objects, schedule; required by the V0.5 cold-boot-to-desktop demo and the four apps.

title: Replace namespace and cgroup wrapping with native Component membership
justification: Removes namespace and cgroup creation from the native path so Component and ResourceDomain membership are native kernel state; the Linux personality keeps namespaces for compatibility software only.

title: Define Object<Component> in the native object model
justification: Specifies the Component object, its lifecycle states, rights and handle semantics at S-state prototyped (no L1 freeze in V0 per the critique), the Native Platform layer entry for Components.

title: Preserve Component identity across restart so clients can rebind
justification: V0.5 exit criterion (compositor crash recovery rebinding all windows) and §32 need a stable Component slot identity with an instance generation counter on Object<Component>; SVC owns supervision, CMP owns the identity and exit-cause surface it consumes.

title: Document a browser-shaped Component graph as the composition example
justification: §11 example graph (UI, Network, per-Tab Renderer) is CMP composition guidance for SDK samples, not an SDK runtime feature.

title: Share verified code pages across Component instances of one Package
justification: §34: executables are verified once, shared and deduplicated; sharing code pages across instances is the main lever that keeps per-component resident memory under the register target measured by bench-idle-component-memory.

title: Study Erlang/BEAM supervision and restart strategies for Component recovery
justification: Informs Component-side restart identity and exit-cause reporting consumed by SVC supervision at V0.5; non-gating research study scheduled at the rung where restart/rebind first matters.

title: Measure the dominant costs of Component creation on the Linux wrapper
justification: Prototype Component creation over task_struct/mm_struct/cgroups and attribute cost to address-space setup, page-table population, capability table and scheduler registration; the breakdown feeds decide-wrapper-vs-native and the V0 conditional adr if p50 exceeds 500 us.

title: Benchmark wrapper, prewarmed-template and native Component strategies
justification: Compare a thin wrapper, prewarmed address-space templates and a dedicated native kernel object against the tens-to-hundreds-of-microseconds target on QEMU and the reference desktop; the V0 wrapper-vs-native adr may not be accepted without these numbers.

title: Study Genode composition, session routing and resource budgets
justification: Research study informing decide-graph-declaration and SCH budget nesting; moved out of V0 per the critique because it does not inform a V0 surface.

title: Measure hardware address-space cost against SFI-style in-address-space isolation
justification: Measures the lower bound of isolation cost (address-space switch, TLB, page-table footprint) versus an SFI or Wasm-style in-address-space sandbox on legacy x86-64 hardware so decide-address-space-model rests on data rather than intuition.

title: Extend the warm-startup harness to every shipped native application
justification: V2 benchmark gate: application warm startup for all shipped native applications published with Terminal and Editor holding the register target; extends bench-warm-startup to the shell and store client.

title: Prove the native Component implementation keeps the ABI unchanged
justification: Runs the V0, V0.5 and V1 acceptance suites and bench-component-creation on the native implementation; V2 benchmark gate allows no regression above 10% without an accepted adr.

title: Add full-text search to the documentation site
justification: GAP-0380 explicitly requires full-text search on the versioned site; split from the site build so size stays one subsystem.

title: Build the versioned documentation site with per-release snapshots
justification: GAP-0380 remainder: versioned public site and per-release snapshots for SDK v1 consumers. Search is a sibling task. Hosting/CDN remains REL.

title: Publish the research study catalog and template
justification: workstreams.md and critique give DOC ownership of research/ comparative studies under §58. This is the catalog, template and index other workstreams' studies link from; GOV keeps process, citation rules and kill criteria (INV-1151, GAP-0070).

title: Add broken-link and outdated-example checks to docs CI
justification: V4 exit: broken-link and outdated-example checks pass in CI. Extends V1/V3 docs CI with link and snippet compilation against the freeze-candidate SDK.

title: Generate complete Layer 1 reference pages for every entry point
justification: V3 exit: 100% of Layer 1 ABI entry points have reference pages. ABI/IPC/CAP/MEM/TSK/CMP author semantics; DOC generates and publishes every page from IDL plus authored prose. Sibling of ABI-@docs-l1-reference-complete.

title: Complete remaining user, admin, SDK, compatibility and ABI docs
justification: V4 exit: user, admin, SDK (Rust and C), compatibility, security and ABI references complete. Editorial pass that closes holes left by per-guide tasks before sign-off.

title: Decide the documentation taxonomy and ownership
justification: GAP-0381. Options must name at least two taxonomies and assign an owner per class (user, administrator, developer, ABI specification, architecture and Decision record, compatibility). Required before the V1 site and generated reference; V1 is the earliest gate that needs it.

title: Decide the documentation toolchain, search and snapshots
justification: GAP-0380 dependents need a recorded choice of generator, site, full-text search and per-release snapshot scheme before the V1 IDL-to-docs site is built. Separate from taxonomy (information architecture). Same rung as the builds it unblocks.

title: Gate documentation coverage and the docs build in CI
justification: V3 exit: documentation build is part of CI and 100% of Layer 1 entry points have pages. Fails the merge if a Layer 1 symbol lacks a page or the site build breaks.

title: Generate API reference pages from the IDL and SDK
justification: GAP-0380 and the V1 IDL-to-docs gate: reference pages generated from IDL (via IPC doc-comment IR) and SDK sources so docs cannot drift from Interfaces. Domain workstreams author normative prose; DOC owns the generator.

title: Package documentation into the SystemGeneration store
justification: Offline os help and man pages must ship as an immutable Package in the SystemGeneration, rolled back with the OS. PKG owns the store; DOC owns the docs Package.

title: Publish architecture, Decision and glossary records
justification: GAP-0381 taxonomy includes architecture and ADR record; synthesis gives DOC glossary stewardship. Publishes Decision and architecture indexes and the product glossary on the V1 site. GOV keeps BASELINE.md, PRINCIPLES.md and the living §69 diagram.

title: Set up the documentation translation pipeline and string freeze
justification: GAP-0383. Contributor tooling and per-release freeze for documentation catalogs. UI/OS string catalogs stay TXT (GAP-0258); this pipeline consumes the freeze calendar and ships translated docs. License terms remain GOV GAP-0073.

title: Ship man-page equivalent docs inside the Linux personality
justification: EXTRA-040 second half: man-page equivalent for the Linux personality, generated from the same corpus so native and personality help cannot diverge. LNX installs the viewer; DOC owns the pages.

title: Ship offline os help from the generated docs corpus
justification: EXTRA-040 / critique item 39: on-device os help with no network. Content is the generated corpus; SDK supplies the os CLI. V2 desktop preview is the earliest rung that needs offline docs.

title: Record documentation review sign-off for beta
justification: V4 exit: a documentation review sign-off recorded. Process gate over the complete user, admin, SDK, compatibility, security and ABI set.

title: Snapshot the 1.0 documentation set per release
justification: 1.0 documentation completeness and GAP-0380 snapshot machinery: freeze the 1.0 docs set so later 1.x snapshots are comparable and the ABI reference stays pinned to the stability statement.

title: Prototype IDL-to-docs generation from the V0 IDL
justification: Critique: IDL-to-docs must exist at V1 with SDK v1. A V0.5 spike produces IR, page templates and missing-comment behaviour so the V1 generator is not invented on the freeze-candidate path. V0 cap forbids an earlier rung.

title: Write the Android permissions, Binder and A/B updates study
justification: Critique moves §58 research studies to DOC. Android permissions, Binder IPC, sandboxing and A/B updates inform SEC and PKG, not a V0 kernel surface.

title: Write the Redox Rust-in-kernel and schemes study
justification: Reassigned from KRN. §58 Redox study does not inform a V0 kernel surface (critique). V0 cap is 0 so the research/ paper lands at V0.5 as non-gating; GOV owns the research-program process (INV-1151).

title: Write the XNU Mach ports, launchd and entitlements study
justification: Reassigned from KRN. §58 XNU/launchd/entitlements study feeds SVC supervision and SEC sandbox, not the kernel fork. Same rung as V0.5 supervision, earlier than V1; V0 cap forbids V0.

title: Verify documentation completeness for the 1.0 gate
justification: 1.0 exit: Layer 1 ABI reference 100%, SDK guides for Rust and C, user, administrator, compatibility and security guides, release notes, documentation CI green. Gate-verifying checklist over the V3/V4 set.

title: Verify public docs suffice for unaided install
justification: V3 gate: a user without project involvement installs from public media following only public documentation (≥ 8 of 10). DOC verifies install and user guides are the sole materials and records gaps as tasks.

title: Wire documentation generation into CI
justification: V1 IDL-to-docs must not drift: CI builds generated pages and fails on generator errors. GOV GAP-0164 remains roadmap/ADR parse CI at V0; this is the product-docs pipeline.

title: Write the administrator guide
justification: GAP-0381 taxonomy and the 1.0 definition require an administrator guide. Public alpha adds FDE, Secure Boot, multi-user, updater and recovery, so V3 is the earliest gate. STO authors storage chapters.

title: Write the additional-language SDK guide
justification: V4 ecosystem: SDK bindings for C and one additional language, with developer-program documentation. DOC writes the guide for the language SDK selects.

title: Write the C SDK guide
justification: V4 and 1.0 exits require SDK guides for Rust and C. C bindings ship at V1; the complete C guide is the V4 documentation gate.

title: Write the os CLI reference from command metadata
justification: §64 first-class tooling (os inspect, trace, history, restore, env) is the daily-driving surface at V1. SDK owns the CLI; DOC publishes the reference that V2 os help snapshots.

title: Write Linux and Windows personality compatibility notes
justification: V2 gates W1 and L3; taxonomy names compatibility notes. First public mapping of what runs where, feeding the V3 compatibility guide. LNX/WIN own ratings; DOC publishes the notes.

title: Write the compatibility guide
justification: V3 exit: compatibility guide published and reviewed. Expands V2 notes into the public guide for Linux personality and Windows personality, including what deliberately does not exist. GOV GAP-0034 owns trademark wording.

title: Write the public contribution guide
justification: V3 scope lists a contribution guide among public documentation. GOV GAP-0066 is the V0 repo CONTRIBUTING process; this is the product-facing contributor guide on the docs site.

title: Write the desktop user guide
justification: V2 desktop-preview scope: shell, permissions UI, snapshots UI and store client need a user guide covering launch, grants, rollback and lock. Expanded at V3 for the unaided-install study.

title: Write the developer guide for the native SDK
justification: V1 scope ships SDK v1 to external developers; workstreams.md names references and guides. First-cut Rust developer guide; V3 completes and reviews it. Domain guides (UIP, CMP, SCH, SVC, PKG) are authored there and published through this pipeline.

title: Write developer-program documentation
justification: V4 exit: developer program documentation published; ≥ 100 external native Packages. REL/SDK own the program; DOC publishes the docs.

title: Write the documentation style guide
justification: V1 site and later translation (GAP-0383) need one voice, glossary casing and no-unmeasured-claim rules (§54 / INV-1039) before third-party contributions. Enforced later by docs CI.

title: Write the getting-started tutorial for a first Component
justification: V1 developer-preview onboarding: clone-to-running Component tutorial used by daily-driving and the SDK hello-Component path. GOV INV-0978 (reference example) is process-adjacent; this is the published tutorial.

title: Write the public install guide
justification: V3 exit: install guide published and reviewed; unaided-install study of 10 participants using only public documentation. INS owns the installer; DOC owns the guide.

title: Write migration guides for users and SDK porters
justification: GAP-0382. User guides from Linux distributions and Windows plus developer porting to the native SDK. SDK GAP-0455 is the V1 POSIX/Win32 concept map; this is the public-alpha migration set.

title: Write the POSIX and Win32 to native concept map
justification: Porting guide is documentation. SDK GAP-0455 reassigned to DOC; the V3 migration guides expand it.

title: Complete and review the SDK guide
justification: V3 exit: SDK guide published and reviewed; documentation coverage includes the developer guide. Promotes the V1 developer guide to the public-alpha SDK guide.

title: Publish the platform security guide
justification: 1.0 and V4 documentation gates require a security guide; V3 public alpha is the earliest audience. States what is protected in each power/lock/developer-mode state. SEC/GOV author policy (GAP-0241); DOC publishes through the site.

title: Write 1.0 release notes with V3 and V4 migration paths
justification: 1.0 exit: release notes with a migration path from V3 and V4, plus the explicit non-promises list. REL owns the channel; DOC authors the notes.

title: Attach the native Terminal and Editor to a development environment
justification: Workstream scope: editor and terminal integration. Grants the native Terminal and Editor the environment's endpoint and snapshot Capabilities so they attach without a Docker plugin. APP owns the apps; ENV owns the attach API.

title: Create a CapabilityNamespace for each development environment
justification: V1 os env scopes which Capabilities Components inside the environment may hold. Discovery model is CAP; ENV instantiates the namespace at environment creation.

title: Create a NetworkNamespace for each development environment
justification: V1 os env isolates service ports and network policy. Implements decide-endpoint-grant so declared services are reachable from shell, IDE and browser without ambient network. NET owns NetworkConnection objects.

title: Map environment resources onto a ResourceDomain
justification: V1 os env creates a ResourceDomain per environment and maps environment.yaml resources (memory, cpu) onto SCH budgets. Exceeding a budget returns a typed error and does not start further Components.

title: Create a StorageSnapshot for each development environment
justification: V1 cached enter needs a CoW view of project and dependency storage. ENV creates the snapshot; STO owns the primitive (STO-@environment-storage-snapshot). Acceptance: no overlay filesystem stack is used.

title: Convert docker-compose.yml and devcontainer.json to environment.yaml
justification: V2 adoption: converters report unsupported constructs explicitly so developers are not forced to hand-rewrite project environments.

title: Decide how environment endpoints are granted without ambient network
justification: Answers INV-0665 for the V1 enter gate. Options: per-service loopback Endpoint capabilities; named Capability<NetworkConnection> filtered to declared ports; vs a shared environment network grant. Must not confer ambient network authority (§9).

title: Decide whether DevelopmentEnvironment is kernel or userspace
justification: V1 scope composes ResourceDomain, StorageSnapshot, CapabilityNamespace, NetworkNamespace and Components (§35). Options: userspace supervisor Component; Package-profile instantiation with no extra object; new Layer 1 kernel object. §65 prefers userspace; no new L1 surface, so no V0 spike.

title: Decide environment.yaml schema versus Package manifest profile
justification: V1 os env gate needs a canonical project definition. Options: distinct environment.yaml schema; a profile of the Package manifest (§28). Also decides YAML versus typed manifest, lockfile location, version specifier locking (php: 8.6) and service Package discovery.

title: Decide how environment services are hosted and packaged
justification: V1 os env must reach Postgres and Redis. Options after spike-service-hosting: Linux-personality OCI images inside native isolation; native Packages; both with a documented default. Depends on the spike; precedes instantiate-services.

title: Implement the environment.yaml schema with lock and validation
justification: V1 os env from environment.yaml. Parser and schema for runtime, services and resources; identical yaml plus lock yields identical immutable Component sets. Depends on decide-env-schema. Parser fuzz remains SEC GAP-0130.

title: Publish the development environment authoring guide
justification: V3 exit: SDK guide published for strangers. ENV owns the environment.yaml, os env, converters and catalogue chapter; DOC owns the docs site.

title: Emit development environment changes as history events
justification: V1 exit: os history lists environment events (Changed project environment). ENV emits; PKG owns the log (PKG-@history-event-types-v1). Restore of environments is V2.

title: Build the environment.yaml conformance suite
justification: V4 feature freeze: permanent suite that identical yaml plus lock yields identical Component sets, nongoals still hold, and the php-postgres-redis reference still enters. B-025 remains BEN.

title: Implement development environment create, rebuild and destroy
justification: V1 scope os env lifecycle. Object operations for create, rebuild and destroy (snapshot drop, cache drop, Component teardown). SDK INV-0655 owns list/enter/leave CLI; this is the ENV object API those verbs call.

title: Implement DevelopmentEnvironment as composed native primitives
justification: V1 gate: development isolation is a native OS object, not a userspace container tool. Implements the object chosen by decide-env-placement as a composition of existing primitives. CLI verbs stay SDK (INV-0654, INV-0655, INV-1262).

title: Implement the development environment cache for warm enter
justification: V1 gate B-025 cached enter. Pre-resolves Packages, pre-creates StorageSnapshots and keeps warm Component images so a second enter reuses them. Measurement and docker-compose baseline stay BEN (INV-0661, INV-1026).

title: Inject service secrets as Capabilities into environment Components
justification: V1 enter gate: Postgres and Redis reachable without ambient authority (§9). Wires SEC secrets into service Components as Capabilities; no secret files in the project snapshot by default.

title: Expose DevelopmentEnvironment state through os inspect
justification: §64 and the OBS invariant that every primitive ships with inspect data. ENV owns DevelopmentEnvironment records (domain, snapshot, namespaces, Components, endpoints); SDK owns the os inspect CLI.

title: Instantiate environment services as isolated Components
justification: V1 enter with Postgres and Redis reachable. Instantiates runtime and services as Components inside the environment ResourceDomain and namespaces, including Linux-personality software per decide-service-hosting. LNX INV-0869 is the personality host; this is the ENV consumer.

title: Isolate development environments across user sessions
justification: V3 multi-user gate: two users with separate sessions and capability stores. Environments, snapshots, caches and endpoints of one user are not enterable or inspectable by the other.

title: Forbid OCI, Docker and VM dependencies in native software
justification: V0 standing lint for §36: native crates and services must not depend on an OCI runtime, Docker daemon, Linux VM or Docker Desktop. Collapses the §35 nongoals into one CI gate before any development environment ships.

title: Lock the environment.yaml schema for the 1.x line
justification: V4 feature freeze and Layer 2/3 version lock. Pins the environment.yaml and lockfile schema versions decided at V1, with old-definition/new-supervisor evolution tests. Not a Layer 1 freeze.

title: Publish environment runtimes as third-party Packages
justification: V3 public package repository: third parties publish additional environment runtimes and services into the catalogue. ENV defines the runtime Package contract; REL/PKG own signing and review.

title: Publish the environment service catalogue and version index
justification: Workstream scope: service catalogue. Indexed named runtimes and services with lockable versions for environment.yaml, backed by the Package repository. First-party php, postgres and redis are already in the V1 reference stack.

title: Rebuild a development environment when environment.yaml changes
justification: V2 daily-driving: an environment.yaml edit rebuilds via env-lifecycle, emits a history event, and leaves the previous snapshot restorable. STO owns file-change Operations; ENV owns the rebuild trigger.

title: Ship the php-postgres-redis reference environment.yaml
justification: V1 exit and demo: os env enter on a cached environment presents a working shell with Postgres and Redis reachable. This is the B-025 workload and the permanent V1 acceptance test.

title: Resolve environment.yaml runtimes to immutable Packages
justification: V1 runtime section (php: 8.6) resolves named versions to content-addressed Packages (§27, §29) and maps them directly; no image extraction. PKG owns the store; ENV owns the resolver.

title: Restore a development environment from system history
justification: V2 snapshots and rollback UI; §31 os restore covers environments. Re-materialises the environment recorded by emit-history-events. Full workspace restore (open projects) waits for 1.0 INV-0584.

title: Restore workspaces of open projects and environments
justification: 1.0 os restore ambition (§31): revert open projects and environments together. Builds on V2 restore-environment; APP owns window/session restore of the editor.

title: Provide the self-host environment.yaml for building the OS
justification: V1 exit: a clean checkout builds the full system image on the OS inside os env. ENV ships the tree's environment.yaml and enter path; BLD owns the toolchain and image build (B-039).

title: Expose a semantic startEnvironment action for automation
justification: V2 exit: example rule project opened → start environment. ENV exports a typed semantic action over the SEM registry; no AI broker here. SEM owns discovery and the rules engine.

title: Measure environment service hosting paths against B-025
justification: GAP-0552 requires measurement before the hosting ADR. Prototype Postgres and Redis as Linux-personality OCI images, as native Packages, and as a hybrid, and report cached and cold enter against B-025 for each path.

title: Store environment build outputs as content-addressed objects
justification: §27 cached build outputs from development environments. ENV writes through STO's hash-keyed cache (INV-0515); hits are reused across enters and rebuilds of the same inputs.

title: Verify cached environment enter on every Tier 1 machine
justification: 1.0 benchmark gate B-025 and the working-day demo in os env. Re-runs the reference stack enter on every Tier 1 machine; BEN publishes the number.

title: Bring up the AMD APU internal panel and external displays on the AMD laptop
justification: V2 hardware scope adds an AMD laptop; extends the driver regression matrix and hot-plug tests to it.
