title: Benchmark compositor restart-to-rebound time
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate 'compositor restart-to-rebound time'; the target lives in BEN's register, this task delivers the harness and published measurement.

title: Benchmark compositor frame deadline misses under a mixed desktop workload
justification: V2 benchmark gate: deadline misses under a scripted mixed workload at 60 Hz; harness plus published measurement, target in BEN's register.

title: Benchmark compositor commit-to-scanout latency against a Wayland compositor
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate and §54 'compositor frame latency'; published p50/p99 beside a Wayland compositor on the same hardware.

title: Benchmark GUI input-to-photon latency on the photodiode rig
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate and §54 'GUI input-to-photon latency'; harness drives LAB's V0 rig and publishes beside a Linux Wayland desktop on the same machine.

title: Implement Buffer as a GPU-compatible MemoryObject
justification: Defines the Buffer abstraction and the GPU-compatible / GPU-accessibility properties the compositor and renderers query; MEM owns the kernel property flag, GFX owns the Buffer semantics over it.

title: Implement per-Surface and per-Display screen capture capabilities
justification: V2 exit: an application without the capture capability receives a black or denied surface (tested).

title: Support colour-managed Surfaces with declared colour spaces
justification: Surfaces declare primaries and transfer function so composition converts correctly.

title: Fix compositor and trusted-UI findings from the external security audit
justification: V4 exit requires all High/Critical audit findings fixed and re-verified; the compositor enforces trusted UI, lock and capture and is in the audit scope.

title: Compose Surfaces on the GPU with scene graph and damage tracking
justification: GPU-accelerated composition using the decided render backend; damage tracking keeps the idle desktop at zero dropped frames.

title: Automate compositor kill and verify every client Surface rebinds and renders
justification: V0.5 exit: 100 consecutive passes on QEMU and 20 on hardware in CI.

title: Drive a single fixed-refresh display through atomic DRM/KMS from the compositor
justification: V0.5 exit: compositor drives the reference GPU via DRM/KMS and presents at the display's fixed refresh.

title: Implement compositor-owned lock mode inhibiting input and overlay
justification: V1 scope includes session lock; APP owns the lock UI, GFX enforces input inhibition, notification hiding policy and the no-overlay guarantee on idle, lid close and suspend.

title: Implement disconnect, rebind and restore-state for compositor clients
justification: §32 client contract in the UI runtime and compositor; applications continue rendering after restart with no exit. Depends on SVC supervision semantics.

title: Run the compositor as a privileged Component holding Display and DRM master
justification: Compositor lifecycle under SVC supervision with DRM master and Display capabilities granted from the system generation, not ambient root.

title: Write the compositor and trusted-UI section of the threat model
justification: Extends SEC's V0 threat model with overlay, spoofing, capture and crash-to-unlock threats before the trusted-UI and lock designs are fixed.

title: Define and implement the ComputeQueue abstraction shared with HET
justification: §39/§37 shared object; V1 Mesa-in-Component needs compute submission and HET's V2 ComputeDevice demo consumes it.

title: Decide compositor architecture: monolithic or split display/scene/input
justification: Depends on the split-latency spike. Options: monolithic display server plus shell; split display server / window manager / shell; display+input core with out-of-process shell.

title: Decide compositor infrastructure reuse versus build-anew
justification: One decision: which existing compositor infrastructure (if any) is vendored for DRM/KMS plumbing. Options: Smithay crates, wlroots via FFI, Mutter/KWin fork, greenfield Rust.

title: Decide explicit GPU synchronisation as the only path for native Surfaces
justification: Standing invariant decided once: timeline semaphores / drm_syncobj mandatory, no implicit-sync path. Options: explicit-only, explicit with implicit bridge for personalities, implicit default.

title: Decide the compositor frame scheduling model
justification: V0.5 exit requires an accepted ADR for compositor frame scheduling. Options: fixed vblank-aligned callbacks, deadline-scheduled callbacks with per-client budgets, client-driven presentation timing.

title: Decide the GPU userspace strategy from the Mesa-behind-capabilities spike
justification: One decision: how Mesa is hosted (unmodified Mesa with brokered fd, patched Mesa WSI layer, Mesa inside a Linux-personality helper). Depends on the Mesa spike.

title: Decide the HDR and colour management pipeline
justification: V2 exit requires an accepted HDR/color pipeline ADR. Options: scRGB linear compositing, PQ/HLG passthrough with per-surface transforms, hybrid with per-plane hardware LUTs.

title: Decide the GPU API native applications render with
justification: Options: Vulkan via Mesa inside the Component, a WebGPU-like native API over RenderQueue, or both with Vulkan as the escape hatch. Must precede RenderQueue implementation and SDK v1.

title: Decide the NVIDIA support stance for 1.0
justification: V3 Tier 1 adds an NVIDIA desktop 'decided by ADR'. Options: open kernel modules plus NVK/Mesa, proprietary userspace via the Linux personality, unsupported.

title: Decide the proprietary GPU kernel driver policy
justification: Critique places the NVIDIA kernel-module adr at V1; covers GPL-only symbols, tainting and support commitments. Options: open kernel modules plus NVK, proprietary module tolerated untainted-support, unsupported.

title: Decide whether RDP/VNC clients and a remote-desktop server are in 1.0 scope
justification: Pulled from V4 to V3 so the decision precedes the V4 feature freeze. Options: out of scope for 1.0, clients only via the Linux personality, native server over remote surfaces.

title: Decide compositor rendering backend policy: Vulkan-only or Vulkan plus GL
justification: Evaluated against the V2 target machine list so older laptops are not excluded silently. Options: Vulkan-only, Vulkan plus GL fallback, Vulkan plus software fallback only.

title: Decide which compositor state survives restart and where it is checkpointed
justification: Answers the §32 question for geometry, stacking, focus and workspace. Options: kernel-owned window objects, persistent broker Component, client-replayed state.

title: Decide whether Wayland is served by the compositor or by a bridge Component
justification: Determines whether LNX's Wayland bridge translates into the native UI protocol or the compositor speaks Wayland directly; must land before the V0.5 Wayland app gate.

title: Demonstrate compositor crash, restart, rebind and continued rendering
justification: §60 service restart/rebind demo; the Text Editor keeps its unsaved buffer.

title: Implement display arrangement and per-display configuration persistence
justification: Arrangement, primary display and per-display mode persisted per connector fingerprint; surfaced by APP settings.

title: Build the per-machine display test suite for Tier 1 hardware
justification: V3 six Tier 1 machines fully tested each release and the HCL needs display hot-plug, HDR/VRR and multi-monitor results per machine; runs every RC through V4 and 1.0.

title: Define and implement Display with mode, refresh, scaling, HDR and VRR metadata
justification: Single display at fixed refresh is exercised in V0.5; the metadata fields are defined now so V2 HDR/VRR do not change the interface shape.

title: Move display management policy into a user-space service
justification: Mode selection, hot-plug policy and per-display preferences outside the compositor core so V2 multi-monitor policy can restart independently.

title: Implement fractional scaling in the compositor
justification: V1 Intel laptop with HiDPI internal display; L2 integration check scores correct scaling.

title: Define and implement Frame with explicit fences and timelines for presentation
justification: Presentation unit carrying timeline semaphores; implements the explicit-sync-only decision from the first compositor.

title: Implement client frame callbacks aligned to display deadlines
justification: Implements the frame scheduling adr; required for the animating-at-refresh V0.5 exit criterion.

title: Build golden-image comparison tolerant of documented rasterisation differences
justification: Headless desktop testing needs per-backend tolerance rules so virtio-gpu, software and AMD renders compare against one golden set.

title: Enforce ResourceDomain GPU time and memory budgets
justification: §23 GPU budget replaces vendor-specific controls for native software; depends on the V1 enforcement spike.

title: Grant Capability<RenderQueue> at Component creation without other surfaces
justification: §9.1 PhotoEditor example: a launched application receives render queues only; screen contents and other surfaces stay unreachable.

title: Run the retained GPU driver regression matrix on virtio-gpu and the AMD desktop
justification: Second of the two permitted 'retain X' tasks: kernel DRM regression matrix (amdgpu, i915/xe, nouveau, virtio-gpu) run per kernel rebase, extended per milestone as machines arrive.

title: Report explicit degraded recovery to users and clients after GPU reset
justification: §32: where driver constraints prevent seamless recovery the system reports it rather than failing silently; needed once real Mesa workloads run at V1.

title: Publish the 1.0 GPU support statement and non-promises
justification: 1.0 explicitly does not promise a native GPU driver stack; publishes the retained DRM/Mesa posture and the NVIDIA stance for the support window.

title: Run shader cache and GPU allocation broker as user-space services
justification: §33 higher-level GPU services above retained DRM/KMS; the allocation broker also holds the DRM fd on behalf of Components per the GPU userspace strategy adr.

title: Add CI lint forbidding DRM ioctls, device nodes and fourcc in public graphics IDL
justification: Enforces the §39 invariant and the explicit-sync-only rule as a review gate over the IDL rather than one task per rule.

title: Add fuzz targets for compositor and graphics interfaces
justification: V3 gate: IPC fuzzing runs continuously with no open crasher older than 14 days; BLD owns the fuzz infrastructure, GFX owns its targets.

title: Review Surface, Buffer, RenderQueue, Display and Frame as SDK v1 freeze candidates
justification: V1 SDK v1 marks L2 interfaces as freeze candidates; nothing L1 freezes before V4 per the critique.

title: Use the hardware cursor plane for the pointer
justification: Removes cursor motion from the composition path; prerequisite for direct scanout.

title: Verify external display, HDR and VRR on every HCL Tier 1 machine per release
justification: 1.0 HCL lists external displays and HDR/VRR as working on every Tier 1 machine; runs the V3 display test suite as a release gate.

title: Output HDR10 from the compositor with a native HDR test application
justification: V2 exit: HDR10 verified on the HDR display with a native HDR test app; needs LAB's reference display and colorimeter.

title: Expose HDR Surfaces to the Wayland bridge and Windows personality
justification: V2 exit requires a Windows-personality HDR game; LNX/WIN consume the HDR surface metadata GFX provides.

title: Implement HDR-to-SDR and SDR-in-HDR tone mapping
justification: Mixed SDR and HDR surfaces on one display require tone mapping under the decided colour pipeline.

title: Automate 100 hot-plug and unplug cycles including an MST daisy-chained dock
justification: V2 exit criterion, extended per the critique to cover DisplayPort MST docks.

title: Support render offload selection and mux switching across both personalities
justification: Per-application GPU selection surfaced through RenderQueue capabilities and passed through the Wayland bridge and Wine.

title: Apply per-display ICC profiles in the compositor
justification: Colour management baseline for creative users; validated with the colorimeter.

title: Test zero dropped frames over a 60 s idle desktop capture
justification: V0.5 exit criterion verified by capture-card or KMS vblank counters on the reference desktop.

title: Support tearing and immediate presentation for fullscreen Surfaces
justification: Fullscreen games opt into tearing/async presentation; exposed to the Windows personality via the Frame interface.

title: Tune the presentation path to meet the input-to-photon p99 target
justification: V4 benchmark gate: input-to-photon p99 within one frame interval plus 4 ms and deadline misses under 0.1% on every Tier 1 machine; verified by bench-input-to-photon and bench-frame-deadline-misses.

title: Bring up i915/xe internal panel and USB-C external display on the Intel laptop
justification: V1 hardware scope adds an Intel laptop with internal display plus one external display over USB-C; extends the driver regression matrix.

title: Present as late as possible before scanout to minimise latency
justification: §40 latency-aware presentation; measured by the input-to-photon and frame-latency benchmarks.

title: Lock Surface, Buffer, RenderQueue, Display and Frame interface versions for 1.x
justification: V4 exit: Layer 2 interface versions enumerated and locked with the old/new client evolution test passing for every core interface.

title: Test that a compositor crash while locked restarts into the locked state
justification: Pulled from V2 to V1 because the lock exists at V1 and crash-to-unlock is a known bypass class; standing invariant enforced by a permanent regression test.

title: Run Mesa Vulkan and OpenGL inside native Components with capability-mediated GPU
justification: V1 GPU acceleration for native applications; implements the GPU userspace strategy adr on top of the V0.5 spike.

title: Support DisplayPort MST topologies and daisy-chained docks
justification: Docking stations are the dominant laptop multi-monitor path; MST topology changes must not lose windows.

title: Render on one GPU and scan out on another
justification: §40 multi-GPU awareness; hybrid laptops route dGPU renders to iGPU-attached panels.

title: Support multi-monitor hot-plug, docks and USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode
justification: V2 exit: two displays with different scales and refresh rates, hot-plug without compositor restart or window loss.

title: Implement night-light colour temperature mode
justification: Desktop essential listed in GAP-0306; implemented as a compositor output transform, scheduled by APP settings.

title: Scan out fullscreen Surfaces directly via overlay planes
justification: V2 gaming proof of concept and HDR video need direct scanout to avoid a composition pass.

title: Implement per-display scale factors
justification: Different scale factors per display is an explicit V2 exit criterion.

title: Mediate Linux personality GPU access through RenderQueue capabilities
justification: V1 exit: browser WebGL, GL and Vulkan samples accelerated through the personality; LNX owns the personality, GFX owns the brokered render-node access.

title: Skip idle frames and lower refresh on battery under SCH energy intent
justification: §40 power-aware rendering for the V2 battery runtime benchmarks; PWR supplies the policy signal.

title: Provide a non-suppressible indicator layer for camera, microphone, capture and location
justification: Compositor-protected layer no Surface can cover, fed by CAP audit events with per-application attribution; APP's shell renders the icons.

title: Support Surfaces produced on another machine over a network transport
justification: The cross-machine half of §40 remote surfaces; 1.0 excludes distributed interfaces, so it is parked pending the remote-desktop scope adr and IPC's distribution transport.

title: Define and implement the RenderQueue abstraction
justification: Capability-scoped render submission object per §39; depends on the native GPU API adr.

title: Make shader cache, allocation broker and display policy restartable
justification: §32 selected GPU user-space services restartable where driver support permits; tested with kill-and-rebind like the compositor.

title: Inventory retained DRM/KMS drivers and pin the no-native-GPU-stack rule
justification: Collapses all GFX 'retain/preserve Linux DRM' items into one inventory (amdgpu, i915/xe, nouveau, virtio-gpu) that feeds KRN's retained-mechanism inventory and records the §57 non-goal as a standing review rule.

title: Build the OS-owned screen recorder over the capture capability
justification: Records via capture capability with encode delegated to MED's hardware encoder Component.

title: Build the OS-owned screen-share picker with per-app scoping for portals
justification: Trusted-UI picker minting capture capabilities; LNX's xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast calls into it.

title: Build the OS-owned screenshot tool with region selection and annotation
justification: §40 forbids unrestricted capture so the OS must supply the tool users would otherwise install.

title: Dispatch seat input from the HW input service to the focused Surface
justification: V0.5 exit: a native application receives keyboard and mouse input. HW owns devices and UIP owns the input protocol; this is the compositor's focus and hit-test dispatch plus software cursor.

title: Evaluate Smithay, wlroots, Mutter and KWin for DRM/KMS plumbing reuse
justification: Prototype-and-measure study of reusable DRM/KMS, GBM and input plumbing versus building anew; produces the option matrix the reuse adr needs.

title: Prototype monolithic versus split compositor and measure crash-rebind and latency
justification: Crash recovery and latency pull in opposite directions; the prototype measures both for each candidate split before the UI protocol depends on it.

title: Spike dma-buf interoperability between MemoryObject and DRM drivers
justification: Measures whether a GPU-compatible MemoryObject can be imported by amdgpu/i915/virtio-gpu as the same physical pages; result gates the zero-copy import build.

title: Spike GPU time and memory budgets via DRM scheduler and cgroup GPU controllers
justification: Measures enforceability on amdgpu, i915/xe and NVIDIA before the V2 ResourceDomain GPU budget build.

title: Assess GPU driver risk and mitigation plan for AMD, Intel and NVIDIA
justification: §56.1 names GPU the hardest hardware problem; the report fixes the AMD/Intel/NVIDIA mitigation plan before any V0.5 graphics spike commits to a path. Report deliverable, no code.

title: Spike Mesa/Vulkan inside a native Component without ambient /dev/dri access
justification: Proves Surface/Buffer/RenderQueue can map onto DRM render nodes, GBM and Vulkan WSI with the DRM fd held by a broker, not the application; the V0.5 risk register names Mesa's fd assumptions as the top graphics risk.

title: Evaluate NVIDIA open modules with NVK and proprietary userspace against capabilities
justification: V2 tracks an NVIDIA desktop as experimental; the spike measures each stack behind brokered device access before the stance adr.

title: Test that a UI+GPU Component cannot read other Surfaces or the framebuffer
justification: Enforces the §9.1 no-screen-contents invariant with a denial test rather than a standalone rule task.

title: Define and implement Object<Surface> with typed interfaces
justification: Core §39 abstraction; every window, chooser and bridge surface is built on it.

title: Keep Surface and window objects alive across compositor restart
justification: Implements the restart-state-checkpoint adr: objects owned by the kernel or a persistent broker so the restarted compositor re-attaches them.

title: Render choosers, prompts and elevation in compositor-protected trusted Surfaces
justification: The V0.5 UserSelected chooser grants authority; applications must not overlay, spoof, resize or inject input into it.

title: Provide software-rendered and virtio-gpu compositor paths for QEMU CI
justification: V0.5 hardware scope names virtio-gpu for compositor CI; without it every UI change needs physical hardware.

title: Support Surfaces produced by a KVM guest as remote surfaces
justification: §40 remote surfaces for producers inside a VM; VIRT's V2+ VM manager presents guest virtio-gpu output as native windows.

title: Support variable refresh rate output with display-reported verification
justification: V2 exit: VRR verified via display reporting at variable frame rates.

title: Define window objects as Capability<Surface> handles over typed interfaces
justification: §60 window objects created and managed through typed interfaces, not a Wayland-shaped protocol.

title: Define the window management policy interface between compositor and shell
justification: Typed interface for placement, stacking, focus and workspace policy so APP's shell can own policy without DRM master.

title: Import a MemoryObject into the GPU driver without copying
justification: Renderer hands a MemoryObject to the GPU as the same physical pages via dma-buf; verified by page-identity test. Depends on the dma-buf spike.

title: Decide code hosting forge and repository layout
justification: Forge versus self-hosting and where the Markdown roadmap lives, plus whether that repo is standalone. Distinct from BLD GAP-0086 (kernel/userspace topology). Every V0 CI and review path depends on it.

title: Decide codec and proprietary-font shipping and patent policy
justification: Pulled from V2/V3 to V1 because MED packages codecs at V1 (EXTRA-058). One Decision: default-image royalty-free codecs, hardware-passthrough H.264/HEVC/AAC, optional packages, jurisdiction splits, and proprietary fonts versus metric substitutes for migrated documents.

title: Decide redistribution licensing for personality software wrappers
justification: Redistribution licensing and wrapper ownership for third-party Linux/Windows software (Flatpak, Wine wrappers, installers) is GOV legal policy. PKG decide-personality-packaging is mechanics only. Options: project-owned wrappers with redistributable licenses versus publisher-owned wrappers versus no official repackaging.

title: Decide contributor licensing, copyright holder and DCO or CLA
justification: One contribution-model Decision: DCO Signed-off-by on kernel commits, DCO versus non-assignment CLA for userspace, copyright retained versus assigned, and whether a relicensing clause exists. Provenance cannot be reconstructed after the first external commit.

title: Decide open-source-steward versus manufacturer status under CRA
justification: Critique LIC fold sends CRA/EAA policy to GOV. SEC GAP-0078 assesses obligations; this Decision picks steward versus manufacturer before 1.0. EAA conformity stays ACC.

title: Decide the license for published benchmark and HCL datasets
justification: CC0 versus ODbL for community datasets. REL consumes the Decision for HCL and benchmark publication.

title: Decide the documentation license and translation terms
justification: CC-BY-SA versus CC-BY versus CC0 and translation-contribution terms, before V1 docs site and V3 translations. DOC consumes the Decision.

title: Assess export-control and cryptography distribution obligations
justification: Public alpha distributes disk encryption and TLS worldwide. Decision on classification and mirror obligations; filing is docs-file-ear-notice.

title: Decide firmware blob redistribution for official versus non-free
justification: V1 Intel-laptop Wi-Fi/GPU images cannot ship blobs without redistribution rights. Policy of official image versus non-free repository versus download-on-demand. HW GAP-0015 is the per-blob audit.

title: Decide font shipping versus metric-compatible substitutes
justification: Workstreams.md gives font licensing to GOV. V0.5 ships the first immutable image with fonts; TXT-@font-license-audit inventories terms. This Decision allows only redistributable fonts in that image. Proprietary fonts and metric substitutes stay with GAP-0473 on the V1 codec Decision.

title: Decide the funding model and publish infrastructure-cost finances
justification: Donations, sponsorship tiers or fiscal sponsor, with transparent finances. Pulls GAP-0395 from V3 because hardware, CI, CDN and signing cost money before V2 lab and desktop gates.

title: Adopt the governance charter for decisions and maintainers
justification: BDFL versus council versus foundation TSC, appointment, removal, voting and conflict resolution, before the repo opens to external contributors at V1.

title: Decide legal-entity form able to hold marks and signing keys
justification: Foundation, fiscal sponsor or company as counterparty for trademarks, signing keys, shim, OIN and vendor agreements. Depends on spike-entity-jurisdiction. Needed before V1 trademark filing and V3 public distribution.

title: Decide the license firewall and outbound project licenses
justification: One license-policy Decision mapping Layer 1 to GPLv2 and Layers 2–4 to a chosen permissive class, picking the userspace-service license (needed before V0.5 headers), licensing the roadmap/decisions repo, and stating outbound terms for native kernel code beside inherited GPLv2. Coordinates with KRN-@adr-native-kernel-code-license. V0 because copyleft leak and missing headers cannot be fixed later.

title: Decide whether Linux appears in product naming
justification: Linux is a registered trademark. Obtain an LMI sublicense or forbid Linux in product naming before public alpha marketing.

title: Decide OEM partnerships or hardware certification versus later
justification: Question: OEM/certification before 1.0 or park to post-1.0. A certified machine is the strongest adoption vector and a scarce-engineering commitment.

title: Decide Open Invention Network membership and a patent pledge
justification: Patent exposure grows with public distribution. OIN membership and a defensive pledge require the V1 legal entity.

title: Decide the 1.0 portability commitment as x86-64 only shipping
justification: §38: ship x86-64 only while the ABI stays architecture-neutral. Recorded before SDK v1 freeze candidates so ARM64/RISC-V remain LATER without fossilizing x86 into Layer 1.

title: Decide redistribution policy for third-party Linux and Windows software
justification: Flatpak, AppImage, Wine wrappers and whose license applies. PKG implements; GOV records the legal policy.

title: Decide package-repository developer agreement, content and DMCA terms
justification: Public alpha repository is an intermediary: developer agreement, content policy, malware removal and DMCA notice. Legal, not REL mechanics.

title: Decide the Markdown-plus-Rust-CLI roadmap process
justification: Accepted as D-0001 during repository generation: Markdown sources of truth, a small Rust validator, draft IDs then assign-ids, no calendar dates, generated roll-ups. GOV-@build-roadmap-registers implements the remaining register and parseability work.

title: Decide governance of the standard semantic interface catalogue
justification: Who may extend Document/Mail/Calendar/Project and how RFCs land, before the V2 automation-then-AI demo. SEM owns registry implementation; GOV owns catalogue governance. AI broker stays after a done registry task.

title: Decide opt-in usage telemetry policy apart from crash reporting
justification: V3 opt-in alpha telemetry gate. What is collected, anonymisation, retention and the user-visible toggle. Implementation is OBS/INS/REL; INS GAP-0043 is the privacy policy.

title: Decide trademark usage, derivative branding and compatible-with claims
justification: V3 exit requires a published trademark policy. Derivatives, spins, merchandise, compatible-with claims, remixes and unofficial builds. Third-party marks already handled at V2.

title: Decide vendor NDA policy for hardware documentation
justification: What may be read versus reproduced. Hardware enablement may use NDA docs; the tree and public docs may not.

title: Decide whether to run a vulnerability reward program
justification: 1.0 funding and triage-capacity Decision. SEC GAP-0047 is the V4 bounty-or-not design; this confirms funding at the stable declaration.

title: Decide the workstream-split procedure at the size warning
justification: CONVENTIONS: files over workstream_lines_warning are remedied by a GOV adr. Critique expects an APP shell/apps split around V2. Records prefix permanence, See also, and that old IDs never move.

title: Enable independent verification for every done V1 and later task
justification: Critique contradiction 10 and CONVENTIONS §13: switch require_independent_verification on when V1 is active so agents cannot self-close. V0 already requires it for adr and Freezes.

title: Implement roadmap check --base, impact summary and covers audit
justification: Critique structure weaknesses 5 and 9 and CONVENTIONS planned GOV commands: diff-aware check --base, impact --summary, and covers-orphan reporting. Needed once parallel workstreams land, before V1 contributor traffic.

title: Warn when a hub task's fan-in exceeds the configured threshold
justification: Critique structure weakness 5: ABI-shape, IDL, threat-model and hardware ADRs will be depended on by hundreds of tasks; the validator must warn so hubs can be split.

title: Implement roadmap stale, slipped, history and dropped reasons
justification: AGENTS.md planned GOV commands stale, slipped and history, plus critique dropped-reason taxonomy (already in fields.json enums). Needed once V1 has a living task graph.

title: Implement roadmap mutation commands from claim through renumber
justification: AGENTS.md and CONVENTIONS §18 list claim, unclaim, block, done, drop, split, move and renumber as GOV tooling still done by hand. Ship them before V1 external contributors edit tasks.

title: Complete roadmap registers, ADR CI and task parseability
justification: Workstreams.md gives this repo's tooling to GOV. Finish corpus-register schema/validation (entries stay LNX/WIN), add the invariants register with Enforced-by links, and fail CI on broken ADR/task ID links or unparseable templates. IDL-to-docs generation remains DOC/SDK.

title: Add See also citations so gates can name LATER tasks
justification: Critique structure weakness 11: the 1.0 2.0-planning RFC must cite LATER items without depending on them. Ship the field before V3 gates grow See-also lists.

title: Verify published governance, license, trademark, RFC and security
justification: 1.0 exit: license, trademark, contribution, RFC and security policies published. Gate-verifying checklist over earlier GOV deliverables.

title: Publish 1.x maintenance-branch and backport governance
justification: 1.0 scope: 1.x maintenance branch and backport policy (GOV, KRN). KRN creates the kernel branch; GOV states who may backport and how ABI freeze is preserved.

title: Publish RFC, ADR, research and ABI-review process with principles
justification: V0 exit requires accepted ADRs with rejected options. Encode RFC stages, ADR lifecycle, §57 checklist, PRINCIPLES.md, §68 litmus questions, fossilization review, heightened ABI review versus SDK, and the research-programme process that graduates spikes. Invariants of borrowing and replacement become ADR-template gates.

title: Publish charter, vision, architecture map and layer stability policy
justification: V0 identity surface: MISSION.md from §70, vision of what is not built (§1), living §4/§69 architecture map with workstream owners, and the per-layer stability policy (§66). ABI later fills concrete L1/L2 deprecation windows.

title: Adopt a Code of Conduct with named enforcement body
justification: Required before the repository opens to external contributors at developer preview. V3 community infra adds moderation roles on top.

title: Stand up community channels with moderation and archives
justification: V3 scope: forum, chat, announcement feed, mailing lists, moderation and archive guarantees. CoC already adopted at V1.

title: Publish contributing, CODEOWNERS, AI policy and V0 gate governance
justification: CONTRIBUTING, MAINTAINERS/CODEOWNERS, AI-assisted contribution rules, and who may close a gate with what evidence. Maps every §59 item into the V0 milestone file and states that V0 is not a usable desktop.

title: Assemble a legally reviewed redistributable compatibility corpus
justification: Legal review of Linux/Windows apps, games, fonts, images and documents CI may redistribute. Distinct from EXTRA-062 register schema. V1 L2 corpus cannot run on runners without it.

title: Publish the developer program and third-party onboarding
justification: V4 scope: developer program, 100 external native packages, 25 external contributors. SDK owns bindings; GOV owns the programme terms and publisher identity.

title: Publish downstream and derivative-distribution policy
justification: Beta-stage spins: rebranding, unofficial builds and use of the official package repository. Follows the V3 trademark Decision.

title: Track external-contributor and native-package ecosystem metrics
justification: V4 exit thresholds (100 external packages, 25 contributors) need a published GOV metric, not only REL store counts.

title: Publish feature-freeze and RC soak governance for the beta
justification: V4 exit: feature freeze at RC1, RC soak cycles, P0 restarts the cycle. Extends V0 gate governance to freeze and soak rules.

title: File the EAR encryption-source notice and classification
justification: Public binary distribution of cryptography from or through the US. File EAR 742.15(b) and document classification for FDE and TLS releases.

title: Publish the GPL corresponding-source written-offer policy
justification: Workstreams.md GPL boundary. REL publishes corresponding source (GAP-0013/0374); GOV states the written-offer policy the installer About view (INS GAP-0014) must surface.

title: Publish issue triage labels, severity, templates and stale policy
justification: GAP-0386 requires the policy before public alpha. Define at V1 (generation ID, hardware/personality tags, response targets) so V3 community infra only staffs it.

title: Document kernel-fork maintenance staffing and process
justification: §56.4 standing cost, encoded as an invariant at V0; the actual staffing/process document is due before Phase D and at the first V1 upstream rebase.

title: Adopt maintainer succession, key escrow and bus-factor plan
justification: Public alpha must survive loss of any maintainer: admin access, key escrow and workstream continuity.

title: Open the 2.0 planning RFC listing deferred LATER items
justification: 1.0 exit: 2.0 planning RFC opened listing explicitly deferred items (ARM64, native FS/GPU, distributed interfaces, casting). Cites LATER via See also without depending.

title: Publish the privacy policy for crash reports, HCL submissions and telemetry
justification: GDPR data-handling design for crash reporting, Hardware Compatibility List submissions and telemetry. GOV owns the policy; INS/REL implement.

title: Publish the public governance, license and trademark bundle
justification: V3 exit: governance document, license and trademark policy published. Packages already-accepted V0–V3 Decisions into the public site.

title: Register domains, namespaces and handles under the entity
justification: Domains, package-repo namespace, forge org and social handles held by the legal entity, not an individual. Depends on adr-legal-entity. Blocks V3 public alpha identity.

title: Publish package repository developer agreement and intermediary terms
justification: Developer agreement, content policy, malware-removal and DMCA notice/counter-notice are legal intermediary duties. docs-developer-program is V4 onboarding; REL implements the repo those terms govern. No existing GOV slug for these duties.

title: Populate the repository-alias register from the hosting Decision
justification: registers/repos.md aliases are owned by GOV. After adr-code-hosting, replace placeholder URLs so Evidence lines resolve.

title: Publish the research-programme index that every ADR must cite
justification: Workstreams.md: GOV tracks the §58 research programme. DOC writes the studies (INV-1151 reassigned); this index is what ADR templates require. Non-gating V0.5 per critique ordering of research.

title: Publish RFC templates and the discussion venue for contributors
justification: GAP-0056 defined the process at V0; V1 opens to external developers with SDK v1. Templates and venue must exist before the V3 five-RFC gate.

title: Exercise the RFC process through five external RFCs to Decision
justification: V3 exit: public RFC process has processed at least five external RFCs to Decision. Gate-verifying, not a new process.

title: Record GOV roles in security-response and advisory sign-off
justification: V3 scope names GOV beside REL/KRN for security response. REL GAP-0239 owns the process; GOV names who may sign advisories and speak as the entity.

title: Define governance roles for root signing-key custody
justification: REL GAP-0045 owns ceremony and HSM; GOV names which governance roles hold quorum shares for Secure Boot and repository signing at public alpha.

title: Publish the 1.0 stability contract, support lifecycle and UX bar
justification: The 1.0 promise: frozen ABIs, breaking-change definition, 24-month support, CVE SLA, each §70 pillar mapped to a workstream with exit criteria, and compatibility UX proving Linux and Windows software feel native (§49).

title: Draft support window, CVE SLA, HCL and ABI-stability policy
justification: V4 exit: support window, CVE SLA, HCL tiers, ABI stability statement drafted, RFC-reviewed and accepted. REL GAP-0062 owns lifecycle mechanics; ABI drafts the stability statement; GOV owns the published contract drafts.

title: Define rules for third-party marks in compatibility claims
justification: Pulled from V3 to V2: Windows, Steam, Proton and related marks first appear in public V2 W1/gaming gates. Trademark usage policy for derivatives stays V3.

title: Run trademark clearance and register word and logo marks
justification: Clearance and filing before any public release. V1 is the last rung before V2 desktop preview names the product in public.

title: Publish the userspace dependency license allowlist
justification: Pulled from V1 to V0.5 because the first immutable packages land then. Excludes AGPL, SSPL, BUSL and similar from the default image and SDK tree. BLD enforces the list in CI.

title: Author the V0.5 milestone gates mapping the application model
justification: Gate-verifying docs: every §60 item in the V0.5 file, including four demo native apps from immutable packages on the native compositor.

title: Author the V1 milestone gates including self-hosting and dogfooding
justification: Gate-verifying docs: every §61 item, self-hosting, internal daily-driving metrics, and ecosystem criteria on every V1+ gate (INV-1102).

title: Author the V2 milestone gates mapping the desktop preview
justification: Gate-verifying docs: every §62 item in the V2 milestone file.

title: Author the V3 milestone gates and audience-specific messaging
justification: Gate-verifying docs: every §63 item, written for enthusiasts, developers, OS researchers and experimenting gamers.

title: Define V4 beta and 1.0 stable criteria the baseline omitted
justification: §63 left V4/1.0 unspecified. Write SLOs, audit, ABI freeze, support commitment, hardware list and compatibility pass rates into the V4 and 1.0 milestone files, citing B-IDs and C-IDs only.

title: Publish vendor influence and conflict-of-interest policy
justification: Hardware vendors, game platforms and sponsors at public alpha. Target-hardware selection and gaming partnerships are capture risks.

title: Publish vendor NDA policy for hardware documentation
justification: Vendor NDA policy (what may be read versus reproduced) is legal/governance; no existing GOV NDA slug. HW consumes the policy when writing drivers. Distinct from docs-vendor-conflict-policy (influence/COI).

title: Complete the Wine, DXVK and VKD3D-Proton license review
justification: LGPL Wine and related Windows-personality components before W1 gates. WIN owns clean-room and upstream-first policy; GOV records the license review. PKG owns LGPL relinking.

title: Encode standing invariants and non-goals as linted register rules
justification: Critique: collapse nongoals and invariants into lint/register tasks, not one task each. Populate I-IDs for §1/§2/§3/§53/§54/§56.5/§57/§66/§67/§69 rules (not a distro or DE, mechanism-versus-semantics, personality firewall, no fake speedups, ecosystem gates from V1, ideas stay in Layer 3/4) and enforce them on ADRs and public material.

title: Compare legal-entity jurisdictions for export, GDPR and tax
justification: Question answered before adr-legal-entity: export controls, GDPR, trademark cost and donation tax treatment. Jurisdiction is expensive to change.

title: Define GPUDispatch cancellation after work is submitted to the GPU
justification: V2 GPU path must state what the caller observes when an in-flight GPUDispatch is cancelled after GPU submit, so Operation cancellation remains uniform without pretending hardware abort always succeeds.

title: Decide GPU ComputeDevice backend among Vulkan, DRM, or deferral
justification: Must precede V2 GPU ComputeDevice implementation. Pulled from inventory V2 to V1 so the V2 dispatch gate is not blocked on an undecided backend. Defer-after-1.0 remains an option but conflicts with the V2 Throughput-on-GPU exit criterion.

title: Decide portable workload representation for heterogeneous dispatch
justification: Must precede compute.dispatch. Pulled from inventory V2 to V1. Options: SPIR-V, Wasm, native kernels per device, or a multi-format envelope. Wasm as the only native machine ABI is rejected per §57.

title: Ship ComputeDevice Layer 1 conformance tests for the ABI freeze
justification: V4 freezes Layer 1: every ComputeDevice, ComputeQueue, and GPUDispatch entry point needs a conformance test. No L1 freeze is scheduled before this rung.

title: Define NPU ComputeDevice class with one reference hardware backend
justification: V3 expands ComputeDevice beyond CPU/GPU with at least one NPU backend on target hardware, proving the open-ended class id does not require an ABI break.

title: Define DSP FPGA and accelerator ComputeDevice classes without backends
justification: §37 requires DSP, FPGA, and generic accelerator classes as interface definitions with backends optional before 1.0, so the taxonomy stays open without shipping unused drivers.

title: Route Throughput to GPU and LowLatency to CPU in the V2 demo
justification: V2 exit criterion: a sample workload with preference Throughput runs on the GPU and LowLatency on the CPU, and os inspect shows the ComputeQueue.

title: Dispatch a sample workload on the CPU ComputeDevice
justification: V1 ABI reservation must be callable, not a type-only stub. A CPU ComputeQueue submit/complete path proves GPUDispatch exists before the V2 GPU signal path.

title: Publish Layer 1 reference pages for ComputeDevice and ComputeQueue
justification: V3 documentation gate requires 100 percent of Layer 1 ABI entry points to have reference pages, including ComputeDevice, ComputeQueue, and GPUDispatch.

title: Enumerate NVIDIA GPU as a ComputeDevice on the V3 desktop
justification: V3 hardware scope adds a gated NVIDIA desktop. ComputeDevice enumeration and dispatch must work on that GPU using the V1 backend decision, not a native NVIDIA driver rewrite.

title: Encode ComputeDevice dispatch preferences for workload placement
justification: Collapses the six §37 preference axes (latency, throughput, energy, precision, memory, locality) into one schema used by compute.dispatch and the placement service.

title: Decide ComputeDevice enumeration ABI and open-ended class taxonomy
justification: V0 scope-in is only the ComputeDevice enumeration ADR. Collapses topology, CPU-only, open-ended taxonomy, unfixed CPU/GPU split, NPU, novel-arch, and Principle 9 invariants into one decision with options: closed class enum versus extensible class id; CPU as ComputeDevice versus CPU-as-scheduler-only; hide versus expose placement cost.

title: Expose ComputeDevice locality and cost through inspect data
justification: Principle 9 and the V0 enumeration ADR require abstractions to expose locality and cost rather than hiding them. OBS owns the inspect command; this task emits the per-device records.

title: Expose the GPU as a ComputeDevice on the chosen backend
justification: V2 gate requires GPU dispatch. Uses retained DRM/Mesa or Vulkan compute per the V1 backend ADR; does not rewrite a native GPU driver stack.

title: Fuzz GPUDispatch submission and preference decoding without panic
justification: V3 continuous fuzzing of the native syscall surface must include GPUDispatch submit and preference blobs so a public alpha does not ship an unfuzzed L1 object.

title: Gate ComputeDevice access behind Capability with no ambient path
justification: No-ambient-authority applies as soon as a CPU ComputeDevice exists, so this is pulled from inventory V2 to V1. Dispatch without Capability<ComputeDevice> returns Error::Rights and allocates no handle.

title: Implement compute.dispatch as an asynchronous Operation
justification: User-facing §37 compute.dispatch(workload, preference) submits an Operation that placement routes to a ComputeQueue. Kernel GPUDispatch is the submit/complete primitive.

title: Implement ComputeQueue as a typed submission Object
justification: Object<ComputeQueue> is the submission queue of a ComputeDevice. CPU queues land at V1 with the device ABI; GPU queues bind at V2. GFX RenderQueue remains GFX.

title: Implement ComputeDevice kernel ABI with CPU as first class
justification: V1 must reserve the Layer 1 ComputeDevice object so later GPU/NPU classes do not break the ABI. CPU is the first enumerable class; taxonomy stays open-ended per the V0 ADR.

title: Implement optional DSP and FPGA ComputeDevice backends
justification: V3 ships DSP and FPGA as interface-only classes with backends optional before 1.0. Real backends are parked on LATER so they can return without living as fake 1.0 work.

title: Place workloads on a ComputeDevice from requirements and preferences
justification: Layer 2 placement service selects CPU versus GPU from encoded preferences. Kernel ABI stays device and queue objects; unmatched workloads fail closed with a typed error.

title: Integrate dispatch preferences with scheduler intent and frequency
justification: Throughput, LowLatency, and EnergyEfficient dispatch must influence device choice and frequency selection via SCH intent. SCH owns GPU-queue priority; this is the HET side of the bridge.

title: Lock the Layer 2 dispatch preference schema for the 1.x line
justification: V4 locks Layer 2 interface versions for 1.x. Dispatch preference records and the placement-service interface are L2 and must pass old-client/new-service negotiation.

title: Measure ComputeDevice dispatch overhead against Vulkan and Rayon
justification: Harness for B-048 (bench:compute-dispatch). V2 target is publish-only; later rungs use the same harness for regression bands.

title: Prototype Vulkan compute versus DRM job submission on AMD
justification: Critique freeze-before-spike: GAP-0553 and the V2 GPU ComputeDevice gate need a measured prototype on the reference AMD GPU before the backend ADR is accepted. Does not build a native GPU driver stack.

title: Publish B-048 ComputeDevice dispatch results on every Tier 1 machine
justification: 1.0 re-runs every tracked benchmark on Tier 1. B-048 target is regression versus V4 using the V2 harness; no superiority claim without the published table.

title: Decide how ComputeDevice relates to ComputeQueue
justification: Answers whether a ComputeQueue is derived from a ComputeDevice Capability and who owns scheduling, before Object<ComputeQueue> and GPU backends land. Options: queue derived from device; independent queue objects; GFX ComputeQueue as the GPU device with CPU having no queue.

title: Review ComputeDevice against CXL unified memory NPU and CHERI
justification: Workstream scope and the 1.0 fossilization review require checking ComputeDevice against x86-64, coherent memory, and discrete-GPU assumptions (CXL, unified CPU/GPU memory, NPUs, CHERI) without claiming hardware capability enforcement.

title: Complete GPUDispatch when the GPU signals queue completion
justification: Inventory placed GPUDispatch at V0.5, but V0.5 has no HET gate and compositor GPU work is GFX RenderQueue. Earliest gate is V2 ComputeDevice dispatch; this is the GPU-signal completion path onto ComputeQueue.

title: Survey heterogeneous dispatch models before the ComputeDevice API
justification: Critique requires L1 spikes in V0 and freeze-before-spike forbids committing the ComputeDevice API without this survey of SYCL/oneAPI, CUDA graphs, Vulkan compute, Metal, Level Zero, and ONNX Runtime EPs.

title: Publish Bluetooth pairing time and audio latency on target machines
justification: V2 benchmark gate: Bluetooth audio latency and pairing time measured and published on the three target machines. Numbers live in the BEN register; this harness produces the reports. No superiority claim.

title: Publish user-space versus in-kernel driver latency and throughput
justification: INV-1057 measured performance parity for a migrated class. Harness compares the Bluetooth or USB HID user-space driver to the inherited in-kernel path on the same Reference machine; BEN owns the register target.

title: Run the Bluetooth host as a restartable user-space Component
justification: §33/§55: migrate the Bluetooth host to user-space where the spike showed acceptable cost, demonstrating one inherited class moved with measured parity (bench-userspace-driver). V2 exit: user-space Bluetooth crash recovers without reboot.

title: Grant Capability<BluetoothDevice> from a pairing agent and chooser
justification: BLE scanning is a location-tracking vector. Apps receive per-device Capabilities, never adapter-wide scan authority. APP/UIP render the chooser; HW owns pairing, bonding and the Capability. Covers pairing UI in INV-1217.

title: Ship A2DP, HFP, HID, GATT, BLE privacy and file-transfer profiles
justification: V2 laptop day demo: headset A2DP/HFP, mouse and keyboard HID, file transfer. LE Audio/LC3 is included where hardware supports it; BLE privacy is on by default. AUD owns audio rendering; HW owns the host profiles.

title: Restart the Bluetooth service with paired devices reconnecting
justification: §32 Bluetooth service restartable; V2 exit tests stack crash recovery without reboot. Paired headsets, mice and keyboards reconnect after supervisor restart.

title: Bring up the V0 AMD desktop Reference machine to a booting kernel
justification: V0 hardware scope and exit: the fork boots on QEMU and one designated AMD desktop from a CI-built image. LAB racks the machine; HW records SKU, firmware, IOMMU/TPM/Secure Boot posture from decide-target-hardware and a passing boot log.

title: Bring up the AMD laptop Reference machine including amdgpu
justification: V2 hardware scope: named AMD laptop (Zen 4-class APU, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth). Completes INV-1061 laptop GPU support. Lid, touchpad, BT and firmware quirks are the V2 HW risk the ladder names.

title: Bring up one additional Intel laptop and one additional AMD laptop
justification: V3 Tier 1 is six machines: three V2 targets plus NVIDIA desktop plus one extra laptop per vendor. HW bring-up of the two new SKUs onto the same HID/GPU/USB/firmware matrix.

title: Bring up the Tier 1 Intel desktop Reference machine
justification: V4 hardware scope: at least 10 named machines including one Intel desktop. SKU recorded in the hardware register; HID, GPU, USB, firmware and HCL row required before RC soak.

title: Bring up the V1 Intel laptop Reference machine for daily-driving
justification: V1 hardware scope: designated Intel laptop (iGPU, Intel Wi-Fi, NVMe, internal plus one USB-C display). Critique: laptop procurement is LAB at V0.5; HW bring-up must exist before Wi-Fi/audio/suspend gates that PWR/NET/AUD own.

title: Bring up second-generation AMD and Intel laptops and a second AMD GPU
justification: V4: AMD desktops at least two GPU generations, Intel laptops two generations, AMD laptops two. Completes the ten-machine Tier 1 floor with SKUs, firmware matrix and suite green.

title: Decide Bluetooth host placement and required profiles
justification: V2 Bluetooth gate depends on this adr, fed by spike-userspace-bluetooth. Options: retain BlueZ in-kernel/host, move the host to a native Component per §33, or a hybrid. Profiles: A2DP, HFP, HID, LE Audio/LC3, GATT, BLE privacy.

title: Decide user-space driver access: VFIO, UIO or native Device DMA
justification: INV-0623 must precede the V1 user-space driver framework. Options: reuse VFIO/UIO-style interfaces, a native Device Capability with IOMMU-protected MemoryObject DMA, or a hybrid. Fed by spike-usb-hid-driver.

title: Decide criteria classifying each driver as inherited, native or rewritten
justification: Merges the two §33/§55 classification adrs: latency, DMA safety, interrupt performance, isolation value, inherited-driver compatibility and maintenance cost. Options per class: keep in-kernel, move to user-space, or rewrite in-kernel. Feeds the driver status registry.

title: Decide pragmatic driver residency over microkernel purity
justification: Collapses the §33/§55/§57 nongoals and invariants: no microkernel purity, hardware support wins when it conflicts with native work, and driver transition is incremental per class with no flag-day. Options: all-userspace, kernel-only, and pragmatic residency by measured cost.

title: Decide Capability<InputDevice> rights with no ambient device nodes
justification: EXTRA-042 and §9: native apps must not receive ambient HID streams. Options: per-seat focused-surface only, per-device Capability with attenuable grab rights, or a privileged input broker. Must precede input-hid-service consumers in UIP.

title: Decide whether IOMMU is required for user-space drivers and DMA
justification: Without IOMMU a user-space driver can DMA over the kernel. Options: hard requirement on all target hardware, required only for user-space DMA drivers, or software-only isolation with documented degradation. Target SKUs already require IOMMU via GAP-0211.

title: Decide NVIDIA support and Secure Boot handling of proprietary modules
justification: Critique places the NVIDIA adr at V1 so V2 experimental and V3 Tier 1 bring-up are not research. Options: open modules plus NVK, vendor-signed proprietary module, machine-owner MOK signing, or defer past 1.0. Coordinates with KRN module-signing and GFX compositor stance.

title: Decide driverless-first native printing with PDF spool and CUPS in LNX
justification: Must precede the V3 print service. Options: IPP Everywhere/driverless native service with PDF spool, CUPS as the native service, or CUPS only inside the Linux personality for legacy drivers. Print job is a typed Operation; APP owns the dialog chrome.

title: Decide 1.0 sensor support per device class in or out of scope
justification: Critique missing requirement 36: ambient-light auto-brightness, lid and tablet-mode switches, accelerometer rotation declared in or out per device class. Options: all three in, lid-only, or lid plus ALS. Convertible UI remains UIP non-goal.

title: Decide Hardware Compatibility List tiers and promotion criteria
justification: Public vocabulary for tested-in-lab, community-reported and unsupported, plus promotion rules into Tier 1. Options: two tiers, three tiers, or lab-only until 1.0. Feeds publish-known-good-list and the V3 installer verdict.

title: Decide the V1 through V2 Reference machine list and security criteria
justification: GAP-0550 requires the AMD desktop, Intel laptop and AMD laptop SKUs before hardware-dependent spikes. Records x86-64-only, constrained rather than universal PC compatibility, and Secure Boot key enrolment, TPM 2.0 and IOMMU as selection criteria. V0 hardware scope names the AMD desktop this adr designates.

title: Decide policy for third-party user-space drivers and firmware packages
justification: Vendors and community porters need a channel without forking the OS. Options: signed Packages with review and revocation, in-tree only, or unrestricted user-space loaders. How they appear in the Hardware Compatibility List is part of the decision.

title: Decide public vendor priorities for purchase guidance
justification: Honest guidance (AMD graphics first, Intel/MediaTek Wi-Fi, NVIDIA/Broadcom best-effort, or an alternative ranking) before public alpha. Prevents a wave of unsupported-hardware reports. Distinct from SKU selection at V0.

title: Define Object<Device> and mint Capability<Device> from enumeration
justification: §7 Object<Device> is the hardware handle the V0.5 input path and later user-space drivers hold. Surface stays prototyped; depends on spike-device-capability. No ambient device-node grant.

title: Enumerate PCI, USB and ACPI devices into Object<Device> handles
justification: Native device discovery over retained Linux buses so Object<Device> exists for the compositor input path and later drivers. Preserves §2 hardware discovery; does not replace sysfs for the Linux personality.

title: Bridge native Device objects to inherited Linux drivers
justification: §69 hardware abstraction: native Object<Device> over retained in-kernel drivers so native software never opens DRM/USB/HID nodes. Personality software keeps the inherited nodes. Required before GPU-accelerated Linux apps at V1 share hardware with native Components.

title: Lint-forbid flag-day replacement of any inherited driver class
justification: INV-1055 as a CI lint: a change that removes an inherited driver class without an accepted classification adr and a dual-path period is rejected. Enforces decide-driver-pragmatism on every merge.

title: Publish the driver status registry of class and test coverage per device
justification: INV-1058: each supported device records inherited-Linux, userspace-native or rewritten, plus test coverage. Feeds the Hardware Compatibility List and decide-driver-class-criteria outcomes. Regenerated in CI from the three-class model.

title: Enable amdgpu on the AMD desktop Reference machine for composition
justification: V0.5 compositor drives the reference GPU via DRM/KMS. HW bring-up of amdgpu plus RADV/RadeonSI on the designated AMD desktop; GFX owns compositor abstractions. Laptop half of INV-1061 waits for bringup-amd-laptop.

title: Enable i915/xe and ANV/Iris on the Intel laptop Reference machine
justification: V1 hardware scope and GPU-accelerated Linux browser/IDE gate need excellent Intel GPU support on the designated laptop. GFX owns compositor/Mesa mediation; HW owns kernel driver bring-up and a passing acceleration check.

title: Enable basic touchscreen and pen digitizer as InputDevice Capabilities
justification: UIP requires pointer, touch and pen at V0.5 protocol level and ships basic touchscreen at 1.0 while on-screen keyboard stays out. HW enablement of USB/I2C touch and Wacom-class pens on target laptops that include them.

title: Enable fingerprint readers as Device objects for the identity service
justification: SEC greeter adds fingerprint login at V3; GAP-0468 lists fingerprint readers in purchase guidance. HW enables USB/SPI fingerprint devices behind Capability<Device>; SEC owns matching. Out of scope if the SKU has no reader.

title: Audit linux-firmware blobs and set ship, download-on-demand or exclude
justification: Pulled from V2 to V1 because daily-drive images ship firmware. Per-blob redistribution terms: ship in the image, download-on-demand, or exclude. GOV licence scanning (GAP-0155) is the CI net; this is the HW policy for target machines.

title: Ship an LVFS firmware update service recorded in SystemGeneration history
justification: Incoming from BOOT plus HW firmware items: fwupd/LVFS-class updates for UEFI, microcode, SSDs, docks and peripherals, each recorded as a history event with explicit rollback limits. BOOT keeps ESP capsule staging and PCR re-seal; PKG records the history event.

title: Ship a user-runnable hardware conformance tool with consented upload
justification: Public alpha meets hardware the lab never will. Executes the compatibility suite on an arbitrary machine and submits anonymised, consented results. Distinct from the pre-install checker: this is post-install conformance.

title: Sign off hardware soak: no P0 driver or firmware regression on Tier 1
justification: 1.0 risk: last-minute driver or firmware refreshes regress hardware tests during the 30-day soak. Written sign-off that the soak fleet matches published HCL firmware versions and has zero open P0/P1 hardware defects.

title: Ingest community Hardware Compatibility List probes for 100 machines
justification: V3 exit: database has all Tier 1 machines and at least 100 community-submitted machines with probe data. HW owns validation against hcl-schema and hcl-submission-privacy; REL hosts the store.

title: Ship a live-image Hardware Compatibility List checker for PCI USB ACPI
justification: V3 installer compatibility verdict and probe-from-live-image. Inventories PCI, USB, ACPI and firmware identifiers and reports against the database. INS embeds it; HW owns the probe and verdict logic.

title: Ship a host-side Hardware Compatibility List probe for foreign OSes
justification: GAP-0470 also requires a probe that runs on a Windows or Linux host before wiping a disk. Same schema as hcl-compat-checker; output is a file the installer and website can score.

title: Define the Hardware Compatibility List schema and probe record format
justification: V3 public HCL needs a schema before community ingest. Records PCI/USB/DMI identifiers, per-generation status, known issues, workarounds and provenance. REL publishes; HW owns the schema the probe tools emit.

title: Make Hardware Compatibility List submissions opt-in, redacted and reviewable
justification: Invariant: submissions are opt-in, pseudonymous, user-reviewable, no serials or network identifiers. Binding on hcl-compat-checker, hardware-conformance-tool and REL ingest.

title: Automate Tier 2 to Tier 1 promotion from probe data and suite results
justification: V4 scope: Tier 2 process mature with a documented promotion path. Implements decide-support-tiers criteria against community probes plus a lab suite run, without silently claiming Tier 1.

title: Enable iGPU plus dGPU mux and render-offload on hybrid laptops
justification: Critique missing requirement 25 (GFX/HW): hybrid-graphics laptops across compositor and personalities. GFX owns scanout/offload; HW owns ACPI mux, power-well and Device enumeration of both GPUs on machines that have them.

title: Enumerate gamepads as Capability<InputDevice> for native and personalities
justification: V2 gaming proof-of-concept and W1 integration require gamepad input. HW mints HID gamepad Capabilities; WIN/LNX consume them. No ambient /dev/input for native software.

title: Build the HID input service minting Capability<InputDevice>
justification: V0.5 exit: a native application receives keyboard and mouse. EXTRA-042 assigns libinput/evdev/HID device enablement to HW and routing to UIP. Native software never sees /dev/input; the Linux personality keeps evdev.

title: Re-issue InputDevice Capabilities on HID hot-plug and unplug
justification: V0.5 keyboard and mouse must survive unplug/replug without restarting the compositor. Device-management restart of INV-0598 is V1; this is the input-only hot-plug path the four demo apps need.

title: Enable I2C HID touchpads on the Intel laptop Reference machine
justification: V1 daily-driving on the Intel laptop fails without the internal touchpad. HID-over-I2C is the usual laptop path; pointer events go through input-hid-service. Gestures wait for V2 touchpad-gestures.

title: Define and test user-space driver degradation when IOMMU is absent
justification: GAP-0536 requires explicit degradation on systems without IOMMU. Target hardware has IOMMU; this task records the refuse-or-kernel-only behaviour and a test that user-space DMA is not enabled when the IOMMU is off.

title: Implement IOMMU-protected DMA MemoryObjects for user-space drivers
justification: §17 DMA-suitable MemoryObjects are unsafe against malicious peripherals without IOMMU. Implements the chosen access path so a user-space driver can DMA only into MemoryObjects it holds. MEM owns MemoryObject properties; HW wires Device to the IOMMU domain.

title: Implement XKB-data keyboard layouts, compose, dead keys and switching
justification: V1 daily-driving needs non-US layouts from day one. EXTRA-042 places layout data in HW; UIP routes keys; APP owns the shell switcher UI. Reuses xkeyboard-config; per-window versus global policy is configured here and consumed by UIP.

title: Expose laptop function keys, keyboard backlight and brightness
justification: §62 laptop support: function keys, keyboard backlight and display brightness as typed settings. Thermal and frequency stay in PWR (reassigned GAP-0313). First hardware check reviewers make on the two V2 laptops.

title: Deliver lid and tablet-mode switch events as typed Device signals
justification: §62 lid events on reference laptops. GFX lock-on-lid and PWR suspend consume these signals; HW owns ACPI/HID switch enablement. Tablet-mode follows decide-sensor-scope; convertible UI stays out.

title: Support MTP and PTP phone-to-desktop transfer for Android and iOS
justification: Photo import is a top desktop task at public alpha. USB MTP/PTP as a user-space Component granting UserSelected files, not ambient phone filesystem access.

title: Bring up an experimental NVIDIA desktop on the decided driver path
justification: V2 tracks one NVIDIA desktop as experimental with no gate. Exercises decide-nvidia-approach so V3 Tier 1 is not the first boot. Documented supported generations start here.

title: Bring up the Tier 1 NVIDIA desktop on the decided driver and Secure Boot path
justification: V3 hardware scope adds one NVIDIA desktop, proprietary or open path decided by decide-nvidia-approach, fully tested each release. Completes INV-1064 with documented generations and a passing Secure Boot module load.

title: Park NFC, WWAN and eSIM hardware enablement after 1.0
justification: Critique missing requirement 37: NFC, WWAN/eSIM declared LATER so they appear in the 1.0 non-goal list. Casting and MIDI are APP/AUD; this task parks the radio and NFC Device classes only.

title: Ship driverless print discovery and Capability<PrintJob> for a single job
justification: V3 printing scope. IPP Everywhere/AirPrint, USB, WSD and SMB-shared printers via mDNS; printer drivers as user-space Components; OS-owned discovery grants Capability<PrintJob> like the file chooser. APP owns dialog chrome; LNX owns the CUPS socket.

title: Restart the printing service with queued jobs preserved
justification: §32 printing service restartable with queued jobs preserved. Supervisor restart must not drop an in-flight IPP job on Tier 1 machines.

title: Publish the 1.0 Hardware Compatibility List and per-machine lab results
justification: 1.0 scope and exit: final HCL publication with Tier 1 at least 10 named x86-64 machines and Tier 2 community, plus test-lab results per Tier 1 machine. REL hosts; HW authors the content from the database.

title: Publish the tiered known-good hardware list from the compatibility database
justification: §62 constrained target hardware communicated as reference, supported and community-reported, with GPU/Wi-Fi/fingerprint/dock guidance. Regenerated from the database each release. Does not promise universal PC compatibility.

title: Inventory retained Linux buses, firmware load and input in the fork
justification: Critique: retain-Linux items collapse into at most two tasks. This inventory lists PCIe, USB, ACPI, input, Bluetooth, firmware loading, power-management hooks and hardware discovery as inherited, feeding KRN's retained-mechanism list. No driver class is replaced here.

title: Gate retained PCIe, USB, ACPI and input regressions on the AMD desktop
justification: Second of the two retain tasks: kselftest and boot-time enumeration checks for the inventoried buses on QEMU and the AMD Reference machine. A native feature that regresses a retained driver is rejected. Bluetooth and laptop power are presence checks until later rungs.

title: Ship eSCL/WSD and SANE scanning with Capability<Scanner> via a system dialog
justification: V4 hardware test suite lists scanning. Driverless eSCL/WSD plus SANE backends; Capability<Scanner> from an OS dialog. First-party scanner app is APP; this task is the service and dialog grant.

title: Enable SD and MMC readers as Capability-gated removable storage
justification: Common laptop hardware at public alpha. Same authority model as usb-mass-storage: Device enumeration in HW, UserSelected volume in STO.

title: Implement in-scope sensor classes as user-space Components
justification: §33 sensor drivers as user-space Components for the classes decide-sensor-scope includes. Typed settings for ALS and orientation; PWR consumes ALS for brightness. Out-of-scope classes are documented, not stubbed as native APIs.

title: Enable CCID smartcard readers as Device objects for authentication
justification: APP/SEC lock screen lists smartcard authentication. HW enables USB CCID readers as Capability<Device>; SEC owns PIN and certificate use. No ambient PC/SC for native apps.

title: Spike Object<Device> as a Layer 1 Capability-gated hardware handle
justification: Critique freeze-before-spike: Object<Device> is Layer 1, so the spike lands in V0, implementation is prototyped at V0.5, and freeze waits until V4. Explores handle shape, rights and IOMMU placement before define-device-object.

title: Evaluate remaining peripheral classes for user-space driver residency
justification: §33 remaining classes: input already moved, cameras/UVC, storage bridges. Report per class against decide-driver-class-criteria so V3 USB mass storage, webcams and MTP are scheduled as inherited or user-space, not by default.

title: Spike a USB HID user-space driver against the in-kernel path
justification: §33 requires a measured prototype of one USB HID or USB audio user-space driver versus the inherited in-kernel driver before the access-mechanism adr and V1 framework. Report interrupt latency and throughput; no numeric target in prose.

title: Spike a Bluetooth controller in user space versus the in-kernel host
justification: GAP-0537 plus §33: measure interrupt latency and throughput of one Bluetooth controller in user space (VFIO or Device Capability) against the in-kernel host before the V2 Bluetooth stack adr. USB HID half already covered by spike-usb-hid-driver.

title: Implement signed third-party driver and firmware Packages with revocation
justification: Implements decide-third-party-drivers: review, signing, revocation and HCL rows for out-of-tree user-space drivers. PKG/REL own the repository; HW owns Device matching and the compatibility-database fields.

title: Document the three coexisting driver classes and per-class residency
justification: §55 long-term model: inherited Linux drivers, userspace native drivers and selected rewritten in-kernel drivers coexist. Writes the residency map from decide-driver-class-criteria into the driver status registry for V2 target machines.

title: Require IOMMU and authorize Thunderbolt, USB4 and USB devices before DMA
justification: GAP-0210: IOMMU on, all DMA devices behind it, bolt-style Thunderbolt/USB4 authorization before PCIe tunnelling. Extends the same authorization to USB DMA devices so docks at V2 cannot DMA until the user allows them.

title: Run the full hardware suite on every Tier 1 machine each release candidate
justification: V4 exit: every Tier 1 machine passes display hot-plug, suspend/resume cycles, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, audio, camera, USB classes and printing each RC. HW owns the combined suite and per-machine report; PWR/NET/AUD/GFX/MED supply their cases.

title: Enable multi-finger touchpad gestures on the reference laptops
justification: §62 touchpad gestures; UIP GAP-0287 ships basic gestures while on-screen keyboard stays out. HW produces gesture events from the I2C HID device; UIP routes them to focused surfaces.

title: Enable USB-C docks: USB, Ethernet, HID and DisplayPort tunnels
justification: V2 laptop day demo plugs an external display via USB-C. GFX owns MST/hot-plug; HW enables dock USB hubs, NIC, HID and DP-alt-mode Device objects, gated on thunderbolt-usb-auth.

title: Enable common USB classes on Tier 1 and record them in the driver registry
justification: V3 scope: common USB classes beyond HID and mass storage (CDC, hub, serial, audio pass-through to AUD). Per-class residency follows spike-remaining-peripherals. Each class is an entry in the driver status registry.

title: Expose USB mass-storage volumes through Capability-gated storage
justification: V3 scope: USB mass storage and common USB classes. HW enumerates the device; STO mounts with UserSelected authority so apps do not receive ambient removable-volume access.

title: Build the user-space driver framework over Capability<Device>
justification: §33/§55 framework: Object<Device> Capabilities, interrupt delivery as Operation completions, and DMA-capable MemoryObjects. Drivers live outside the kernel where decide-driver-class-criteria says the cost is acceptable. Depends on decide-device-access and decide-iommu-requirement.

title: Restart crashed user-space drivers and re-issue Device Capabilities
justification: §32 device-management services are restartable; §33 isolates driver Component crashes under SVC supervision and re-issues Capabilities to holders. V1 daily-driving must not reboot for a USB HID driver panic.

title: Ship selected USB HID classes as user-space drivers
justification: INV-0615: selected USB classes move to user-space where the spike showed acceptable cost. First class is HID (keyboard, mouse) on the Intel laptop, using the V1 framework. Remaining USB classes wait for usb-class-matrix at V3.

title: Verify headset, mouse and keyboard pairing cycles on target laptops
justification: V2 exit: pairing and reconnect of a headset (A2DP and HFP), a mouse and a keyboard succeed in 95 of 100 automated cycles. LAB supplies peer devices; HW owns the scenario scripts.

title: Verify every listed Tier 1 feature on the 1.0 release candidate
justification: 1.0 hardware coverage: every listed feature works on each Tier 1 machine, including suspend/resume, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, external displays and HDR/VRR where the hardware supports it. Runs tier1-hardware-test-suite as a release gate.

title: Verify keyboard, touchpad and USB HID on the Intel laptop Reference machine
justification: V1 daily-driving gate: core team uses the Intel laptop as primary machine. Scripted HID scenarios (internal keyboard, I2C touchpad, USB mouse) must pass on that SKU before the milestone closes.

title: Verify driverless printing on every V3 Tier 1 machine
justification: V3 scope includes printing on six Tier 1 machines. Scripted IPP Everywhere job from a native app plus discovery of a USB printer; LNX CUPS path is a separate LNX task.

title: Verify HID, GPU, USB and firmware on the three V2 target machines
justification: V2 hardware scope is exactly three named machines. Gate-verifying matrix: internal/external HID, GPU enumeration, USB hot-plug, lid/brightness, firmware probe. PWR/NET/AUD/GFX own their slices; HW owns the combined per-machine report.

title: Enable UVC webcams as Device objects consumed by the camera service
justification: V3 cameras/webcams. HW enables UVC devices as Object<Device>; MED mints Capability<Camera> and the in-use indicator. Native software never receives ambient V4L2 nodes.

title: Record Wi-Fi and Bluetooth inherited-driver breadth in the compatibility database
justification: V3 scope: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth hardware beyond target machines via inherited Linux drivers and the database. NET owns association; HW owns chipset enablement notes and HCL rows for community adapters.

title: Publish delta update size and automatic rollback time
justification: V3/V4/1.0 gates cite B-035. PKG already benches store-level delta size; INS benches client download size and fault-injected rollback time to the previous greeter.

title: Publish install, first-boot and update-apply times
justification: V3/V4/1.0 benchmark gates cite B-034 (install, first-boot, update-apply) per Tier 1 machine. INS owns the harness; BEN owns the register. Publish-only; no superiority claim.

title: Share Bluetooth pairing keys across dual-boot
justification: GAP-0420: pairing keys shared with co-installed Windows or Linux so peripherals stay paired. HW owns the Bluetooth stack; INS owns the dual-boot import/export during install and recovery.

title: Import browser bookmarks, history, passwords and extensions
justification: GAP-0418: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari profile import into the browser the browser strategy selects. Secrets land in the SEC secrets service, not a world-readable file.

title: Ship a built-in bug reporter bundling traces, inspect output and generation ID
justification: Crash-report client owned by INS; OBS supplies traces; REL owns intake.

title: Ship opt-in crash-report client with secret scrubbing
justification: §63 and TEL split: INS owns the client and consent UI. Opt-in, show-and-redact before submit (REL GAP-0365), no disk keys or unlocked secrets in stored dumps (GAP-0235). OBS owns capture format; REL owns intake; kernel dumps under lockdown stay with SEC.

title: Show crash and telemetry contents and allow redaction before send
justification: Critique TEL split: client, consent, exact-contents preview and redaction are INS.

title: Decide desktop-usable boot-success health criteria
justification: GAP-0342: a generation is marked good only after login, display, network and audio come up, so automatic rollback is not a false success. Distinct from BOOT's boot-counter adr (when the counter may clear). Options: greeter reached; user authenticated; required-service quorum including display/network/audio.

title: Decide installer encryption default with opt-out
justification: GAP-0196: encrypt user data by default with opt-out. First-boot at V2 confirms encryption; the V3 graphical installer enforces the default. Options: default-on with explicit opt-out; default-on with no opt-out on Tier 1; default-off. SEC owns the mechanism, STO the layering.

title: Decide hardware clock UTC versus localtime for dual-boot
justification: GAP-0405: RTC UTC versus local time and time-sync with co-installed Windows. Options: UTC with Windows registry fix documented; localtime to match Windows default; UTC-only with a warning. Applied by the V3 installer.

title: Decide installer disk layout, wipe and dual-boot policy
justification: V3 exit requires an accepted ADR for installer disk layout and encryption. STO already decided GPT layout; this adr chooses wipe-versus-alongside, ESP reuse versus new ESP (BOOT ESP adr), and where recovery lives. Must precede the V3 graphical installer.

title: Decide Linux home adopt-in-place versus copy
