justification: GAP-0413: adopt an existing Linux /home in place for the Linux personality versus copy into native storage. Options: copy-only; adopt-in-place read-write for the personality; adopt read-only with copy into Collections. STO three-view mapping is an input.

title: Decide dual-boot shared data partition format
justification: GAP-0430: recommended dual-boot shared data partition (exFAT versus NTFS) and whether the installer offers to create one. STO owns the drivers; this adr is the installer offer and default. Options: exFAT; NTFS; no shared partition by default.

title: Decide client update orchestration, metered links and deferral
justification: GAP-0341: background download, apply-on-reboot versus live userspace activation, metered-network behaviour and user deferral. Must precede the V3 updater; PKG decide-reboot-free-switch and REL channels are inputs. Options: reboot-only apply; live userspace activation with kernel reboot; defer-until-idle with a deadline.

title: Fetch chunk-level deltas between SystemGenerations
justification: GAP-0333 moved to V3 to match the ladder updater-with-deltas gate (jsonl said V2). Uses PKG delta-object-transfer and REL's V2 delta-size spike; the client downloads only new store objects.

title: Document developer image install, update and rollback
justification: V1 self-hosting: core developers must install, apply a repository update as a new SystemGeneration, and roll back using only committed docs. Public install guides stay with DOC at V3.

title: Publish QEMU and USB developer install media
justification: V1 scope: developers install from a scripted image; daily-driving and self-hosting need signed-enough QEMU and USB media produced from the V0.5 builder, not a graphical installer.

title: Preserve foreign OS, ESP and BitLocker during install
justification: Installer-side coexistence: preserve ESP entries, shrink-and-install-alongside Windows/Linux/Intel-Mac, BitLocker/TPM warning with recovery-key confirmation, refuse read-write on dirty or Fast-Startup hibernated NTFS. BOOT chain-loads; STO owns NTFS policy.

title: Prove full-disk encryption install with Secure Boot on Tier 1
justification: 1.0 exit: installer with full-disk encryption and Secure Boot succeeds on every Tier 1 machine; release-ceremony demo of a signed 1.0 image installed that way.

title: Build first-boot account, encryption and privacy setup
justification: GAP-0237: create administrator account, confirm encryption and save the recovery key, privacy and telemetry choices, Secure Boot status explanation. Runs after scripted or guided image install so V2 preview machines are usable; V3 installer reuses the same flow.

title: Build the guided graphical installer with encryption
justification: §63 and V3 exit: guided installer with disk selection, encryption default-on with opt-out, dual-boot awareness. Native UI, not a POSIX anaconda clone. Encrypt-by-default is an acceptance criterion from decide-encrypt-default.

title: Provide guided scripted image install for preview machines
justification: V2 scope: still image-based install with a guided script, not a public graphical installer. Walks disk selection on the three target machines using the V2 disk-policy adr, then hands off to first-boot.

title: Warn from the Hardware Compatibility List before disk writes
justification: GAP-0370 and V3 exit: installer queries the compatibility database and shows an accurate verdict before writing disks; probe runs from live media. REL/HW own the database; SDK owns the probe tool; INS owns the pre-commit warning.

title: Build the SystemGeneration image builder
justification: Critique and workstreams.md: the image builder is a V0.5 INS task so V0.5 generation-switch demos and V1 developers have a bootable image. Consumes PKG generation compose and STO partition layout; does not invent a native filesystem.

title: Run the unaided public-install usability study
justification: V3 exit: a user without project involvement installs from public media on a Tier 1 machine following only public documentation, moderated study of at least 10 participants with the stated unaided success bar.

title: Make installer and recovery screen-reader accessible and localised
justification: GAP-0474/0475: installer, migration assistant and recovery match desktop languages and are screen-reader accessible from the first screen; inherit keyboard, locale, timezone and hostname from an existing OS when present. ACC owns the reader; TXT owns strings.

title: Automate installer QEMU runs across disk layouts
justification: GAP-0150: automatic installer in QEMU for fresh UEFI, encrypted, dual-boot alongside Windows, existing-data preservation, Secure Boot on and off. Permanent CI matrix for the V3 installer gate.

title: Prove installer success rate on every Tier 1 machine
justification: V3 exit: installer completes on all Tier 1 machines in automated runs with full-disk encryption, success rate at the gate threshold over 200 runs, including the live-installer HCL verdict path.

title: Write the installer and updater threat model
justification: Critique: threat model before public surfaces. Extends SEC's V0 model with install-media tampering, dual-boot ESP attacks, update rollback abuse and crash-report leaks before the V3 installer and crash client ship.

title: Import Linux home directories with per-item destination choice
justification: GAP-0415 plus decide-linux-home: XDG dirs, dotfiles, SSH and GPG keys, git config and shell history, each choosable as Linux personality home versus native application data.

title: Ship a live-boot USB desktop that does not touch disks
justification: GAP-0407: live USB full desktop from removable media without touching internal disks, producing a hardware compatibility report before install. Primary HCL submission path at public alpha.

title: Restore a system history point onto different hardware
justification: GAP-0425: machine-to-machine migration restoring generations, packages, configuration and user data onto different hardware from a backup target. STO EXTRA-036 is the backup counterpart.

title: Ship install-media creation with checksum and signature checks
justification: GAP-0408: media creation for Windows, macOS and Linux hosts (or vetted third-party instructions) with mandatory checksum and signature verification. First adoption step happens on a foreign OS.

title: Record each migration import as a restorable history event
justification: GAP-0422: every migration import is a system history event with a pre-import snapshot undoable via standard restore. PKG owns the log; INS emits the events and refuses import without a snapshot.

title: Show third-party notices and GPL offer in installer and Settings
justification: GAP-0014: About/licenses view in the installer and Settings exposing all license texts and the GPL written offer. REL publishes the notices bundle; INS/APP render it.

title: Support offline install media and local repository mirrors
justification: GAP-0337: air-gapped and lab machines install and update without internet via offline media and local mirrors. REL owns mirror protocol; INS ships media that embeds or points at a verified local repository.

title: Prove power-cut mid-update recovers the previous SystemGeneration
justification: 1.0 demo: pull power during an update on a Tier 1 desktop; the machine boots the previous generation and completes the update on retry. PKG atomic-commit test is the unit; this is the hardware demo.

title: Write public install and recovery procedures for strangers
justification: V3 documentation gate and usability study depend on an install guide, recovery guide and dual-boot/BitLocker warnings authored from INS behaviour; DOC publishes the site.

title: Restore a system whose current SystemGeneration is corrupted
justification: V3 exit: recovery environment restores a system whose current generation is corrupted, tested on every Tier 1 machine. Uses PKG store verify/repair inside the INS recovery generation.

title: Build recovery unlock, restore, reinstall and log collection
justification: §63 recovery: disk unlock, restore any generation or snapshot, reinstall from network or media, collect logs, from the V2 signed recovery generation. STO ships fs repair inside it; SVC owns the last-resort text console.

title: Ship a signed recovery SystemGeneration on the ESP
justification: GAP-0205: a permanently resident signed recovery generation on the ESP that boots without the main store. V2 so V3 recovery UX and the installer have something to install; BOOT integrity-failure UX hands off to it.

title: Expose SystemGeneration restore in Settings and boot UX
justification: §30/§62 and V2 exit: rollback is first-class in Settings and at boot, not emergency tooling. Consumes PKG generation-management-interface and BOOT generation menu; PKG keeps `os restore`. Also surfaces automatic fallback so a fault-injected bad update is visible in Settings (V2 demo).

title: Ship scripted install from a built SystemGeneration image
justification: Critique: scripted install at V0.5/V1 before any end-user installer. A non-interactive install into QEMU (and the reference desktop) from the image builder, leaving user data off the immutable generation tree.

title: Run scripted install on the Intel laptop and AMD desktop
justification: V1 hardware scope and daily-driving gate require the scripted image path on the designated Intel laptop and AMD desktop, not only QEMU.

title: Offer a dual-boot shared data partition at install
justification: Implements decide-shared-partition: the installer can create the recommended shared volume and explain Fast Startup / hibernation limits using the NTFS guard.

title: Prove six consecutive channel updates with automatic rollback
justification: V3 exit: updater delivers at least six consecutive alpha releases through the channel; automatic rollback on a fault-injected failing generation works on every Tier 1 machine.

title: Spike macOS Time Machine and APFS migration for 1.0
justification: GAP-0417: Time Machine on external drives and over the local network; decide whether read-only APFS is in 1.0. Report accepts or parks APFS; no native filesystem rewrite.

title: Spike Wi-Fi credential import from NetworkManager and Windows
justification: GAP-0419 question: import from NetworkManager keyfiles and DPAPI-encrypted Windows WLAN profiles versus re-entry. Answers before wifi-credential-import. Report must say which sources are in 1.0 and which require re-entry.

title: Support unattended install from a declarative answer file
justification: GAP-0409: unattended install covering disk layout, user, locale, network and generation channel. Required by the V4 lab matrix and fleet; the same answer file drives QEMU and hardware.

title: Provide a supported uninstall that restores the previous bootloader
justification: GAP-0410: remove JakeOS boot entries, restore the previous default bootloader, reclaim partitions and export user data in standard formats. Dual-boot coexistence must be reversible.

title: Apply updates as atomic new SystemGenerations
justification: §63 updater: create generations atomically, roll back from the updater and from the boot menu, honour decide-update-orchestration (background fetch, deferral, metered links). PKG commits the generation; BOOT falls back; INS is the client.

title: Let the user pick and switch update channels
justification: V3 scope: updater with channels (alpha, testing). REL owns promotion criteria; INS owns the Settings control that selects the channel and shows soak state.

title: Test N-to-N+1, rollback and oldest-to-current upgrade chains
justification: GAP-0149: generation N to N+1 and rollback, plus a long chain from the oldest supported release to current, on QEMU and lab hardware. Keeps the §30 rollback guarantee true across public alphas.

title: Upgrade V3 installs to V4 with data preserved and rollback
justification: V4 exit: at least 100 V3 alpha installs upgraded through the update channel with user data preserved and rollback to V3 possible at the stated success rate. PKG owns format migration; INS owns the client path.

title: Import Wi-Fi credentials during migration when feasible
justification: Implements the spike-wifi-credential-import result so first-boot is not stuck offline. If the spike forbids a source, the installer requires re-entry for that source and records it.

title: Import Windows user-profile data into native Collections
justification: GAP-0414: migration assistant import from on-disk or attached Windows profiles (Documents, Pictures, Desktop, Downloads, Music, Videos, browser profiles) with progress, resumability and post-copy verification. APP may host the UI; INS owns the import engine.

title: Decide whether the kernel offers synchronous call with time-slice donation beside async send
justification: Call semantics change scheduler and ABI shape irreversibly; decided on the separate same-core and cross-core numbers from spike-fast-path-techniques, jointly reviewed with SCH and TSK (§15, §18).

title: Decide which Channel syscalls become Layer 1 freeze candidates for SDK v1
justification: Critique: L1 surfaces are prototyped through V0, freeze candidates at V1, frozen at V4; IPC names its candidate entry points and what stays behind user-space interfaces, feeding ABI's freeze process (§65, §66).

title: Decide the interface-evolution rules for Layer 2 interfaces (prototyped state)
justification: Defines how interfaces version, add fields, add optional methods and negotiate, using findings from spike-versioning-revisions. Recorded as prototyped in V0 per the critique (freeze L2 evolution rules at V1, not V0); the V1 freeze is adr-freeze-evolution-rules.

title: Select the small-message fast-path technique from measured prototypes
justification: V0 exit requires an accepted fast-path-mechanism ADR listing rejected options; decided from spike-fast-path-techniques results before Channel kernel semantics are fixed (§15).

title: Freeze the Channel Layer 1 ABI surface
justification: V4 exit: Layer 1 frozen with the freeze ADR accepted; IPC's amendment covers channel syscalls, handle-transfer layout and the version header, with deprecated entry points removed (§65, §66).

title: Freeze the Layer 2 interface-evolution rules for SDK v1
justification: Critique ordering fix: L2 evolution rules freeze at V1 with SDK v1, after the V0 prototype and V0.5 UI protocol bump have exercised them; options include deferring the freeze to V2.

title: Decide whether IDL-generated code is committed or generated at build time
justification: Must be decided before the first generated Rust stubs land in the repository; the accompanying determinism CI check is delivered by ipc-ci-gates.

title: Decide that IDL compiler output is owned by its user with no copyleft obligation
justification: Generated stubs land in every application from V0 onward; the decision is encoded as a generated-code exception in every emitted file header by idl-compiler-rust. Reviewed with GOV licensing policy.

title: Decide how the IDL language itself is versioned
justification: V3 opens the public repository to third-party packages authoring interfaces; a language version pragma and compatibility policy for the compiler must exist before that.

title: Decide the IDL: adopt WIT, FIDL, Cap'n Proto schema or design new
justification: Written evaluation against ownership transfer, capability passing, versioning, optional methods, streams and multi-language codegen; records that the IDL ships with an evolution story (INV-0260) and that every interface carries an explicit evolution strategy. Depends on spike-ipc-prior-art. V0 exit requires an accepted IDL ADR with rejected options.

title: Decide the relationship between the native IDL and WIT
justification: Same language, bidirectional mapping or independent; must precede the V1 Wasm-component-on-native-Channel prototype owned by WASM (§13).

title: Decide service naming and discovery: kernel-held registry or user-space broker
justification: Clients must rebind by interface identity across restarts for the V0.5 compositor crash-recovery gate; decided with SVC supervision semantics (§32).

title: License IDL files and the ABI specification under a permissive spec licence with patent non-assert
justification: Layer 2 interface definitions first appear in V0.5 (compositor, package, storage); the licence must be settled before third parties see them. Reviewed with GOV.

title: Decide the pluggable transport abstraction behind generated stubs
justification: Fixes how generated stubs bind to same-component, same-machine (default) and later VM transports without regenerating interfaces (§43); distribution itself stays out of the kernel and remote transports remain LATER per the critique.

title: Decide how capabilities and handles cross a VM transport boundary
justification: Native guest components talking to host services need proxied capability semantics that honour attenuation and revocation (§43); precedes vm-transport-prototype and VIRT's guest tools.

title: Decide the typed-message wire format and inline-payload threshold
justification: Chooses fixed-layout, self-describing or schema-indexed representation and its zero-copy properties, and resolves the size threshold and heuristics for inline small message versus MemoryObject transfer, from spike-wire-encoding measurements (§14, §15).

title: Implement batched Channel send and receive submission over Operations
justification: Productionises the batching measured in spike-fast-path-techniques for high-rate streams (compositor frames, audio) that gate V1, using TSK's Operation submission path (§15, §18).

title: Extend the IPC benchmark with Windows and macOS baselines for 1.0 publication
justification: 1.0 exit: every §54 metric published on Tier 1 hardware against Linux, Windows and macOS; adds ALPC and Mach-port ping-pong baselines to the V0 harness under BEN methodology with no unmeasured claim.

title: Build the IPC round-trip benchmark against Linux UDS and pipe ping-pong
justification: V0 benchmark gate: small-message same-core and cross-core p50/p99 measured on reference hardware and QEMU and published beside Unix-domain-socket and pipe numbers, publish-only in V0; registered with BEN and run in CI on every merge. Also the vehicle for the OBS tracing-overhead gate.

title: Write reference pages for every Channel Layer 1 entry point and object type
justification: V3 exit requires reference pages for 100% of Layer 1 ABI entry points; DOC owns the build, IPC authors the channel, handle-transfer and error-type pages.

title: Define Channel<T> backpressure: bounded depth, slow-receiver policy, depth in os inspect
justification: Critique extra item: bounded queue depth per channel, sender behaviour as block-as-Operation, fail or drop-by-policy, and queue depth exposed to OBS for `os inspect channel`.

title: Define graceful close, drain and peer-closed delivery for Channel endpoints
justification: Service restart and client rebind (V0.5 exit) need deterministic close ordering: in-flight messages drained or failed with a typed result, peer-closed observable as an Operation, no lost handles on close (§32).

title: Add conformance tests for every frozen Channel Layer 1 entry point
justification: V4 exit: every Layer 1 entry point has a conformance test and binaries built against the freeze candidate run on every subsequent beta build.

title: Add structure-aware fuzz targets for the Channel syscall surface
justification: Kernel-side counterpart of the generated interface fuzzers: targets for channel create, send, receive, handle transfer and close, handed to BLD's fuzzing infrastructure and required by the V3 continuous IPC fuzzing gate.

title: Implement the Channel kernel object with typed endpoints, send, receive and inspect data
justification: Kernel Core owns channel transport (§4); Object<Channel<Message>> handles, endpoint pairs, queueing, peer-closed state and the ownership/relationship data behind `os inspect channel` (V0 exit criterion). Built on the wrapper strategy from CMP and handle representation from ABI.

title: Charge Channel queue memory and handle slots to the owning ResourceDomain
justification: SCH scope includes kernel-object limits; queued messages must not evade the ResourceDomain memory budget proven in V0, and bounded depth from channel-backpressure needs an accounting home before real applications ship in V0.5 (§23).

title: Generate client-side disconnect, rebind and retry support for restartable services
justification: V0.5 exit: killing the compositor rebinds all windows with no application exit, 100 consecutive times; generated proxies observe disconnect, re-resolve by interface identity via the discovery mechanism and re-establish per the interface's declared restart policy (§32).

title: Define and implement typed error, peer-death and timeout semantics for calls
justification: V0 fault demo: B panics and A observes a typed disconnect; IDL error taxonomy, disconnect result on peer death and Timeout result via Operation deadlines (§12, §32).

title: Implement feature negotiation between interface endpoints
justification: Endpoints advertise and agree optional feature sets at connect time per adr-evolution-rules; needed by SDK v1 so applications built against v1.0.0 keep working across v1.x services (§12).

title: Add IDL codegen backends for the remaining supported SDK languages
justification: Languages beyond Rust and C selected by SDK's bindings adr; each backend passes the shared conformance corpus so all bindings interoperate over one wire format (§50).

title: Define the IDL compiler backend interface so SDK languages add codegen targets
justification: Codegen must target every supported SDK language (§50); a stable backend API over the compiler's typed IR lets SDK add languages without touching the front end.

title: Generate C bindings from the IDL for the Layer 1 ABI and core interfaces
justification: V1 scope: C bindings for the Layer 1 ABI ship with SDK v1; C is the second codegen target and validates idl-backend-plugin-api.

title: Fuzz the IDL compiler front end against malformed third-party interface files
justification: Third-party packages in the V3 public repository submit IDL; the compiler becomes an attack surface in the build pipeline and joins BLD's continuous fuzzing.

title: Implement the IDL compiler with Rust wire layout, stub, ownership and tracing codegen
justification: Front end (parse, typecheck, move/borrow/share annotations) plus the first backend: generated wire representation, client and server stubs, ownership semantics and per-method tracing metadata so IPC calls appear as semantic spans in `os trace` (§14, §24). The IDL is the single schema source; emitted headers carry the generated-code licence exception.

title: Carry doc comments and semantic metadata through the IDL compiler IR
justification: Critique: IDL-to-docs generation must exist at V1 with SDK v1 (DOC owns the generator); the compiler must preserve documentation and deprecation metadata for it.

title: Emit fuzz harnesses and structure-aware mutators from the IDL compiler
justification: Every typed IPC boundary is a trust boundary; harnesses generated for each interface and wire format feed BLD's fuzzing pipeline and the V3 continuous IPC fuzzing gate.

title: Add an IDL lint enforcing the interface design guidelines
justification: Turns the V0.5 guidelines into CI checks (naming, error taxonomy, stream and capability-passing idioms) before third parties author interfaces against SDK v1.

title: Add IDL annotations for semantic interfaces consumed by the semantic registry
justification: V1 exit requires semantic interface v0 for Terminal and Editor; SEM owns the registry but needs IDL attributes for semantic verbs, object types and automation exposure, kept in dependency order registry before AI broker (§42, §57).

title: Implement the same-component transport for generated interface stubs
justification: First alternate transport proving adr-transport-abstraction: an interface served in-process with identical application semantics, used by component graphs and the toolkit (§43).

title: Generate typed Inputs<T> and Outputs<T> endpoint bundles for Components
justification: Components declare typed receiving and sending endpoints; the critique moves the Inputs/Outputs manifest to V0.5 with CMP component graphs, so codegen lands here and CMP consumes the types in the manifest (§10).

title: Publish interface design guidelines for IDL authors including failure and restart semantics
justification: Naming, error taxonomy, async and stream patterns, capability-passing idioms and required client behaviour on service loss (disconnect, rebind, retry, restore-state), reviewed before the first Layer 2 interface freezes (§12, §32).

title: Build the interface compatibility tool that diffs two IDL versions
justification: Classifies changes as compatible, forward-only or breaking against the frozen evolution rules and runs in CI on every Layer 2 interface change (§12).

title: Publish interface evolution guidelines for SDK authors
justification: Companion to the frozen rules and diff tool for SDK v1 authors; DOC publishes, IPC authors the content (§12).

title: Generate Interface<T> proxies with async methods, futures and in-flight cancellation
justification: Typed service contracts as declared in the IDL (interface ImageDecoder { async decode(Image) -> Bitmap; }); methods surface as Operation<Result> futures from TSK and cancelling the Operation cancels the in-flight call. Required by the V0 demo and cancellation demo (§12, §14, §59).

title: Generate interface version identities and negotiation code
justification: Per-interface version identity and generated negotiation at connect time per adr-evolution-rules; required by the V0.5 exit criterion that bumps the UI protocol v0 to v0.1 with old clients still running (§12, §14).

title: Close High and Critical findings from the external IPC security audit
justification: V4 scope: external audit of IPC among kernel capability enforcement and personalities with all High/Critical fixed before RC1.

title: Add CI lints for IPC non-goals, transport-agnostic stubs and generator determinism
justification: Standing rules enforced once: no sockets, raw byte[] payloads, per-service serialization, hand-written protocols or duplicated schemas in native code; generated stubs must not assume same-process or same-machine endpoints and no distribution logic may enter the kernel; generator output is deterministic and matches checked-in IDL.

title: Tune the IPC fast path to the V1 same-core and cross-core round-trip targets
justification: V1 benchmark gate sets p50 ≤ 2 µs same-core and ≤ 5 µs cross-core on the reference desktop, published beside Linux UDS and futex ping-pong; the first rung where a numeric target applies.

title: Measure fuzz coverage of every Channel syscall and Layer 2 interface for the V3 gate
justification: V3 exit: kernel and IPC fuzzing run continuously with no open crasher older than 14 days; this report proves every IPC surface has a generated or hand-built target and tracks crasher age.

title: Publish the unsafe-code inventory for IPC kernel and runtime code
justification: V4 exit requires an unsafe-code inventory with justification per block; IPC contributes its fast-path and handle-transfer blocks (§51).

title: Run old-client/new-service and new-client/old-service tests for every Layer 2 interface
justification: V4 exit requires the interface-evolution test to pass for every core interface; the matrix is built in V3 when third-party packages start depending on Layer 2 versions so V4 locks on evidence.

title: Register Layer 2 core platform interfaces with strong versions and a CI version check
justification: Compositor, storage, network, audio and package interfaces are declared in the IDL with version identities; CI rejects an interface change without a version bump or evolution-rule compliance (§66).

title: Enumerate and lock the Layer 2 interface versions served for 1.x
justification: V4 exit: Layer 2 versions for 1.x enumerated and locked with the evolution test matrix green for every core interface (§66).

title: Publish the supported Layer 2 interface versions and deprecation policy for 1.x
justification: 1.0 exit: a published compatibility document lists supported Layer 2 versions with a minimum two-minor-release deprecation overlap; IPC owns the versioning rules, ABI and GOV sign off.

title: Lower large and variable-size payload types to MemoryObject transfer in codegen
justification: The IDL must make MemoryObject transfer the natural encoding for large data; the compiler applies the adr-wire-format threshold so image, buffer and file payloads in the V0.5 apps never move bytes (§15).

title: Transfer Capability and MemoryObject ownership inside Channel messages
justification: V0 demo and exit criterion: a MemoryObject capability moves between components without copying the payload, verified by physical-page identity; handle slots in the wire format with move semantics so large payloads never copy per hop (§15, §16).

title: Harden receiver-side wire validation for bounds, handle counts and type tags
justification: Typed IPC boundaries are the trust boundaries between components (GAP-0129 rationale, SEC threat model at V0); validation cost measured in spike-wire-encoding is spent here with hostile-message tests before untrusted Wayland-bridge and package clients appear in V0.5.

title: Support optional methods and forward/backward schema evolution in the IDL
justification: Adding fields without breaking old receivers, unknown-field preservation by new receivers and optional methods with typed unsupported results, as exercised by the V0.5 UI protocol bump (§12).

title: Prototype a remote-machine transport honouring capabilities, identity and encryption
justification: Distributed and remote interfaces are explicitly not promised by 1.0 and parked in LATER; the prototype must surface latency, expose explicit failure semantics and stay outside the kernel (§43, §57).

title: Review that interfaces permit a remote transport with surfaced latency and failure
justification: Design review of core interfaces confirming nothing precludes a future remote-machine transport, that latency would be surfaced not hidden and that disconnect, timeout and partial failure are explicit; no remote transport is built (1.0 non-promise, §43).

title: Switch directly to a waiting receiver on send without a run-queue round trip
justification: §53 native IPC shape; V0 benchmark gate measures native task handoff versus Linux thread switch. Coordinated with SCH for the direct-switch hook and with adr-call-semantics.

title: Implement the selected minimal-copy small-message fast path
justification: Implements adr-fast-path-selection so the common small-message case needs no userland serialization or deserialization step (§15, §53); measured by bench-ipc-roundtrip.

title: Prototype and measure ring, register, handoff and batched small-message fast paths
justification: Single measured comparison on identical hardware (QEMU + reference AMD desktop) of shared ring buffers, register-carried messages, seL4/LRPC-style direct handoff, lock-free cross-core queues and io_uring-style batching; same-core and cross-core round trips recorded separately. Publish-only numbers (critique contradiction 5: no '< 1 µs' V0 target). Precedes adr-fast-path-selection and adr-call-semantics.

title: Study Cap'n Proto RPC, FIDL/Overnet, Genode and QNX before fixing the Channel wire model
justification: Written study of capability semantics across transports, synchronous message passing and restartable resource managers; feeds adr-idl-selection, adr-wire-format and adr-call-semantics (§43, §58). One of the research studies the critique keeps in V0 because it informs V0 surfaces.

title: Evolve one real V0 interface through three incompatible revisions to exercise the versioning scheme
justification: Critique ordering fix: the versioning design must fail on a real evolution before any rule is frozen; uses the V0 demo ImageDecoder-style interface and produces findings for adr-evolution-rules (§12).

title: Benchmark in-place zero-copy access versus compact encode/decode including validation cost
justification: Measures encoding, decoding and receiver-side validation cost for representative message shapes and sizes so adr-wire-format and the inline-vs-MemoryObject threshold are decided on numbers (§14, §15, §53).

title: Support stream (multi-value) results with flow control in the IDL and runtime
justification: Compositor frame events, input events and file listings in V0.5 need multi-value results; stream flow control reuses channel-backpressure policy (§12).

title: Add the permanent UI protocol v0 to v0.1 interface-versioning regression test
justification: V0.5 exit criterion: interface versioning exercised end to end by bumping the UI protocol with an added optional method while old clients still run, retained permanently as a regression test; IPC verifies its own gate with UIP.

title: Build the virtio VM transport from a native guest component to a host service
justification: First non-local transport behind adr-transport-abstraction, non-gated in V2 alongside VIRT's KVM manager and JakeOS guest images (§43); remote-machine transport remains out of scope through 1.0.

title: Add the version header and forward/backward unknown-field compatibility tests
justification: V0 exit criterion: a message with an unknown newer field is accepted by an older receiver and an older message by a newer receiver. Includes the message-level part of the Layer 1 negotiation handshake test that ABI owns (critique contradiction 12); the full schema-evolution feature set lands in optional-methods-schema-evolution.

title: Decide which kernel evolution phase is required at 1.0
justification: Which of Phases C, D or E is a hard 1.0 requirement is KRN divergence policy, not GOV legal. divergence-policy-document defines phases; phase-e-readiness-assessment is the 1.0 measurement. This adr picks the gate. Options: Phase C wrappers still allowed, Phase D controlled divergence required, or Phase E independent native ABI required.

title: Decide eBPF's native role and the Linux personality's bpf() exposure
justification: Decides whether eBPF is the tracing substrate, sched_ext host and network policy engine natively, and whether the personality exposes bpf() beyond a CAP_BPF-equivalent capability; OBS and NET tasks at V1/V2 depend on it.

title: Decide kernel-core vs user-space service boundary and the criteria for moving one
justification: §4 places memory, IPC, capabilities and scheduler in the kernel core and UI/storage/network in user space; the ADR fixes that split for V0 with measured-cost criteria for crossing the boundary, so residency is decided by cost rather than ideology.

title: Decide kernel strategy: Linux fork vs new microkernel vs Linux-as-hypervisor
justification: V0 exit requires an accepted ADR for every V0 architectural choice; this records the hardware-maturity-vs-native-model rationale of §1/§5 and lists microkernel-for-purity and Linux-as-hypervisor as rejected options, which is how the two microkernel non-goals are enforced.

title: Decide how KVM is exposed natively as Capability<VirtualMachine>
justification: Answers the §69 question of the native virtualization object and whether compatibility personalities may fall back to VMs; VIRT's V2 VM manager and the KVM object task depend on it.

title: Decide that kernel live-patching is a non-goal in favour of generations plus reboot
justification: Records generations plus reboot as the update model with live-patching as a rejected option before the update channel ships at V1.

title: Decide module signing under Secure Boot for out-of-tree, GPU and local modules
justification: Pulled from V2 to V1 because the critique notes HW's V1 NVIDIA ADR depends on it; options include project key only, MOK enrolment, and local developer keys with taint.

title: Decide the licence for new native kernel code
justification: Options GPLv2-only, GPLv2-or-later, dual GPLv2/MIT for reusable abstractions; must precede the first native commit because it decides whether kernel-side abstractions can ever be shared with permissive user space. Coordinated with GOV's licensing policy.

title: Decide out-of-tree module policy: GPL-only native exports and taint semantics
justification: Settles whether native kernel symbols are exported GPL-only and how taint behaves before the native ABI stabilises at V1; MODULE_LICENSE semantics for inherited modules are preserved as the baseline option.

title: Decide Phase D entry: when full upstream merges stop being mandatory
justification: Applies the measurable triggers from the divergence policy to the merge-bot and delta-report data and decides whether controlled divergence begins; the Phase D playbooks depend on it.

title: Decide kernel Rust toolchain pinning relative to the Rust-for-Linux minimum
justification: Answers the V0.5 question early because the fork repository and CI need a toolchain on day one: track upstream's minimum, pin independently, or pin with a bounded lag, and what happens when upstream stabilises features the fork depends on.

title: Decide the upstream Linux tree and LTS series the fork is cut from
justification: Nothing in KRN can start before the base is chosen; the ADR decides mainline vs LTS and the specific series, with options and a six-month review hook fed by the V0.5 rebase-cost report.

title: Decide the upstream-first policy for the hardware layer and Rust abstractions
justification: Decides whether driver and subsystem fixes and reusable Rust abstractions go to upstream Linux and Rust-for-Linux before or alongside the fork, which bounds the divergence surface from the first patch.

title: Decide upstream tracking: rebase vs merge and cadence per divergence phase
justification: Separate from the base-version decision: fixes periodic-rebase vs merge, the cadence for phases A-C, and how stable-branch backports are automated; the merge bot, delta report and V1 rebase gate depend on it.

title: Establish the process for adopting upstream architecture improvements
justification: Phase D source of architecture improvements (x86 mitigations, new CPU features) needs an adoption process with the mitigation benchmark as its acceptance check.

title: Publish the architecture maintenance plan with build-only ARM64 and RISC-V CI
justification: x86-64 is the only shipped target, but the fork must not break ARM64 or RISC-V; build-only per-architecture CI enforces that and the plan documents what a future port needs.

title: Prune the kernel attack surface for the three target machines
justification: §62 constrains hardware to three named machines, so unused legacy drivers, obsolete filesystems and protocols can be disabled; the pruned config must keep every facility the retained inventory and LNX's V1 decisions (seccomp, userns, overlayfs, ptrace, inotify, ia32) require.

title: Remediate external audit findings in kernel-resident native code
justification: V4 exit: external security audit of kernel capability enforcement and IPC with all High/Critical findings fixed and re-verified by the auditor; KRN owns the kernel-side fixes.

title: Benchmark security mitigation overhead with mitigations on versus off
justification: The V4 benchmark gate cites mitigation overhead measured and published; the harness lands with the hardening baseline so every later baseline change is costed on the IPC, component-creation and L2 workloads.

title: Extend the CVE pipeline to backport fixes into diverged subsystems
justification: Phase D security fixes need patch-porting automation and applicability checks against diverged or removed code so the V3 21-day median and 1.0 14-day SLA remain reachable.

title: Build the CVE ingestion pipeline tagging applicability against the fork
justification: Pulls kernel CNA and upstream advisories, auto-tags applicability against forked or removed subsystems using the ledger, and opens triage tasks; required before the fork carries daily-driving users.

title: Exercise kernel CVE response and publish the V3 response-time distribution
justification: V3 exit: inherited High/Critical CVEs fixed in a shipped generation with median under 21 days and the distribution published, and the process exercised via at least two advisories.

title: Write the kernel CVE response process: triage, backport, test, disclosure
justification: Defines triage, upstream patch identification, backport, testing and disclosure timeline for the forked kernel; REL owns publication and advisories, KRN owns the kernel-side steps.

title: Publish the 90-day kernel CVE SLA compliance report for 1.0
justification: 1.0 exit: trailing 90 days of CVE response meet the 14-day SLA for at least 90% of applicable CVEs with the distribution published, and the ledger shows zero unclassified patches at the gate.

title: Build the divergence ledger classifying every fork patch with a CI gate
justification: Every patch is tagged upstream-candidate, fork-only or temporary with rebase status, exposed as a generated report; the CI gate fails a milestone roll-up on any unclassified patch. The SBOM half of GAP-0055 is verified by BLD's SBOM gate.

title: Write the kernel divergence policy defining phases A-E and their gates
justification: Defines what upstream tracking each phase requires and the measurable triggers for entering Phase D, and records that upstream mergeability is never preserved at the expense of the architecture (§57).

title: Build tooling to pull upstream driver changes into the fork per subsystem
justification: Per-subsystem cherry-pick and adapt tooling with conflict reports and regression-matrix runs, so driver fixes keep flowing while native hooks grow (V1 risk).

title: Merge the first upstream stable release into the fork with boot matrix green
justification: Rehearses the tracking strategy on a real release before the V1 gate requires it, keeping Phase A close to upstream and producing the measured rebase cost the base-version ADR asked for.

title: Create the kernel fork repository with upstream remote and rebase workflow
justification: Establishes the repository, upstream remote, patch-series tracking and a documented rebase workflow that every later KRN task builds on; boot from a tagged commit is a V0 exit criterion.

title: Run the GPU driver update process tracking amdgpu, i915, xe and nouveau fixes
justification: V1 requires GPU acceleration on the AMD desktop and Intel laptop; a nightly tracking job and documented cadence bring upstream GPU fixes into the fork without destabilising DRM.

title: Write the hardware enablement process for new devices after divergence
justification: V3 Tier 2 machines and the compatibility database require a process for enabling new devices when upstream merges are no longer mandatory.

title: Create the 1.x kernel maintenance branch with backport rules
justification: 1.0 scope: the 1.x maintenance branch and backport policy (GOV, KRN); the kernel branch pins the LTS base from the V4 policy and wires the CVE pipeline to it.

title: Maintain a base defconfig plus per-target fragments with a build-and-boot check
justification: QEMU minimal, QEMU desktop and reference AMD desktop fragments with a CI check that each still builds and boots; prevents CONFIG drift from silently breaking hardware, and keeps the retained facilities the personality needs enabled.

title: Define and CI-enforce the kernel hardening configuration baseline
justification: KASLR, stack protector, kCFI, SMEP/SMAP, IBT, shadow stacks, init_on_alloc/free, hardened usercopy, W^X and randomized freelists as a checked-in config with a CI check that no fragment weakens it.

title: Set kernel identity: uname strings, version scheme and bug-report routing
justification: Once developers daily-drive the OS at V1, crash and bug reports must never reach upstream Linux as Linux; fixes uname, version scheme, taint flag and the routing text in oops output.

title: Draft the 1.x kernel base and support-window policy
justification: V4 scope lists LTS branch policy and support policy drafts (CVE SLA, support window) with KRN as co-owner; decides which upstream LTS underpins 1.x and how stable backports flow for 24 months.

title: Wire KUnit and Rust kernel unit tests for native primitives into pre-merge CI
justification: Capability derivation, channel semantics and Operation lifecycles need in-kernel unit coverage under QEMU on every pre-merge build before integration tests are viable.

title: Test KVM and nested virtualisation in CI including the harness inside a guest
justification: Preservation claims for KVM need tests: the retained path and nested virtualisation run in CI and JakeOS runs its own test harness inside a guest.

title: Expose retained KVM to native software as a capability-mediated VirtualMachine
justification: Kernel-side object wrapping KVM VM and vCPU handles behind capabilities with MemoryObject-backed guest memory; the VIRT workstream builds the VM manager on it at V2.

title: Enforce signature verification for modules and driver firmware under Secure Boot
justification: Kernel lockdown, module signature enforcement and verified firmware loading so the chain of trust does not end at the kernel image; V3 Secure Boot on all Tier 1 machines depends on it.

title: Add the native platform as an in-tree kernel subsystem beside Linux facilities
justification: Phase A mechanics: a self-contained native subsystem with its own Kconfig and minimal hooks into core files, such that a build with it disabled is functionally upstream; this keeps the fork close to upstream while ABI/CAP/CMP/IPC land their code in it.

title: Write the Phase D playbook for adapting upstream driver improvements
justification: Once merges are no longer mandatory, driver improvements are adapted rather than merged; the playbook codifies selection, adaptation and regression-matrix steps on the V1 tooling.

title: Assess Phase E readiness and open the 2.0 kernel divergence RFC
justification: Measures the kernel against the §6 Phase E definition (independent native ABI, execution, security, IPC and system semantics) and lists the deferred divergence items in the 2.0 planning RFC required by the 1.0 exit.

title: Capture kernel panics to pstore/kdump and hand them to the crash reporter
justification: Kernel panics are the highest-severity regressions; persistent capture and hand-off after the next successful boot feed the V3 crash-reporting pipeline and panic-rate telemetry.

title: Publish the six-month rebase cost report and revisit the tracking ADRs
justification: GAP-0534 requires a measured rebase cost after the first six months; the report records engineer-days, conflict counts by subsystem and regressions, and reopens the base and tracking ADRs if thresholds are exceeded.

title: Define the retained-subsystem regression matrix as a merge-blocking gate
justification: The second of the two collapsed retain tasks: kselftest subsets for DRM, PCI, USB, NVMe/block, networking and ACPI plus a module-licence/GPL-only-symbol test, run on QEMU and the reference desktop; any regression blocks a native feature from merging. BLD hosts the runners; KRN owns the matrix contents.

title: Write the rewrite-versus-retain policy for replacing inherited C with Rust
justification: One document covers all the no-heroic-rewrite non-goals: a rewrite is allowed only with an ADR citing a semantic or measured benefit, and mature C is retained where rewriting adds insufficient value.

title: Enforce Rust-first and rewrite-requires-ADR rules with a kernel-tree CI lint
justification: V0 exit: all new kernel code is Rust unless an ADR exempts a specific file and clippy/rustfmt are clean; the lint enforces the exemption list and refuses patches that replace inherited C without a linked ADR, covering the standing rules as a gate rather than per-rule tasks.

title: Establish selective adoption of upstream mm, scheduler and subsystem patches
justification: Defines how algorithms, scheduler ideas, memory-management improvements and subsystem patches are evaluated and adapted rather than blindly merged, with benchmark evidence required per adoption.

title: Produce the retained-mechanism inventory from a study of Linux subsystems
justification: Per the critique the 46 preserve/retain items collapse into one inventory task; it lists every retained mechanism (page tables, allocators, interrupts, scheduler, block, net, drivers, KVM, x86-64 plus untouched ARM64/RISC-V arch code) with the semantics each replaces, and is reviewed at every later gate.

title: Spike Rust-in-kernel viability and decide the C-versus-Rust boundary
justification: V0 risk: the Rust-for-Linux API surface may lack bindings to mm, scheduler, DRM and VFS; the spike identifies which subsystems need new abstractions for the native platform and reports the boundary the rewrite-vs-retain policy and lint gate enforce.

title: Publish the subsystem maintenance ownership map for retained Linux code
justification: Assigns an owner to every inherited subsystem in the retained-mechanism inventory so CVE triage tasks and merge conflicts route to a person.

title: Add kernel config fragments for the Intel and AMD target laptops
justification: V2 hardware scope adds two laptops; each gets a fragment in the build-and-boot check so laptop-specific drivers cannot drift out of the config.

title: Publish the kernel unsafe-code inventory with a justification per block
justification: V4 exit requires the unsafe-code inventory published with justification per block and unsafe authority minimised per §51; generated from the native subsystem tree and gated in CI.

title: Generate the upstream delta report: patch delta, conflict hot-spots, unmerged fixes
justification: Consumes ledger and bot output to publish patch delta, conflict hot-spots and unmerged upstream security fixes per subsystem; feeds the Phase D entry ADR and the CVE pipeline.

title: Build the upstream-tracking bot that trial-merges stable and mainline tags
justification: Attempts merges of each upstream stable and mainline tag, reports conflicts by subsystem and runs the boot matrix on the result, giving continuous visibility of divergence cost before Phase D.

title: Rebase or adapt one upstream stable release during V1 per the divergence policy
justification: V1 exit criterion: at least one upstream stable release rebased or adapted following the divergence policy with L0 still green; includes the milestone review of the retained-mechanism list.

title: Verify V0 kernel gates: reproducible boot from a tagged commit and L0 parity
justification: V0 exit criteria: the fork boots on QEMU and the reference desktop from a CI-built image reproducible from a tagged commit, with native components started from the retained initramfs per the critique, and the L0 corpus matches the unforked kernel; includes the first milestone review of the retained-mechanism list.

title: Retain watchdog, softlockup, hung-task and NMI detection and wire them to supervision
justification: Daily-driving needs lockups surfaced: kernel detectors stay enabled and emit typed events to the SVC supervisor and the OBS crash-capture path.

title: Automate lid, dock, hibernate and RTC-wake cycles on laptops
justification: GAP-0143 and V2 laptop gate: suspend/resume, hibernate and lid/dock events with RTC wake across the milestone cycle count on each laptop Reference machine. Extends automate-suspend-cycles. PWR/HW own policy daemons; LAB owns the fixture and repetition.

title: Automate suspend and resume cycle testing on V1 Reference machines
justification: V1 exit requires automated suspend/resume on the Intel laptop and AMD desktop with Wi-Fi, display and audio functional afterwards (B-030 harness consumes the traces). Lid, dock, hibernate and the V2 cycle-count gate are automate-laptop-events (GAP-0143).

title: Build the Input-to-photon photodiode rig on the reference desktop
justification: Critique EXTRA-049: build the rig on the reference desktop before V0.5 compositor benchmarks. GAP-0138's physical half (HID injection plus photodiode or high-speed capture) lands here; later racks reuse the fixture. GFX-@bench-input-to-photon and BEN INV-1028 publish B-020.

title: Decide lab site and the remote power, console and capture stack
justification: Baseline gap: LAB has no §; CONVENTIONS requires the first adr to define that open scope. Critique Missing workstreams: LAB owns machines and rigs. Options: colocation with PDU plus serial versus office Redfish/IPMI versus hybrid. Must precede EXTRA-052 racking. Scheduler family is decide-lab-scheduler.

title: Decide lab job-scheduler family and unbootable-machine recovery
justification: GAP-0141 needs an accepted choice (LAVA versus KernelCI versus custom) and a recovery path via firmware boot-order fallback to a known-good SystemGeneration. Adr sits on the same rung as the spike and before V1 deploy. BLD owns CI tiers that consume job results.

title: Deploy lab scheduling that reserves, flashes and recovers machines
justification: GAP-0141: scheduler reserves machines, flashes images, runs jobs and returns results to CI, with automatic recovery of an unbootable machine. V1 nightly hardware lab (BLD GAP-0109) and INV-1052 regression matrix depend on this. Infrastructure as code is shared with BLD GAP-0108.

title: Equip the lab with netboot, capture, USB switching and radio peers
justification: GAP-0140: physical lab holding §62 Reference machines with network boot, consoles, HDMI/DisplayPort capture, USB device switching, programmable HID, two Wi-Fi access points for the V1 roaming gate, Bluetooth peers, and audio loopback for B-028. QEMU cannot validate GPU, suspend, wireless or peripherals (§55).

title: Install Linux comparison baselines on lab Reference machines
justification: B-020, B-031 and V1 energy and Input-to-photon gates require a mainline Linux baseline on the same Reference machine. LAB images dual-boot or swap disks; BEN publishes comparisons. Windows dual-boot waits for V2 W1/HDR gates.

title: Install Windows dual-boot baselines on the AMD desktop
justification: V2 B-027, HDR/VRR gaming and battery comparisons need Windows on the same AMD desktop where dual-boot exists. LAB owns the disk image and boot-order; WIN owns W1 scenarios; INS owns end-user dual-boot policy.

title: Instrument lab machines with external meters and battery-drain cycles
justification: V1 B-031 publishes idle draw and battery runtime on the Intel laptop; software counters are not evidence. Pulled from the jsonl V2 slot because the V1 energy gate is earlier (critique). BEN owns methodology (GAP-0547); this wires meters and drain cycles into scheduler jobs.

title: Maintain a firmware version matrix and test vendor updates
justification: GAP-0144: firmware silently changes ACPI, TPM and boot behaviour. Lab matrix records versions per machine and runs before/after vendor updates as scheduler jobs. Firmware update service and LVFS policy are HW (EXTRA-043, GAP-0343).

title: Procure assistive-technology hardware including a braille display
justification: ACC-@braille-output schedules braille at V3 so LAB can procure a display before the V4 assistive-technology script gate. USB switching from equip-reference-lab attaches the device. Screen-reader software is ACC.

title: Procure an HDR reference display and colorimeter
justification: Critique and EXTRA-051: V2 HDR10 and VRR gates need a reference HDR display and colorimeter. GFX-@hdr-output-pipeline and ICC profiles consume the fixture; LAB owns the hardware. Color pipeline adr is GFX.

title: Procure external power meters for the energy-measurement path
justification: Critique: power meters at V0.5 before V1 battery gates (B-031). LAB owns the meters; BEN GAP-0547 owns energy methodology and workloads. Installation and drain cycles are instrument-energy-path.

title: Procure and rack the Intel laptop with remote power and console
justification: Critique Hardware before the milestone: laptop procurement must be V0.5 so V1 Wi-Fi roaming, suspend-cycle and B-031 gates have a named Intel laptop. V0.5 hardware scope allows exploratory laptop use with no V0.5 gate. SKU is HW's Intel laptop adr.

title: Procure and rack the reference AMD desktop with power and capture
justification: V0 hardware scope is QEMU plus one AMD desktop; EXTRA-052 and the V0 boot-on-hardware gate need remote power, serial or USB-debug console and display capture. Later racks expand per milestone hardware scope. SKU choice is HW GAP-0550; soak scheduling is GAP-0141.

title: Procure and rack the six-machine V3 Tier 1 lab fleet
justification: V3 hardware scope: three V2 targets plus one NVIDIA desktop (gated) and one extra laptop per vendor, six machines fully tested each release. Critique: lab build-out spans V1–V3 and is on the critical path of later gates. NVIDIA SKU follows the HW NVIDIA adr.

title: Procure and rack the ten-machine V4 Tier 1 lab fleet
justification: V4 hardware scope and demo: at least ten named Tier 1 machines (second GPU generations, Intel desktop, NVIDIA, laptops per vendor) and a ten-machine run of the full suite with per-machine results. HCL publication is HW/REL; LAB owns the fleet.

title: Procure and rack V2 target machines, dock and extra displays
justification: V2 hardware scope: AMD desktop, Intel laptop and AMD laptop, plus an experimental NVIDIA desktop with no gate. Attach Input-to-photon and energy fixtures, a dock and a second display so B-020 at 60 Hz and maximum refresh, B-031 per laptop, and multi-monitor/lid-dock jobs can run. SKUs are HW target adrs.

title: Run installer and Secure Boot qualification across the Tier 1 fleet
justification: V3 installer gate (automated runs across the fleet with FDE) and Secure Boot on every Tier 1 machine need LAB scheduler jobs, key enrolment and capture. INS owns the installer; BOOT owns Secure Boot strategy; LAB drives the fleet and recovery.

title: Run Vulkan CTS and compositor tests nightly on lab GPUs
justification: GAP-0142 and §56.1: nightly Vulkan CTS, dEQP and compositor tests on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA lab machines with pass rates tracked per driver generation. NVIDIA remains non-gating at V2. GFX owns compositor tests; LAB runs them on hardware via the scheduler.

title: Run multi-day soak and release-candidate fleet soaks on Tier 1
justification: GAP-0134: multi-day soaks covering suspend/resume, generation accumulation, repeated launches and compositor uptime with memory and latency trend alerts. Also verifies the V4 RC soak-on-Tier-1 gate. OBS leak detection and BEN dashboards consume the traces; LAB owns calendar and execution.

title: Run the public-stable soak on the full Tier 1 fleet
justification: 1.0 exit: final release candidate soaked on the full Tier 1 fleet with zero open P0/P1, and HCL test-lab results per machine. REL owns channel launch; LAB executes the fleet soak and publishes per-machine hardware results used by HW/REL HCL.

title: Prototype lab reservation, image flash and unbootable recovery
justification: Critique: without automation the lab is a manual queue CI cannot depend on (GAP-0141). Spike on the V0 desktop plus Intel laptop compares LAVA, KernelCI and a custom scheduler, including firmware boot-order fallback, before decide-lab-scheduler.

title: Prototype photodiode versus camera Input-to-photon measurement
justification: Critique: schedule the Input-to-photon rig at V0 before V0.5 compositor benches (B-020). Report must choose photodiode or high-speed camera, HID injection, and calibration so build-photodiode-rig is not a guess. BEN owns published results.

title: Accept community Linux compatibility reports
justification: V3 community-submitted compatibility reports with a documented verification process into the compatibility database.

title: Decide the Linux personality container engine surface
justification: Pulled to V1 because the L2 corpus requires 100% OCI container runtime; answers Docker socket vs podman.

title: Decide the default Capability bundle for Linux apps
justification: Unmanifested Linux apps need a default directory/network/device bundle plus portal upgrades; wrong default breaks apps or hollows §9.

title: Decide /dev, sysfs and udev coexistence with native drivers
justification: User-space native drivers vs Linux-personality /dev, sysfs and udev for the same device; GPU and input at V1.

title: Decide whether ia32 emulation is retained
justification: Critique: ia32 decision before any syscall-pruning; Steam and many Windows titles depend on it.

title: Decide incremental native-interface adoption
justification: Whether a Linux-personality app may adopt native file chooser, semantic interfaces and capabilities without eroding the §3 firewall.

title: Decide how native applications opt into a Personality
justification: §3 question: capability to a Personality, embedded Linux Component, or SDK shim, and what authority that grants.

title: Decide first-class Linux packaging formats
justification: Flatpak, AppImage, deb/rpm via container, or Nix, and which is first-class; L2 corpus includes Flatpak.

title: Decide Linux personality depth and translation phase
justification: Earliest adr for per-milestone depth and the KRN-reassigned phase B–D move from direct syscall ABI to translation; must precede V1 Phase B and V2 translation.

title: Decide xdg-desktop-portal as the native grant bridge
justification: V1 D-Bus/portal strategy ADR; portals are the sandbox interface Linux apps already speak.

title: Decide the POSIX path view of native storage
justification: How the Linux personality presents native storage objects as POSIX paths while respecting Capability scope; STO owns the objects.

title: Decide X11 primary selection stays inside the bridge
justification: Critique contradiction: primary selection is emulated inside the Wayland/X11 bridge and never crosses the native clipboard.

title: Decide terminal-session authority for Linux programs
justification: V1 developer terminal is the one place users expect ambient Linux authority; policy must be explicit or §9 erodes.

title: Decide source-built versus redistributed Linux userland
justification: Trademark and license obligations of redistributing another distribution versus building from source; locks the V1 userland.

title: Decide glibc /usr/lib interoperation with Packages
justification: Native dependency model vs Linux shared libraries that expect a global /usr/lib namespace; required for unmodified glibc at V1.

title: Decide Wayland hosting and X11 via Xwayland
justification: V0.5 Wayland bridge depends on nested vs in-compositor hosting and X11-only-via-Xwayland; adr no later than the bridge.

title: Apply the default Capability bundle to Linux apps
justification: V1 daily-driving of browser/IDE without ambient home access; implements the default-bundle Decision and portal upgrades.

title: Publish Linux compatibility overhead on L2 workloads
justification: B-026 V1 publish-only gate: syscall latency and L2 non-graphics throughput vs upstream Linux on the same hardware.

title: Publish Linux compatibility overhead at 1.0
justification: B-026 1.0 publish of L5 workload overhead beside upstream Linux on every Tier 1 machine; no superiority claim without the table.

title: Publish Linux compatibility overhead on L3 workloads
justification: B-026 V2 publish on L3 workloads vs upstream Linux on the three target machines.

title: Publish Linux compatibility overhead on L4 workloads
justification: B-026 V3 publish on L4 workloads across Tier 1.

title: Publish Linux compatibility overhead on L5 workloads
justification: B-026 V4 publish on L5 workloads on every Tier 1 machine.

title: Bound POSIX authority by Component capabilities
justification: A Linux process must not reach a resource its enclosing Component was not granted, regardless of uid or file mode; capability model would otherwise be hollow.

title: Expose the native print service as a CUPS-compatible IPP socket
justification: Linux personality print bridging; Wine spooler follows WIN. Native print dialog stays APP.

title: Bridge native IME via text-input and IBus
justification: zwp_text_input_v3 plus IBus/Fcitx D-Bus so one active IME types into Linux windows; Wine IMM32/TSF is WIN out of scope.

title: Bridge org.freedesktop.Notifications to native
justification: V2 notification center and do-not-disturb for Linux apps via Notifications and portal D-Bus; Windows toast is WIN out of scope.

title: Bridge Wayland apps as native compositor windows
justification: V0.5 gate and demo: a Wayland Linux app appears as a normal window with input and clipboard, using existing Linux mechanisms underneath.

title: Capture Linux core dumps and Crashpad minidumps
justification: EXTRA-009 Crashpad path plus gdb/strace; V1 browser and IDE crash capture must work under the Personality.

title: Close High findings from the Personality audit
justification: V4 external security audit of personalities; all High/Critical Linux-personality findings fixed and re-verified.

title: Define the Steam runtime sub-corpus
justification: V2 L3 Steam-on-Linux: pressure-vessel, gamescope, userns, 32-bit multilib, /dev/input via udev, SDL evdev, with scenario scripts.

title: Define freedesktop, Mesa and systemd engagement policy
justification: Linux compatibility is a product whose Wayland, PipeWire, portals, Mesa and systemd components must not be forked casually.

title: Document unsupported Linux software classes
justification: 1.0 statement of what is not supported: kernel-level anti-cheat, vendor DRM, and Broken corpus entries with reasons.

title: Emulate Linux uid, gid, DAC, seccomp and LSM hooks
justification: Linux security semantics as needed for Chromium, Flatpak and containers, always bounded by the enclosing Component Capability set.

title: Emulate NetworkManager D-Bus and resolv.conf
justification: Browsers, chat clients and package managers query NM and nsswitch; Windows proxy/WinINet is WIN out of scope.

title: Satisfy systemd assumptions for Linux desktop apps
justification: sd-bus, socket activation, logind sessions/seats, user units, journald and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR per the glibc/systemd spike.

title: Emulate UPower and logind power D-Bus APIs

justification: V3 exit: 100% of L1 reference pages; every MemoryObject entry point, property and Capability right documented through DOC's IDL-to-docs pipeline.

justification: Pulled to V0.5 because GPU buffer allocation depends on it: physically contiguous or IOMMU-mappable allocation with a queryable suitability attribute per decide-dma-gpu-backing.

title: Implement the encrypted MemoryObject property and key-ownership semantics
justification: §16 encrypted property with who may map plaintext and how hardware memory encryption is used. Parallel to STO encrypted-at-rest; keys are Capabilities, never ambient.

title: Implement the executable property with W^X enforcement
justification: Component code pages are executable MemoryObjects; the kernel refuses any mapping that is simultaneously writable and executable and refuses to add executable to a writable-mapped object; regression test in CI.

title: Add MemoryObject syscall fuzz targets with ownership and W^X oracles
justification: V3 exit: continuous syscall fuzzing with no open crashers; MEM supplies the targets and invariant oracles (single owner, no post-transfer access, sealed never writable) for BLD's fuzzing fleet.

title: Implement MemoryObject map and unmap in a Component address space
justification: V0 exit: a Component creates and maps a MemoryObject; the writable property governs mapping protection; mappings are tracked per Component and torn down on destroy.

title: Implement the pinned property so a MemoryObject is never swapped or migrated
justification: Low-latency audio and DMA in V1 need pinned buffers; pinned pages are limited per ResourceDomain with SCH and released on owner death.

title: Implement the immutable property and sealed read-only mappings
justification: Sealing is one-way and kernel-enforced; a sealed object rejects writable mappings and write faults; needed by the V0 demo result object and later by immutable package mappings.

title: Document MemoryObject security semantics for the V0 threat model
justification: Critique moves the threat model to V0; SEC needs MEM's section on transfer enforcement, sealing, W^X, shared-mapping side channels and ownership as a §51 memory-safety layer before CAP/SEC designs are fixed.

title: Implement the shared property with multiple concurrent mappers
justification: Multiple readers per decide-coherence-model with mapper accounting; a non-shared object rejects a second mapper with a typed error; covered by tests in the V0 acceptance suite.

title: Write the retained-mm CVE triage runbook for MemoryObject in 1.x support
justification: 1.0 support commitment: upstream shmem, dma-buf and mm CVEs must be mapped to MemoryObject exposure and fixed within the 14-day SLA; the runbook records the mapping and the regression tests to run.

title: Transfer network-received MemoryObjects to a Decoder without copying
justification: §17 first stage: NIC DMA lands in a MemoryObject that NET hands to the media decoder by ownership; jointly with NET and MED on the V1 Intel laptop and reference desktop.

title: Track and expose NUMA locality of a MemoryObject
justification: §17: the system understands NUMA locality; allocation honours a preferred node and the locality is queryable for placement and `os inspect`.

title: Implement single-owner MemoryObject transfer over a Channel with sender losing access
justification: V0 exit and §59 demo: a MemoryObject Capability moves from Component A to B without copying; per decide-transfer-enforcement the sender's mappings are revoked or its handle invalidated; ABI message encoding of the move is done with IPC.

title: Implement MemoryObject placement attributes exposed to dispatch
justification: Implements decide-placement-model so HET's ComputeDevice dispatch can read where an object lives and request placement.

title: Define reclaim, swap and migration behaviour for unpinned MemoryObjects
justification: V1 daily-driving on a laptop needs memory pressure handled: which MemoryObjects Linux mm may swap or migrate, how ownership and shared mappings survive migration, and typed pressure signals to the owner.

title: Study bounds-enforced pointers and bounded MemoryObject views in the ABI
justification: §8 study that must land before L1 freeze candidates: whether the ABI can express bounded sub-views of a MemoryObject without committing to a hardware model.

title: Study CXL-attached and disaggregated memory as MemoryObject backing providers
justification: Parked research: exercises decide-backing-provider-model against remote and CXL memory on hardware not in any 1.0 tier, keeping distributed memory out of the 1.0 promise.

title: Prototype dma-buf-backed MemoryObjects with a NIC-to-GPU zero-copy path
justification: Demonstrates on the reference desktop that a dma-buf-backed MemoryObject can be filled by NIC DMA and imported by the GPU driver without a copy; evidence for decide-dma-gpu-backing.

title: Study hardware memory capabilities as an enforcement backend for mappings
justification: §8 study, with CAP's CHERI work, of whether MemoryObject mappings could be enforced by hardware capabilities without ABI change; informs the V4 freeze.

title: Measure page-table and huge-page effects on startup and TLB for package mappings
justification: The V0.5 warm-startup benchmark gate depends on how cheaply verified immutable pages are mapped and shared; measures per-Component page-table cost and huge-page TLB effects.

title: Prototype MemoryObject ownership transfer over shmem, dma-buf and native backings
justification: Measures transfer cost for 4 KB and 64 MB objects including TLB shootdown on QEMU and the reference desktop; input to the basis and enforcement decisions and to BEN's transfer-cost benchmark.

title: Preserve pinned and DMA-compatible MemoryObjects across suspend and resume
justification: V1 exit: 200 of 200 suspend cycles with display and audio functional afterwards requires GPU and audio buffers backed by MemoryObjects to survive; adds a check to the PWR cycle harness.

title: Verify MemoryObject transfer by physical-page identity in the V0 demo pipeline
justification: V0 exit criterion: transfer verified by physical-page identity check and the 1 GiB transfer measured against the register target; also asserts the sender faults after transfer and that a leaked object is reclaimed with its Component.

title: Add an interface review lint that large payloads move MemoryObjects by default
justification: Enforces Principle 6 where it first matters: the V0.5 SDK and IDL surfaces expand; the lint flags interface methods that carry large byte arrays inline or copy where a MemoryObject move is possible.

title: Implement DHCPv4 and IPv6 SLAAC/DHCPv6 with privacy extensions
justification: V1 gate: DHCP works on Ethernet and Intel Wi-Fi, including IPv6-only networks named by GAP-0292. Address assignment is a userspace service over retained kernel autoconfig, gated by network Capabilities. Split DNS waits for VPN at V2.

title: Implement airplane-mode that drops radio Capabilities without tearing profiles
justification: V2 laptop-day and desktop-essentials fill: radios off while connection profiles remain so Wi-Fi reconnects on restore. NET owns radio Capabilities; HW owns Bluetooth power. Needed before public alpha enthusiasts check the quick-settings tile.

title: Publish NetworkConnection throughput and latency against Linux sockets
justification: GAP-0538 requires measured throughput and latency for the placement decision; §54 tracks throughput. Harness compares native NetworkConnection to Linux TCP on the same hardware and publishes only; no superiority claim. BEN owns the B-ID; NET owns this harness.

title: Decide whether to ship a native typed remote shell after 1.0
justification: EXTRA-020 later half: sshd via the personality is V1; a native typed remote shell is post-1.0. Options: keep sshd only; a Channel-based remote shell honouring capabilities; an SSH-compatible native daemon. §43 forbids making distribution a kernel concern; this adr stays in userspace.

title: Decide the native TLS library and how it consumes the CA trust store
justification: Critique missing requirement 19: native TLS consumes the SEC CA trust store. Options: rustls in the native runtime, OpenSSL linked into native Components, or kernel TLS offload. Personality TLS stays in LNX/WIN. Must precede native-tls. No POSIX sockets as the native API.

title: Decide per-application network Capability granularity and inbound firewall
justification: V1 exit requires an accepted network capability-model ADR and that a Component without a network Capability cannot connect. Options: binary any/none; the GAP-0293 set (any, internet-only, local-network, specific hosts/ports, listen); flow-level per connection. Default-deny inbound is retained nftables, not a rewritten filter.

title: Decide NET baseline-gap scope: preserved stack versus native objects
justification: Synthesis: NET carries a Baseline gap header and its first adr defines scope. Options: preserve Linux TCP/IP, nftables and inherited drivers with native NetworkConnection plus SVC-hosted management; rewrite a userspace TCP stack; expose Linux sockets as the native API (rejected by §57). Must precede every V1 NET build. V0 cap forbids placing this adr in V0.

title: Decide whether NetworkConnection wraps the kernel TCP/IP stack
justification: GAP-0538 and INV-0110: data path versus capability broker placement shapes firewall and VPN. Options: wrap retained TCP/IP directly; pass every byte through a userspace service; hybrid kernel data path with userspace policy. Cites spike-netconn-placement. Surface stays prototyped until V4.

title: Decide whether 1.0 ships an SMB server and where it is hosted
justification: GAP-0434 pulled from V4 to V3 so a V4 implementation can land before feature freeze. Options: do not ship a server; Samba in the Linux personality; a native sharing service. STO owns SMB clients (reassigned GAP-0433).

title: Decide the Wi-Fi supplicant: iwd, wpa_supplicant or native Rust
justification: GAP-0291 names the supplicant ADR; the choice is the security and maintenance surface for V1 laptop daily-driving. Options: iwd, wpa_supplicant, or a native Rust supplicant. Must precede wifi-station-personal. APP owns the shell picker UI.

title: Write the native NetworkConnection programming model for SDK v1
justification: V1 SDK v1 gate needs a native networking guide so developers never reach for sockets. Documents Capability rights, Operations, resolver use and TLS. SDK packages it; NET owns the model text.

title: Fuzz NetworkConnection Connect, Accept, Send and Receive without panic
justification: V3 gate: continuous syscall and IPC fuzzing with no known open crasher. NetworkConnection is a new L1 object and must have a harness before that gate. Runs in BLD nightly; NET owns the target.

title: Verify published HCL Wi-Fi claims on every Tier 1 machine for 1.0
justification: 1.0 definition: Tier 1 HCL lists Wi-Fi as working on at least ten named machines. Re-runs tier1-wifi-suite on the soak candidate and attaches results to the published HCL. REL publishes; NET owns pass/fail.

title: Implement Wi-Fi hotspot and USB/Bluetooth tethering
justification: GAP-0296 hotspot and USB/Bluetooth tethering for public alpha. Bluetooth PAN depends on HW's V2 Bluetooth stack; USB tethering uses retained gadget/cdc. Listen/forward rights are network Capabilities.

title: Lock Layer 2 network management and resolver interface versions for 1.x
justification: V4 exit: Layer 2 interface versions for 1.x are enumerated and locked with old-client/new-service tests. NET-owned L2 surfaces are netmgr, resolver, mDNS and VPN. NetworkConnection remains L1 and freezes with ABI, not here.

title: Provide native mDNS/DNS-SD with Avahi and Bonjour personality compatibility
justification: GAP-0435 plus the mDNS/DNS-SD clause of GAP-0292. Native .local and DNS-SD for printers, NAS and developer tooling; Avahi and Bonjour APIs exist only inside personalities. SVC hostname is an input.

title: Implement metered-connection flagging and MAC address randomisation
justification: GAP-0296 public-alpha laptop checks: metered flag for update/backup policy and per-network MAC randomisation. Native only; personalities observe the same flags via LNX GAP-0295.

title: Implement native TLS on NetworkConnection using the system CA store
justification: Critique missing requirement 19: native TLS consumes SEC's CA trust store with per-application pinning. Implements decide-native-tls so signed-repo fetch and native HTTPS do not go through POSIX sockets. Personality certificate stores stay in LNX/WIN.

title: Implement the network Capability broker and default-deny inbound firewall
justification: INV-0110 userspace broker above kernel TCP; INV-0203 no ambient network access; GAP-0293 default-deny inbound on retained nftables. A Component with no network Capability cannot open or listen; listen is an explicit right. Enforces decide-net-capability. SCH owns the ResourceDomain policy field this broker applies.

title: Write the retained TCP/IP and Wi-Fi CVE triage runbook for 1.x support
