justification: Search/indexing service domain profile set to Background with I/O priority mapping; preemption test shows Interactive latency unchanged while indexing runs.

title: Implement intent declaration on ResourceDomain and Task with Interactive and Background
justification: Per the critique V0 carries only Interactive and Background. Adds the typed intent field to domain CPU policy and per-Task override, and wires intent into scheduling class and placement through the mapping chosen by decide-intent-mapping on the retained Linux scheduler; kernel core owns scheduling natively.

title: Influence core selection on hybrid CPUs and SMT siblings from intent
justification: Performance versus efficiency core placement and SMT sibling avoidance for LowLatency/Realtime; Intel laptop (hybrid topology) enters the hardware scope at V1.

title: Add Deadline intent class with declared period and completion deadline
justification: Deadline work declares period and deadline (SCHED_DEADLINE lineage or native class per the adr) with admission control bounded by the domain CPU quota; required by the V0.5 compositor frame-scheduling adr and compositor-intent-vblank.

title: Add EnergyEfficient intent class trading latency for lower power
justification: Class that prefers efficient cores and lower frequencies via uclamp.max/EPP hints; V1 gate publishes idle power and battery runtime on the Intel laptop.

title: Gate Realtime and LowLatency intent behind Capabilities shown in the permissions UI
justification: §9 no ambient authority: elevated intents are a resource grant, requested in the package manifest and revocable; V2 exit requires the permissions UI to list every active grant and revocation to take effect immediately.

title: Drive cpufreq and EPP hints from scheduling intent
justification: Latency-sensitive work is not throttled and Background work is; PWR consumes frequency 'via SCH intent' per workstreams.md so SCH owns the hint mapping. Measured on the Intel laptop energy gate.

title: Map scheduling intent to GPU priority for RenderQueue and ComputeQueue
justification: With GFX and HET: domain intent sets DRM scheduler priority for render and compute submissions so the compositor wins over background compute; V1 brings GPU acceleration for native and Linux apps.

title: Write developer guidelines for choosing scheduling intent and domain budgets
justification: SDK v1 ships at V1 and DOC generates references from IDL; SCH supplies the guide mapping §22 examples (audio, compositor, compiler, indexing, sync) to classes and budgets so third-party developers do not reach for numeric priority.

title: Map scheduling intent to I/O priority for storage and network Operations
justification: Operations submitted by a domain carry its intent into block-layer and network queue priority so Background indexing does not starve Interactive file access; part of the V1 daily-driving experience.

title: Influence NUMA and GPU-local memory placement from domain intent
justification: With MEM and HET: domain intent and ComputeDevice preference steer allocation to NUMA node or GPU-local versus host memory; V2 ComputeDevice demo dispatches Throughput to the GPU and LowLatency to the CPU.

title: Add Realtime intent class with bounded scheduling latency
justification: Critique moves Realtime to V1 alongside the native audio path. Bounded-latency class with admission control, quota fallback and a grant requirement; validated by bench-audio-callback-jitter.

title: Add Throughput and LowLatency intent classes
justification: Critique moves these classes out of V0. Throughput maximises total progress for batch work and LowLatency minimises wakeup delay; both mapped per decide-intent-mapping and measured by bench-intent-wakeup-latency.

title: Steer interrupt affinity from LowLatency domain CPU policy
justification: Domain CPU policy for LowLatency/Realtime domains pins relevant device IRQs to or away from the domain's allowed cores; effect published through bench-audio-callback-jitter on the three V2 target machines.

title: Map Linux personality nice, ionice and sched_setattr onto domain-bounded intents
justification: V1 daily-driving runs the browser and IDE through the Linux personality; their scheduler syscalls must translate into intents bounded by the app's ResourceDomain rather than raw priorities, keeping L2 compatibility overhead within the published target. LNX owns the syscall path; SCH owns the mapping policy.

title: Create per-session ResourceDomain roots with fair sharing between users
justification: V3 exit adds multi-user; each login Session (SEC) receives a delegated domain root so one user's Throughput work cannot starve another's Interactive session; tested with two concurrent sessions.

title: Add CI lints enforcing native intent, universal accounting and no cgroup steps
justification: Review-gate tests: native ABI/SDK exposes no numeric priority; every Component and Task has a domain at creation; no native code path references cgroupfs or Linux scheduler syscalls. First matters when native init, packages and services appear in V0.5.

title: Apply default ResourceDomain profiles to third-party packages from the public repository
justification: V3 opens the public repo to third-party packages; packages without a declared profile receive conservative budgets and Interactive-by-default intent, and elevated intents require the intent-escalation Capability reviewed at install.

title: Allow per-ResourceDomain pluggable scheduling policies via sched_ext
justification: Parking rung: custom user-supplied scheduling policies scoped to a domain depend on KRN's eBPF role adr and add divergence risk; deferred until the intent classes are frozen and demand is shown.

title: Report scheduling latency and budget-exhaustion incidents from the beta fleet
justification: V4 requires 99.5% crash-free sessions across the fleet; budget-exhaustion terminations and latency spikes appear as crashes or hangs in opt-in telemetry, so SCH publishes an analysis and files fixes before feature freeze.

title: Add fuzz and soak targets for ResourceDomain and intent syscalls
justification: V3 requires continuous syscall fuzzing; SCH supplies fuzz targets for domain creation, delegation, budget updates and intent changes plus a soak that checks accounting leaks over 10^6 domain lifecycles, feeding BLD's fuzzing fleet.

title: Ship the conformance suite for frozen ResourceDomain and intent Layer 1 surfaces
justification: V4 freezes L1 with a conformance suite; tests every domain and intent syscall, error code and negotiation behaviour named by decide-sch-l1-surfaces so 1.x binaries stay compatible.

title: Sign off SCH benchmarks at no more than 5% regression versus V4 on Tier 1
justification: 1.0 gate: no regression over 5% versus V4 final on any tracked benchmark on any Tier 1 machine; runs the four SCH harnesses on the release candidate during the 30-day soak and links results in the release notes.

title: Write the 1.0 stability statement for ResourceDomain and scheduling intent
justification: 1.0 publishes an ABI stability statement and explicit non-promises; SCH's section lists frozen surfaces, the versioned profile schema deprecation policy, and states that Realtime is bounded-latency best effort, not hard real time.

title: Prototype scheduler-aware Channel handoff and measure latency and fairness
justification: Direct switch to the receiver on Channel send is the §53 'scheduler-aware handoff' claim; prototype on the small-message fast path and publish round-trip latency and fairness impact against plain wakeup so the V0 IPC benchmark table (publish-only) has the native-handoff column.

title: Prototype scheduling-intent routes and measure audio and compositor latency
justification: Measures whether EEVDF+uclamp+cgroup controllers can express the seven intent classes, then prototypes intent as (a) extension of the existing class, (b) sched_ext BPF scheduler, (c) new scheduler class; publishes wakeup latency for audio-like and compositor-like workloads on QEMU and the reference desktop. Critique requires explicit V0 spikes before any decision; report lands in reports/spikes.

title: Throttle Background and Throughput domains first under thermal pressure
justification: V2 scope lists laptops thermal under HW and SCH; when PWR reports capacity loss the scheduler reduces Throughput/Background quotas before touching Interactive/Deadline, keeping the desktop UX script passing on both laptops.

title: Validate intent and domain benchmarks across the six Tier 1 machines
justification: V3 gate re-runs all prior benchmarks across Tier 1 with no regression over 10% and requires a public number for every §54 item; runs the four SCH harnesses on every Tier 1 topology (hybrid Intel, AMD, NVIDIA desktop) and files ADRs for any regression.

title: Measure timed onboarding from SDK install to a hello-Component
justification: Onboarding target lives in the benchmark register; this harness times host-OS sessions each release without stating a number in prose.

title: Restore opted-in application state through os restore
justification: §31 long-term restore of application state where apps opt in to checkpointing; SDK exposes the checkpoint API and os restore consumes it.

title: Run binding conformance tests for every shipped language
justification: V3 multi-language SDK must not silently diverge; one conformance corpus per binding against the same Layer 2 Interfaces.

title: Provide the C SDK binding over the Native ABI
justification: V1 scope is SDK v1 plus C bindings for Layer 1; ABI owns the header, SDK owns safe C wrappers and IDL stubs.

title: Prove C SDK binaries against the Layer 1 freeze candidate
justification: V4 L1 freeze: C SDK binaries built against the freeze candidate run on every subsequent beta; ABI owns L1 tests, SDK owns the C crate run.

title: Package C headers and stubs for host and native toolchains
justification: C bindings are unusable from the host SDK without packaged headers and IDL-generated stubs on Linux, macOS and Windows toolchains.

title: Integrate os publish with GitHub Actions and GitLab CI
justification: Developers publish from CI; hosted integrations wrap os publish so catalogue growth is not gated on desktop signing.

title: Add machine-readable os CLI output and shell completions
justification: §64 scripts and later automation need JSON output and completions on the os CLI family.

title: Implement Channel disconnect, rebind, retry and restore-state
justification: V0.5 compositor-restart gate needs client libraries that detect disconnect, rebind by Interface name, retry idempotent Operations and restore session state.

title: Run the SDK compatibility suite through the 1.0 soak
justification: 1.0 30-day soak includes SDK v1 binaries on the release candidate; the suite is the Layer 3 half of the compatibility-proof demo.

title: Build the SDK compatibility suite across adjacent generations
justification: V1 SDK v1 gate: applications built against v1.0.0 run on later v1.x generations and the reverse where promised, enforcing Layer 2 versioning.

title: Implement the #[component] entry macro and Context capability surface
justification: §52 makes the secure path the default: bootstrap, runtime and tracing are generated, and Context exposes only granted Capabilities.

title: Provide the C++ SDK binding
justification: §50 language order: C++ at V2 once C exists; V4 ecosystem gate needs C plus one additional language.

title: Provide the C# SDK binding
justification: §50 V3 language: C# binding over IDL stubs; Windows personality remains a separate workstream.

title: Ship a Debug Adapter Protocol adapter for native Components
justification: Developers keep their editors; DAP is the V1 integration for breakpoints and Task inspection once the protocol adr is accepted.

title: Attach a debugger to a Component with async Task stacks
justification: V1 exit: debugger attaches, breaks inside an async Task, shows the logical stack, and symbolises crash dumps; attach is a Capability, not same-uid ptrace.

title: Provide an isolated ImageDecoder library on the SDK decode path
justification: §52 decode(image) runs as an isolated Component so the PhotoEditor sample does not parse untrusted bytes in the UI Component.

title: Make SDK spawn create a new Component by default
justification: §10 cheap isolation: SDK defaults spawn a separate Component without an opt-in sandbox flag so isolate-it is the path of least resistance.

title: Provide a developer command that builds, boots QEMU and runs CI tests
justification: Contributor onboarding command wrapping BLD's harness; the time target lives in the benchmark register, not in this task's prose.

title: Lint SDK defaults for Capabilities, Tasks, async I/O and typed IPC
justification: Standing §3/§52/§57 invariants collapse into one lint and test gate: no ambient APIs, no POSIX-shaped native surface, no forced Wasm, drop-safe handles, automatic tracing and cancellation.

title: Ship a non-Rust native Package used in the V4 demo
justification: V4 demo: a native Package published by an external developer in a non-Rust SDK language, installed with capability review and tracing visible.

title: Implement files.choose returning a typed UserSelected capability
justification: V0.5 chooser gate: Image Viewer starts without filesystem authority and receives exactly one UserSelected grant; STO owns the chooser, SDK owns the API.

title: Render flame graphs by TaskGroup exportable with traces
justification: Completes the native profiler: flame graphs grouped by TaskGroup and folded into exported traces.

title: Ship a cross-compilation SDK and emulator harness on host OSes
justification: First native apps are built from Linux, macOS and Windows hosts; the SDK plus QEMU/VM harness must not require installing JakeOS to compile.

title: Ship ImageDecoder as the V0 typed-service SDK sample
justification: The V0 demo is the reference typed service: Input of image bytes, Output of a bitmap, ResourceDomain budgets, written against the Rust SDK.

title: Add os inspect support for ComputeQueue
justification: V2 ComputeDevice demo requires os inspect to show the ComputeQueue; OBS owns events, SDK adds the subcommand.

title: Declare a no_std rustc JSON target for native userspace
justification: Native crates must not compile as Linux binaries or the §3 firewall is void; V0 is a custom JSON target with alloc only, not a std port.

title: Provide the Kotlin SDK binding
justification: §50 V3 language: Kotlin binding for native Components, not a JVM personality.

title: Lint deprecated Layer 3 APIs with a deprecation window
justification: Layer 3 semver needs mechanical deprecation detection before 1.0 so SDK v1 APIs that will not survive 1.x are flagged in beta.

title: Lay out Layer 3 SDK crates under semantic versioning
justification: Layer 3 is the native SDK and may evolve quickly; crate layout and semver numbering start while the API is still explicitly unstable.

title: Ship LSP-based tooling for native SDK projects
justification: V1 developer preview meets editors via LSP over the native crate and IDL, not a new IDE.

title: Implement the tiny native runtime that multiplexes Tasks over Operations
justification: V0 exit requires a tiny native runtime with Channel and Capability wrappers sufficient to write the demo in Rust without blocking Linux syscalls.

title: Expose Operation cancel, deadline and await on the Rust SDK
justification: §19 is the SDK surface for outstanding work; V0 cancellation and deadline gates are unusable without these entry points.

title: Implement os bisect across SystemGenerations
justification: Immutable generations make regression bisection cheap; the CLI steps generations to the introducing change for public-alpha bug reports.

title: Invoke Semantic interfaces from the os CLI
justification: Semantic interfaces must support scripting clients; the os CLI is the shell invocation path, SEM owns registry and permissioning.

title: Implement the os CLI skeleton for inspect and trace
justification: §64 requires developer tooling from V0; the os binary is the home for inspect and trace and later env, history and restore.

title: Implement the os env enter command
justification: V1 self-hosting and env-startup gates; ENV materialises the environment, SDK drops the developer into it via os env enter.

title: Implement os env list, status, leave, destroy and rebuild
justification: The os env family is the developer CLI over ENV objects; list/status/leave/destroy/rebuild complete enter.

title: Implement os help serving offline on-device SDK documentation
justification: Critique missing requirement 39: offline on-device docs; DOC owns content, SDK implements the os help CLI.

title: Implement os history listing SystemGeneration events
justification: §31/§64 CLI for history events; PKG records the log, SDK prints timestamped human-readable entries. Restore of user data stays out of V0.5.

title: Ship os inspect for every V0 Object kind
justification: V0 exit prints Component, Task, Channel, Capability, MemoryObject and ResourceDomain state; OBS owns the data plane, SDK owns the command.

title: Implement os new scaffolding for a Component project
justification: V1 onboarding and the published SDK need a generator that emits manifest, requested Capabilities and build config.

title: Implement the os profile command over the native profiler
justification: The profiler is incomplete without an os CLI that records a session, attributes samples and writes the chosen export format.

title: Implement os publish to build, sign and submit Packages
justification: V3 public repository demo: a third-party developer publishes a native Package from the SDK; REL owns review and signing keys.

title: Implement os restore to a chosen history event
justification: V2 snapshots and rollback UI consume history-point restore; SDK CLI invokes PKG restore of OS, packages and configuration.

title: Implement os restore to a previous SystemGeneration
justification: Ladder moves generation restore to V1 (V0.5 is boot-menu rollback only); PKG performs the switch, SDK exposes os restore.

title: Implement os test running the Component harness
justification: V1 SDK testing story needs a single command that runs the mock-capability harness the same way CI does.

title: Ship os trace with structured dynamically enabled tracing
justification: V0 demo and tracing-overhead gate need os trace over the OBS substrate; enablement is dynamic and security-aware.

title: Emit an immutable Package with manifest from a native cargo build
justification: V0.5 packages are installed from local files; SDK build tooling produces the manifest and content-addressed Package PKG stores.

title: Ship the PhotoEditor capability sample and its denial tests
justification: §9.1 worked example must ship as an SDK sample and integration test proving denied Capabilities are absent.

title: Run the same SDK integration tests through C and C++
justification: Language bindings must not drift: one integration corpus compiled as Rust, C and C++ against the compatibility suite.

title: Implement the native CPU profiler attributed to Task and Component
justification: Critique missing requirement 31: sampling CPU profiles attributed to Task and Component, exportable with traces; GPU attribution follows at V2.

title: Attribute GPU samples to Task and Component
justification: V2 ComputeDevice and gaming gates need GPU profiles on the same Task/Component model as CPU; HET/GFX own devices, SDK owns the profiler.

title: Integrate remote development into a JakeOS VM or device
justification: VS Code and JetBrains remote-development into a JakeOS VM or device is required so host-built apps can be debugged on target.

title: Enable userspace exploit mitigations in the native runtime
justification: ASLR, NX, CET where present, guard pages and a hardened allocator are default runtime behaviour and Component manifest requirements; SEC owns policy.

title: Implement the primary Rust SDK crate over the Native ABI
justification: Native applications execute against the SDK rather than the kernel; the crate maps kernel failures to typed errors and defaults MemoryObject APIs to move semantics.

title: Propose the native rustc target for upstream tier-3 inclusion
justification: GAP-0090 later step: the custom JSON target is proposed for rustc tier-3 once SDK v1 and the Layer 3 std crate have been used in the beta fleet.

title: Make SDK and binding packages bit-for-bit reproducible
justification: V4 reproducible-builds gate includes SDK and binding Packages so third-party verifiers can rebuild developer toolchains.

title: Implement the Layer 3 Rust std compatibility crate
justification: std/alloc for the native target is a Layer 3 façade over the SDK; no Layer 1 entry may be added to make std's POSIX shapes work.

title: Provide the Swift SDK binding
justification: §50 V3 language: Swift binding generated from IDL over the recorded non-Rust mapping.

title: Provide a Component test harness with mock capabilities
justification: SDK-level tests need mock Capabilities and mock services so Components can be exercised without the full desktop.

title: Prove a third-party native Package can be published from the SDK
justification: V3 demo and repository drill: an external developer publishes from the SDK and a user installs with capability review.

title: Implement a single command that installs versioned toolchains
justification: GAP-0106 requires one toolchain-manager command so strangers do not reproduce the project's build environment by hand.

title: Package versioned developer toolchains as immutable Packages
justification: V3 third-party developers install rustc target, IDL compiler, image tools and QEMU harness as immutable Packages on Linux, macOS and JakeOS.

title: Export os trace timelines of Component, Task, Channel and Operation
justification: V0.5 needs a viewer or exporter over OBS traces; SDK ships the exporter so developers can inspect IPC and scheduling without a custom GUI yet.

title: Export an os trace session that can be viewed offline
justification: V1 debugger/tracing gate: os trace exports a session viewable offline using the OBS-chosen format.

title: Provide the TypeScript SDK binding via Wasm components
justification: §13/§50 TypeScript binding uses Wasm component integration; WASM owns the runtime, SDK owns the language surface. Does not force native apps into Wasm.

title: Implement ctx.ui.window and window.render on Context
justification: V0.5 SDK expands to windows; UIP owns the protocol, SDK exposes the §52 Context surface the four apps call.

title: Decide SDK language binding order and milestones
justification: Records Rust V0, C V1, C++ V2 and remaining languages at V3 so later binding tasks do not invent a different ladder.

title: Decide POSIX-personality shell versus a native object-aware shell
justification: Fixes how the os CLI, PTYs and job control map onto Tasks and Channels before V1 daily-driving; a POSIX shell remains a Linux personality, not the native API.

title: Decide DAP versus a native debugger protocol
justification: V1 debugger gate and editor integration need a recorded protocol choice before the adapter is built; options include DAP, a native protocol, or DAP over a native control Channel.

title: Decide the userspace executor shape for the native runtime
justification: V0 tiny-runtime gate needs a recorded choice among a custom executor, a Tokio subset over Operations, and an embassy-style executor before the runtime is built; CMP owns the kernel/runtime split.

title: Decide the native linking model and reject path-based loaders
justification: §34/§53 nongoals: no ld.so path lookup and no global constructors on the launch critical path; options are static, content-addressed shared objects, or both.

title: Decide how non-Rust bindings map onto Layer 1 and IDL stubs
justification: Swift, Kotlin, C# and TypeScript at V3 need a recorded mapping onto the C ABI and IDL before those bindings start; options are C-only, per-language codegen, or both.

title: Decide profiler export format and Task attribution
justification: Native profiles are attributed to Task, Component and TaskGroup, not threads; the adr picks pprof, Firefox Profiler, or a native format folded into traces.

title: Decide the license of the native SDK, runtime and language bindings
justification: Third-party native applications begin at V0.5; the adr must permit proprietary apps and sit beside GOV's layer firewall and the ABI header-exception adr.

title: Decide the Layer 3 SDK semver and deprecation policy
justification: V1 gate requires an accepted SDK stability-policy adr; Layer 3 evolves with semver and deprecation windows, not a Layer 1 freeze.

title: Decide that Rust std lives only as a Layer 3 crate
justification: Critique contradiction 1: std fs/net/process must not justify Layer 1 POSIX shapes; this adr precedes the V1 std crate and forbids std-driven Native ABI entries.

title: Document the C++ SDK binding
justification: C++ at V2 needs a binding guide so the V4 extra-language ecosystem gate is not the first C++ documentation.

title: Publish the Layer 3 semver stability statement for 1.x
justification: 1.0 ABI stability statement covers Layer 1; Layer 3 still evolves with semver and must say so explicitly beside the 1.x support window.

title: Complete SDK guides for Rust and C on the 1.0 release
justification: 1.0 documentation gate: SDK guides for Rust and C complete with the rest of the 1.0 doc set; DOC owns site publishing.

title: Complete Rust and C SDK references for the beta review
justification: V4 exit: user, admin, SDK (Rust and C) references complete with review sign-off and broken-link checks.

title: Write the V1 SDK guide for the published Rust crate
justification: V1 published-SDK gate and DOC IDL-to-docs at V1 need a crate guide covering Context, Operations, Packages and the chooser.

title: Publish SDK guides covering Rust, C and one extra language
justification: V3 documentation gate includes the SDK guide; public alpha strangers need Rust, C and the first extra language documented.

title: Document the unstable V0.5 SDK used by the four native apps
justification: V0.5 scope says the SDK expands to windows, files and packages and remains unstable; the four apps need a crate-level guide before v1.

title: Fuzz SDK handle wrappers for use-after-revoke and double-drop
justification: Layer 3 handle safety is a V1 developer-preview concern; harnesses exercise Capability drop, revoke and Operation cancel without kernel panics.

title: Publish SDK v1 with semver policy and compatibility suite
justification: V1 developer-preview gate: a published stable native SDK with documented versioning and deprecation, verified by the compatibility suite.

title: Study Rust async and Tokio for mapping Operations onto SDK futures
justification: V0 runtime cannot wrap blocking Linux syscalls; this spike informs the executor adr and the tiny native runtime used by the V0 demo.

title: Prototype C++ binding shape over the C ABI and IDL stubs
justification: C++ must not invent a second Native ABI; the spike compares header-only wrappers, generated C++ stubs, and C-only plus thin C++ before the binding ships.

title: Prototype DAP breakpoints inside async Tasks
justification: V1 requires breaking at a source line inside an async Task and showing the logical Task stack; the spike explores runtime hooks before the adapter lands.

title: Measure static versus content-addressed shared-object linking cost
justification: The linking adr needs measured startup sharing before Package emission hardens a loader; cites the B-ID for warm start rather than a prose number.

title: Prototype CPU sample attribution to Task and Component
justification: Sampling must not reconstruct threads; the spike measures attribution cost on the OBS trace substrate before the profiler ships.

title: Write the window, chooser, decode and render SDK tutorial
justification: SDK owns the reference example and API tutorial; DOC publishes the site. V1 SDK v1 gate.

title: Define administrator versus standard user
justification: Pulled to V1 so identity-service can create the first account as administrator and Authorization knows which operations elevate.

title: Scope AI Capability grants to project, file, or time
justification: V2 AI demo: grants are scoped and revocable mid-run; the action graph is logged. Implements the AI-principal adr.

title: Decide whether an AI assistant is a distinct principal
justification: V2 AI demo is capability-only. SEC decides permissioning, scoped grants, and whether the assistant is a distinct principal for audit and revocation, after the SEM registry exists.

title: Test no ambient filesystem, home, device, or app data
justification: V0.5 chooser gate and §9.1/§11: a native app and ImageDecoder start without filesystem, home, device, or other-app data authority.

title: Close High and Critical audit findings
justification: V4 gate: all High and Critical findings fixed; Medium findings triaged with public tracking.

title: Triage Medium audit findings with public tracking
justification: V4 gate requires Medium findings triaged with public tracking, distinct from closing High/Critical code fixes.

title: Re-verify High and Critical fixes with the auditor
justification: V4 gate: High and Critical findings re-verified by the auditor, not only by the authors.

title: Define pluggable authenticator interfaces
justification: GAP-0213 and GAP-0219 require pluggable authenticators so V3 fingerprint/FIDO2 and later directory login can land without rewriting identity.

title: Decide authority sources and precedence
justification: §9.1 needs a single precedence among manifest request, launcher policy, user chooser, permissions UI, and delegation before Packages request Capabilities.

title: Build a re-authentication Authorization service
justification: V1 admin actions need scoped Capabilities after re-auth with an audit record, replacing sudo/polkit.

title: Provide a typed CA trust store with pinning
justification: V1 TLS for Git, cargo, and HTTPS needs a typed system CA store with per-application pinning.

title: Decide disk encryption layer and store interaction
justification: Pulled to V0.5 because encryption choice must precede the STO filesystem adr (snapshots, dedup, content-addressed store). Implementation stays V1. Options include LUKS2/dm-crypt, fscrypt, filesystem-native, or both, without inventing a storage layer.

title: Provide encrypted volumes for developer machines
justification: V1 daily-drive: encryption must exist before a lost laptop is possible. V1 scope allows manual FDE; installer UI is V3.

title: Expose a pre-boot disk-unlock key-slot API
justification: BOOT owns the pre-boot unlock UI; SEC owns key-slots, passphrase verify, and recovery-key unlock consumed at V1 manual FDE.

title: Enable secure-enclave Components if the spike recommends
justification: 1.0 explicitly does not promise hardware confidentiality. Enablement waits on enclaves-study and stays off the 1.0 critical path.

title: Study secure enclaves as a confidentiality home
justification: §8 research: whether SGX/SEV-style enclaves can host Components that need hardware confidentiality. Enablement is LATER; 1.0 does not promise hardware enforcement.

title: Enrol enterprise CAs into the trust store
justification: EXTRA-019 enterprise-CA enrolment for public alpha, without directory login (a 1.0 non-goal).

title: Commission an independent security audit
justification: V4 gate: independent audit of capability enforcement, native ABI, and update pipeline; summary published. GOV GAP-0240 is the broader legal commissioning.

title: Verify installer full-disk encryption and recovery key
justification: V3 installer gate: FDE enabled on Tier 1, recovery key saved, no cloud escrow. INS owns the installer; SEC verifies the encryption contract.

title: Support FIDO2 keys for disk unlock and login
justification: V3 public alpha: FIDO2 hmac-secret as an additional disk-unlock and login factor on the pluggable authenticator interface.

title: Add fingerprint login through pluggable authenticators
justification: GAP-0215 required fingerprint login at V3; greeter UI is APP, so SEC owns the authenticator plugin the greeter consumes.

title: Verify measured-boot generation attestation
justification: V3 Secure Boot/measured-boot gate: generation identity is recorded in the TPM event log. BOOT measures; SEC verifies the security claim.

title: Prove grant revocation takes effect immediately
justification: V2 permissions gate: after revoke, camera, microphone, files, network, and screen capture fail on the next Operation with no leftover mapping.

title: Implement the grant taxonomy in the permission runtime
justification: V0.5 Packages declare RequestedCapabilities; the runtime must enforce the grant-taxonomy adr so chooser, prompt, and settings-only classes are distinct.

title: Decide user-mediated grant taxonomy
justification: Critique: grant taxonomy (chooser, prompt, settings-only; one-time, session, persistent, revocable) must be accepted before the Package capability-request schema.

title: Publish kernel-hardening and unsafe-isolation evidence
justification: V4 gate: exploit mitigations enabled and measured, unsafe-code inventory published, unsafe authority minimized per §51. KRN/BLD produce the data; SEC publishes the security evidence pack.

title: Lock the session with hardware-backed secrets
justification: V3 scope: screen lock with hardware-backed secrets where available, using the secrets service and authenticators.

title: Add hardware-enforcement hooks in Capability checks
justification: §51 hardware layer: design hooks now from the x86-enforcement-study, enable on capable hardware later. Does not freeze an L1 surface.

title: Hide stable hardware identifiers without a Capability
justification: No ambient machine ID, TPM EK, disk serial, or MAC; per-application derived identifiers where needed.

title: Build a capability-gated identity service
justification: V1 daily-driving login: local accounts with Argon2id, no ambient shadow file, typed interfaces only.

title: Implement scoped Inspect capability
justification: V0 os inspect gate must not be ambient: Capability<Inspect> is scoped to a ResourceDomain or Component subtree.

title: Review and deny optional Capabilities at install
justification: V2 store-client gate: capability requests are shown and can be denied at install.

title: Freeze the ambient-authority conformance suite
justification: V4 hardening gate: the §9.1 denial suite is complete, runs on every RC, and is part of the evidence pack.

title: Extend isolation suite to ImageDecoder microphone denial
justification: Audio exists at V1; ImageDecoder must still hold no microphone Capability.

title: Extend isolation suite to ambient camera denial
justification: Camera service exists at V2; a native app must not receive camera access automatically.

title: Deny ambient process enumeration in native Components
justification: V0 isolation demo and §9.1/§11 require a Component, including ImageDecoder, to hold no ambient process-enumeration or network Capability.

title: Build the ambient-authority denial test harness
justification: Critique: §9.1 constraints become lint/test tasks. Shared harness for filesystem, home, device, app-data, and later camera/microphone denials on qemu-x86_64.

title: Support passphrase change and cryptographic erase
justification: Rotate key-slots without re-encrypting; cryptographic erase is the factory-reset primitive.

title: Expose coarse and precise location as Capabilities
justification: V2 sensitive permission: timezone/Wi-Fi geolocation versus precise location as separate Capabilities, with no ambient location.

title: Decide 1.0 multi-user and per-user encryption scope
justification: Must precede V3 multi-user sessions: local account count, fast user switching, concurrent graphical sessions, and per-user home keys.

title: Implement multi-user login with isolated sessions
justification: V3 multi-user gate: two users with separate sessions, Capability stores, and encrypted data. Crosses identity, Session, secrets, and storage.

title: Consume the CA trust store in native TLS
justification: EXTRA-019: native TLS consumes the typed store; an app without the store Capability cannot use default system CAs.

title: Forbid setuid binaries in native Packages
justification: GAP-0220: native Packages contain no setuid binaries; CI lint rejects setuid bits on native artifacts.

title: Declare formal certifications out of scope for 1.0
justification: Nongoal adr: do not pursue Common Criteria or FIPS 140 for 1.0.

title: Declare multi-seat, guest, kiosk, and enterprise directory out of scope
justification: Nongoal adr: no multi-seat, guest, kiosk, LDAP/AD/Kerberos/SSO, Group Policy, or fleet management for 1.0, while authenticators stay pluggable.

title: Encrypt per-user data with keys unlocked at login
justification: Implements the multi-user-scope adr: per-user home data encrypted under keys unlocked at login, required by the V3 two-user encrypted-data gate.

title: Decide permission prompt policy against fatigue
justification: V2 ADR list includes permissions prompt policy. Complements V0.5 grant taxonomy with default, persistence, and anti-fatigue rules for the prompt runtime.

title: Implement trusted permission prompts
justification: V2 prompts for capability requests. GFX owns trusted-UI surfaces; SEC owns prompt state, grant recording, and deny-without-crash behaviour.

title: Ship permissions UI to view and revoke grants
justification: V2 gate: permissions UI lists every active grant and revocation takes effect immediately, tested with camera, microphone, files, network, and screen capture.

title: Add audit history and one-time grants to permissions UI
justification: V3 permissions UI v2: per-application audit history, one-time grants, and compatibility-application grants in the same UI as native apps.

title: Run the permissions UI usability study
justification: V3 gate: a user can see every grant and when it was used, revoke or convert to one-time, with usability-study task completion at least 80 percent.

title: Mirror the CA trust store into personalities
justification: EXTRA-019: native trust store is mirrored into Linux and Windows personality certificate stores so pinning and enrolment apply once.

title: Require saving an offline recovery key
justification: GAP-0198 recovery-key path starts when volumes exist: generate an offline recovery key the user must save; no cloud escrow by default.

title: Decide remote-interface Capability, identity, and encryption rules
justification: Critique parks distribution at LATER. When remote transports exist they must honour Capabilities, endpoint identity, encryption, and explicit user policy, and must not become a kernel concern.

title: Record defence-in-depth and authority-design rules
justification: §51 and Principle 3 collapse into standing lint/review rules: Rust is not sufficient, unsafe is isolated, deny-list sandboxes are not the primary mechanism. Unsafe inventory CI is BLD.

title: Require an explicit screen-share Capability
justification: V0.5 compositor must not grant unrestricted capture; capture exists only as an explicit screen-share Capability. User-facing share UX is V2.

title: Verify screen-share denial on the V2 gate
justification: V2 screen-sharing gate: without the screen-share Capability the app receives a black or denied surface; sharing shows a persistent indicator (GFX).

title: Prove no application can read another app's secrets
justification: GAP-0222 isolation claim needs a gate test: enumerate and read of another Component's secrets return Error::Rights and allocate no handle.

title: Build a per-application secrets service
justification: V1 keyring: each app's secrets are Capability-scoped objects under a per-user key unlocked at login.

title: Verify 1.0 security-posture claims against the threat model
justification: 1.0 definition security posture: no ambient authority, permissions UI, FDE, Secure Boot and measured boot on Tier 1, public threat model, external audit closed, continuous fuzzing, reproducible builds.

title: Implement Session linking identity, seat, and root
justification: V1 identity scope: Session binds user, seat, display, and the session Capability root, with lock, unlock, idle, suspend-inhibit, and end-of-session as typed interfaces.

title: Preserve session state across user switches
justification: V3 multi-user gate: switching sessions preserves state.

title: Publish the microarchitectural side-channel statement
justification: Critique missing-req: state what isolation Capabilities claim, which shared resources are cross-domain channels, and which mitigations are on by default.

title: Back SSH agent and Git credentials with secrets
justification: V1 self-hosting needs Git over SSH without plaintext keys; optional TPM- or FIDO2-resident keys come later.

title: Launch Packages in degraded mode when optional grants are denied
justification: V2 store gate: denying optional Capabilities still launches the application in a declared degraded mode.

title: Decide disk-key eviction on suspend
justification: Pulled to V1 because V1 ships suspend/resume. Decides RAM eviction, re-unlock on resume, suspend-then-hibernate, and whether hibernation is allowed under lockdown.

title: Implement suspend key-eviction and hibernate policy
justification: Implements the V1 suspend-key-eviction adr on laptops, including authenticated hibernation images if lockdown allows hibernate.

title: Refresh the public threat model for 1.0
justification: 1.0 definition requires a public threat model; refresh the V0 document against shipped surfaces and closed audit findings.

title: Publish threat model and threat register
justification: Critique moves the threat model and T-ID register to V0 so every CAP/SEC/BOOT adr cites threats before designs freeze. Names adversaries, assets, trust boundaries, safety layers, and per-Component blast radius.

title: Provide passphrase-only unlock without a TPM
justification: GAP-0190 degraded path: machines without TPM 2.0 unlock with passphrase only and skip measured-boot seals.

title: Expose TPM event log and PCR state via os inspect
justification: Local TPM event log and PCR inspection for understandability; remote attestation is a documented 1.0 non-goal.

title: Decide TPM 2.0 as requirement versus optional
justification: V2 measured boot and sealed keys need a hard-requirement versus optional decision and degraded passphrase-only behaviour on machines without a TPM.

title: Reseal TPM-bound keys across firmware updates
justification: Re-seal before and after firmware updates and Secure Boot key changes so PCR changes do not strand the user at recovery.

title: Seal disk keys to TPM PCRs with a recovery key
justification: V2 FDE: optional PIN, PCR-bound unseal, and a recovery key the user already saved; no cloud escrow by default.

title: Expose TPM only through a capability-gated service
justification: No ambient /dev/tpm0 or tpm2-tss; userspace TPM use is a Capability-gated service.

title: Decide user identity versus Capability roots
justification: Pulled to V0.5 so V1 identity and Session work is not blocked. Decides kernel uid versus userspace identity mapped to Capability roots, and how login becomes the session root holder.

title: Research a WebAuthn platform authenticator
justification: Spike whether the OS should be a WebAuthn/passkey provider backed by TPM and biometrics, and what browser integration that needs, before a V4 provider.

title: Ship a WebAuthn platform authenticator
justification: GAP-0226: a 1.0 desktop without a platform authenticator pushes users to third-party managers. Depends on the V3 spike; drop if the spike rejects it.

title: Evaluate MPK, CET, and LAM for unsafe isolation
justification: Pulled to V1 so V2 hardware-enforcement hooks depend on a done spike. Explores x86-64 MPK/PKU, CET shadow stacks, and LAM for isolating unsafe code inside Components.

title: Demonstrate Workspace.search to IDE.runTests action graph
justification: V2 exit and demo: AI assistant performs 'find yesterday's Postgres branch and run its tests' through Workspace.search → Project Capability → Editor.openProject → Editor.runTests; the graph is logged and one step is revocable (CAP).

title: Implement the AI broker over typed Capabilities
justification: Critique: AI broker after registry and automation. INV-0795/0825/0831: the AI broker obtains typed, permissioned, logged, revocable, scoped Capabilities and composes IDL-only action graphs across applications.

title: Define the typed application event model
justification: INV-0839: apps emit typed events such as Download.completed(file) and Meeting.start over Semantic interfaces; events carry delegated Capabilities, not paths. STO owns file.type.

title: Host the assistant runtime as an ordinary Component
justification: INV-0821/INV-0820: the agent runtime is an ordinary Component with an explicit Capability set, not a privileged process; depends on registry-service, decide-model-execution, and lint-ai-after-registry. No model runtime in the OS.

title: Implement the automation layer over Semantic interfaces
justification: INV-0837/INV-0791: the client runtime that automation and scripting callers use to bind and invoke Semantic interfaces with typed Capabilities; depends on registry-service and interface-capability-grants.

title: Publish Semantic interface registry lookup latency
justification: BEN anti-fake-claim: V2 semantic automation is user-visible, so registry lookup latency is published with no target; harness runs on V2 reference machines beside IPC round-trip.

title: Publish Automation rule dispatch latency
justification: BEN anti-fake-claim: event-to-action latency of the rule engine is published with no target so the V2 automation gate never states an unmeasured number.

title: Build the Semantic interface catalogue conformance suite
justification: V4 L2 lock needs a conformance suite proving catalogue methods, Capability passing, and grant denial; binaries built against the freeze candidate keep running on later beta builds.

title: Prove cross-app integration over Semantic interfaces
justification: INV-0794: two distinct applications discover each other through the registry and complete a typed call with a transferred Capability; permanent integration test on qemu-x86_64 and the V2 desktop.

title: Decide Semantic interface discovery and caller permissioning
justification: GAP-0551: accept one of per-interface Capability grants, manifest-declared exposure with session grants, or a user-consent bind flow before any Semantic interface ships at V1; depends on spike-expose-method.

title: Decide where assistant models execute
justification: INV-0834: choose local ComputeDevice/NPU, remote service, or user-selectable both; reject an OS-bundled model runtime. Depends on spike-model-placement and HET ComputeDevice enumeration.

title: Decide the Automation rule format
justification: INV-0844 and the V2 'automation rules model' ADR: choose declarative rules, a scripting language, or Wasm automation modules; WASM owns a Wasm host if that option wins. Depends on spike-rule-formats.

title: Demonstrate Download.completed to Extractor.extract
justification: V2 exit: first of three shipped example rules runs without GUI input; Download.completed with file.type Archive delegates the file Capability to Extractor.extract.

title: Demonstrate Meeting.start to Notes.create
justification: V2 exit: second shipped example rule; Meeting.start triggers Notes.create(meeting) through typed Capabilities with the action logged.

title: Demonstrate Project opened to environment start
justification: V2 exit names three example rules including 'project opened → start environment'; invokes ENV via a Semantic interface when Editor.openProject succeeds.

title: Publish the 1.x supported Semantic interface catalogue
justification: 1.0 exit: Layer 2 supported interface versions are listed in a published compatibility document with the two-minor-release deprecation policy; SEM authors the Semantic interface pages.

title: Publish Semantic interface authoring guidelines
justification: V1 SDK v1 needs verb/object rules, no-input-synthesis, and Capability-passing idioms for IDL authors; complements IPC interface-design guidelines with the §42 Semantic interface contract.

title: Publish the public-alpha automation and Semantic interface guide
justification: V3 public documentation gate: strangers need a user/SDK guide for Semantic interfaces, Automation rules, and the AI broker; DOC publishes, SEM authors the normative pages.

title: Ship the reference Editor Semantic interface in the native editor
justification: INV-0789: Editor.openProject(Project), searchSymbols(Query) -> Symbol[], and runTests(TestSelection) -> TestRun on the native editor, extending V1 Editor.open for the V2 action-graph demo.

title: Run Layer 2 evolution tests on catalogue Semantic interfaces
justification: V4 exit: old-client/new-service and new-client/old-service pass for every core interface; SEM retains the Editor and Terminal evolution tests as permanent CI.

title: Let applications expose typed Semantic interfaces from IDL
justification: V1 scope 'Semantic interface v0 for Terminal and Editor as proof': applications expose typed Semantic interfaces defined in the native IDL; depends on decide-discovery-permission and IPC idl-semantic-annotations.

title: Expose Semantic interfaces from shipped native UI applications
justification: INV-0774 §41 via §42/§45: shipped native UI applications (shell, four apps, settings) expose Semantic interfaces for automation, not widget scraping; toolkit-level actions stay in UIP.

title: Ship Extractor and Notes fixture Components
justification: V2 example rules name Extractor.extract(file) and Notes.create(meeting); fixture Components expose those Semantic interfaces so the demos do not invent a mail or archive product.

title: Fuzz the registry and Automation rule engine
justification: V3 continuous-fuzzing gate extends to userspace SEM services: registry lookup, grant checks, and rule evaluation have harnesses with no known open crasher older than the kernel fuzz SLA.

title: Demonstrate 1.0 AI-assisted automation with visible Capability grants
justification: 1.0 demo: a working day includes AI-assisted semantic automation with visible Capability grants, then rollback of a package change from os history, on a Tier 1 machine of the release candidate.

title: Record Automation rule changes as system history events
justification: INV-0845 §31: Automation rule creation and changes appear in os history and are restorable with configuration; PKG owns history storage, SEM emits the events.

title: Expose registry, rules, and action graphs to os inspect
justification: V2 exit: the AI demo's action graph is inspectable; SEM registers os inspect providers for the registry, Automation rules, and live graphs. OBS owns audit storage.

title: Require a Capability to invoke another app's Semantic interface
justification: INV-0799: access to another application's Semantic interface requires a Capability granted by the user or policy; implements decide-discovery-permission and fails with Error::Rights and no handle when the grant is absent.

title: Isolate the Semantic interface registry per user
justification: V3 multi-user exit: two users have separate Capability stores; the registry and Automation rules must not leak another user's interfaces or grants across sessions.

title: Gate AI broker crates on a done Semantic interface registry
justification: Enforces §57 and §67 principle 13 from V0: AI broker and assistant-host crates cannot land until a Semantic interface registry task is done, and they must not be omnipotent privileged processes.

title: Forbid input synthesis and GUI scraping in Semantic interface code
justification: Collapses the §42/§45/§67 principle-12 invariants into a V0 CI lint and crate review so no Semantic interface is implemented by synthesising mouse or keyboard input or by GUI scraping; INV-0044 is the same standing rule for AI callers.

title: Lock Semantic interface catalogue versions for 1.x
justification: V4 exit: Layer 2 interface versions for 1.x are enumerated and locked; SEM lists Editor, Terminal, Workspace, Mail, Download, Meeting, Extractor, and Notes versions served for 1.x.

title: Define the reference Mail Semantic interface
justification: INV-0790: catalogue IDL for Mail.search, compose, and reply with a fixture Component; APP parks mail sync for 1.0 so this is the interface hook, not a mail client.

title: Define a transferable Project Capability type
justification: INV-0823: Project is a Capability type transferable among Workspace, Editor, and assistant Components with attenuation and revocation; required before the action-graph demo.

title: Implement the system Semantic interface registry service
justification: Critique ordering: registry before automation and AI. INV-0798 is the system discovery service so one Component finds another application's exposed interfaces; extends registry-v0 with live registration, crash rebind, and manifest ingest.

title: Ship a session-local Semantic interface registry
justification: V1 exit needs lookup of Terminal.run and Editor.open without the V2 system-wide registry service; ACC decide-one-tree-or-two and PKG manifest-semantic-interfaces consume this registry design.

title: Hold only delegated Capabilities in Automation rules
justification: INV-0843: rules hold delegated typed Capabilities from events rather than ambient authority. INV-0847: background rules require Capability<BackgroundExecution> from CAP; missing grant returns Error::Rights.

title: Implement the Automation rule trigger engine
justification: V2 exit 'user-visible rules engine' and INV-0840/INV-1229: evaluate when-event if-condition action rules over the event model; depends on decide-rule-format and app-event-model. Critique: automation before AI broker.

title: Ship Terminal.run and Editor.open Semantic interface v0
justification: V1 exit and typed-automation demo: an automation script invokes Terminal.run and Editor.open through typed interfaces without GUI input; retained as a permanent CI test on qemu-x86_64.

title: Prototype one Editor method as a typed Semantic interface
justification: Critique freeze-before-spike: the V1 gate that an automation script invokes Terminal.run and Editor.open needs a measured Editor-method prototype before decide-discovery-permission; V0.5 scope allows interfaces the four apps need.

title: Prototype local ComputeDevice versus remote model placement
justification: Must precede decide-model-execution; measures a local ComputeDevice/NPU path versus a remote-service path and records that the OS supplies Capability plumbing, not a model runtime.

title: Prototype the Postgres-branch test-run AI scenario
justification: INV-0836 validates the capability-based AI model on 'find the Postgres backup branch and run its tests' before assistant-host and ai-broker; depends on registry-service and editor-ide-interface.

title: Prototype declarative, script, and Wasm Automation rule formats
justification: Must precede decide-rule-format; V2 exit requires an accepted automation-rules-model ADR. Report compares declarative rules, a scripting language, and Wasm automation modules on Terminal.run/Editor.open.

title: Define Workspace.search returning Project Capabilities
justification: INV-0822 is the first hop of the V2 AI action graph; Workspace.search returns Project Capabilities consumed by Editor.openProject. ENV owns os env; SEM owns this Semantic interface.

title: Provide ApplicationData private storage granted by default at launch
justification: Every V0.5 native app needs prompt-free private persistent storage; grant taxonomy from SEC GAP-0227.

title: Implement atomic replacement of a file or tree with no partial reads
justification: Generation switching and settings writes at V0.5 require readers never to observe a partial update.

title: Build encrypted scheduled snapshot-based backup to external and network targets
justification: Critique missing requirement 35; incremental snapshot send with keys in SEC's secrets service.

title: Benchmark snapshot creation and restore time on the three target machines
justification: V2 benchmark gate 'snapshot creation and restore time measured and published'.

title: Benchmark capability-scoped storage object I/O against direct Linux file I/O
justification: BEN register metric INV-1027 (V0.5) measures access through storage objects versus direct Linux file I/O; STO owns the harness that drives its own service, BEN owns methodology and publication.

title: Define Blob as a sealed immutable byte object identified by content hash
justification: Immutable sealed versions and sha256:<hex> style identifiers are needed by packages and generations at V0.5.

title: Define a typed change-notification Operation for File, Directory and Collection
justification: Critique missing requirement 5: IDEs in the V1 L2 corpus need watch semantics; STO ships the Operation and a bridge library that LNX wires to inotify/fanotify.

title: Surface data and metadata checksum failures as typed corruption errors on read
justification: Maps substrate checksum detection into the storage Operation error model so applications and the V2 scrub UX get typed errors.

title: Prove files.choose<Image>() works with no Capability to the containing directory
justification: V0.5 exit: Image Viewer opens a chosen image and cannot enumerate or open any other file in the same directory; retained permanently as a regression test.

title: Ship the 1.0 cloud storage providers with on-demand hydration
justification: Implements decide-storage-provider-interface for the providers chosen for 1.0; feature-complete before V4 feature freeze.

title: Define Collection as a typed user-meaningful group of items independent of layout
justification: §25 Collection; foundation for removable volumes, network shares and cloud providers surfacing as capability-scoped Collections.

title: Deduplicate identical objects across packages, generations and caches
justification: V0.5 exit verifies deduplication by store size.

title: Implement content-store garbage collection with pinning and `os store gc`
justification: Implements decide-store-gc-policy; prevents unbounded store growth under daily-driving at V1.

title: Build the content-addressed object store with reference counting
justification: V0.5 exit: installing a package adds objects to the content-addressed store; two library versions coexist.

title: Recompute hashes on ingest and on verification requests
justification: Integrity on ingest protects the store from V0.5; on-demand verification backs the V1 verity work.

title: Expose copy-on-write clone Operations for files and trees over reflink
justification: CoW and cheap clones over the chosen substrate; needed by snapshots, generations and the V1 environment snapshot.

title: Decide whether BitLocker volumes are readable via user-space dislocker-style support
justification: The decision half of GAP-0431; depends on GOV licensing review of the candidate implementation.

title: Decide replacing the global namespace with capability-scoped storage objects
justification: The §25 model ADR: applications see typed objects, humans keep files and folders through privileged holders (File Browser, chooser); options include per-component roots, object graphs and hybrid path facades for personalities.

title: Decide the content-hash algorithm, identifier format, chunking and upgrade path
justification: V0.5 exit requires an accepted content-addressing ADR before packages and generations are stored.

title: Decide when Write and StorageTransaction data is power-loss safe
justification: Critique missing requirement 7; options include fsync-on-commit, group-commit with bounded window and explicit Durable flag on Write.

title: Decide encryption layering across the verified system store and encrypted user data
justification: Must precede V3 FDE installer; depends on SEC's disk-encryption mechanism decision (GAP-0194, GAP-0527) and states how dedup interacts with encryption.

title: Decide how the storage model degrades on foreign filesystems lacking its metadata
justification: Precedes NTFS and exFAT support: xattr fallback, case-insensitivity, forbidden characters, timestamp precision and permission bits.

title: Decide GPT partition and volume layout for store, generations, user data, swap and recovery
justification: Must be fixed before V0.5 generations exist; includes registered partition type GUIDs so foreign tools identify JakeOS partitions.

title: Decide persistent MemoryObject semantics: storage backing, crash consistency, content addressing
justification: Answers the §16 open question before the persistent property ships; depends on MEM's file-mapping definition (EXTRA-006) and the durability contract.

title: Decide how an application gains authority to create one new file in a user-chosen place
justification: Text Editor at V0.5 must save without directory access; options include chooser-created File capability versus a single-use Capability<Directory, CreateOne>.

title: Decide how configuration and application state become versioned restorable objects
justification: V2 exit restores OS, packages and configuration from the UI; options are a structured settings store (SVC GAP-0278) versus snapshotting ApplicationData.

title: Decide the native storage-provider interface for network and cloud Collections
justification: Scheduled before network-share-providers (V3) and cloud-storage-providers (V4) so both use one provider contract with on-demand hydration.

title: Decide the initial Linux filesystem under the native storage layer
justification: V0.5 exit requires an accepted filesystem-choice ADR; critique contradiction 4 requires ZFS listed as rejected on CDDL licence grounds before measurement; the decision also records the standing rule that no native filesystem is built before 1.0.

title: Decide how the content store maps onto the chosen filesystem without double storage
justification: Depends on decide-storage-substrate and PKG's store layout decision (GAP-0525); chooses hardlinked object directory, reflinked files or filesystem-native dedup.

title: Decide content-store garbage collection: root set, policy and user control
justification: Answers the §27 GC question before the V1 signed repository produces many generations; options include generation-count roots, age-based and user-pinned roots.

title: Decide three-view mapping of user data across native and personalities
justification: Critique folds native Collections versus Linux POSIX home versus Windows C:\Users into STO. personality-view-api is the later API, not the mapping Decision. Options: one object graph with two path facades versus copy-on-first-use versus adopt-in-place per personality. INS migration imports consume the mapping.

title: Decide the platform type registry behind choose<T>, UserSelected<T> and file.type
justification: One decision: where typed object kinds such as Image come from and how they map to content types; answers the V0.5 chooser questions and the V2 automation file.type question early so SEM and SDK share one type system.

title: Define Object<Directory> whose Capability scopes access to its subtree
justification: Required by the File Browser and the temporary-storage and ApplicationData roots at V0.5.

title: Build disk health: TRIM/discard policy and SMART monitoring with notifications
justification: Critique missing requirement 34; runs as a supervised SVC service with typed device capabilities from HW.

title: Provide the StorageSnapshot primitive used by `os env` environments
justification: V1 exit `os env enter` cached p50 target needs pre-created copy-on-write snapshots of project and dependency storage (ENV INV-0657, INV-0662); §35 forbids an overlay stack.

title: Support exFAT and FAT32 removable media with formatting and known limitations
justification: Cameras, SD cards and consoles are exFAT; includes timestamp and character-set limitation surfacing per decide-foreign-fs-degradation.

title: Define Object<File> with Read, Write and metadata Operations and its rights set
justification: Completes the V0 File object into the §7 typed object with async Operations, typed errors and the rights taxonomy used by the chooser.

title: Expose File as a typed kernel object reachable only via Capability<File, Rights>
justification: Critique ordering fix: STO collapses to a single V0 deliverable, a File object sufficient for the V0 exit tests (Capability<File, ReadWrite> derives Read, Admin derivation and forged handles fail, revocation at depth 8, isolation demo typed denial). Raw block/filesystem passthrough only per V0 scope-out.

title: Unlock and mount LUKS, ext4, Btrfs and XFS volumes from other Linux installs
justification: Prerequisite for INS's in-place migration at V3.

title: Provide a content-hash keyed cache API for build outputs, decoded assets and precompiled code
justification: ENV's cached build outputs (INV-0523) and PKG precompiled artefacts (INV-0633) need a shared hash-keyed cache with GC integration.

title: Provide on-demand and boot-time integrity verification of stored objects and generations
justification: §26 integrity verification: `os verify` walks a generation against expected hashes; boot-time check reports to BOOT's boot counter.

title: Version the on-disk layout and migrate V3 installs in place
justification: V4 exit: in-place upgrade of V3 installs with data preserved and rollback to V3 possible requires a versioned partition and store layout with a migration step.

title: Provide per-user storage roots and separately encrypted user volumes
justification: V3 exit: two users with separate sessions and separate encrypted data; SEC decides the multi-user model (GAP-0218), STO provides the volume and key-slot layout under decide-encryption-layering.

title: Support SMB, NFS and WebDAV as foreign network filesystems
justification: Critique MIG/STO fold: foreign and network filesystems are STO, not NET. Capability-scoped mounts, not a global FHS.

title: Provide SMB, NFS, WebDAV and SFTP shares as storage-provider Collections
justification: Home NAS and office shares surfaced in the chooser and File Browser with credentials in the secrets service.

title: Retain in-kernel NTFS read/write with dirty-volume and ACL mapping policy
justification: Dual-boot shared data partitions; INS owns the Fast Startup guidance (GAP-0406), STO owns the driver retention and mapping into the native layer.

title: Implement the partition and volume layout library used by the image builder
justification: Critique places the image builder at V0.5 (INS); STO supplies the layout, mkfs and subvolume creation library and its idempotency tests.

title: Enforce no path-based authority and no default filesystem namespace with lint and tests
justification: Invariants collapse into one enforcement task: a lint rejecting native authority checks keyed on paths and a conformance test that a freshly created Component holds no filesystem namespace; first matters when the V0 File object exists.

title: Implement the persistent MemoryObject property backed by durable storage
justification: Implements decide-persistent-memory-object; jointly tested with MEM's mapping coherence.

title: Expose a capability-scoped view API for personalities to synthesise path namespaces
justification: LNX INV-0856 and INV-0493 synthesise POSIX paths and drive letters over native storage; STO must supply the scope-preserving API before V1 browser and IDE file access, without making paths a native authority.

title: Prove the durability contract with a fault-injected power-cut test on NVMe
justification: Depends on decide-durability-contract; uses LAB's power-control rig on the reference desktop and QEMU device-reset injection in CI.

title: Provide filesystem repair and store consistency check from the recovery environment
justification: Third part of EXTRA-035; ships inside INS's resident recovery generation (GAP-0205) and repairs substrate and store metadata.

title: Surface removable and MTP volumes as consented Collections with automount and safe eject
justification: USB sticks, SD cards and phones appear only as user-consented capability-scoped Collections; /media and drive letters exist only inside personalities via personality-view-api.

title: Make `os restore` revert user data through storage snapshots
justification: §31 restore of user data; PKG owns generation restore, STO owns the user-data revert and pre-restore safety snapshot.

title: Inventory retained Linux storage drivers and filesystems with divergence status
justification: Collapses the six retain/preserve items (NVMe, SATA, mature filesystems, storage drivers) into one inventory listing each mechanism, its Phase A-E fate and the personality that depends on it; feeds KRN's whole-kernel retained-mechanism inventory.

title: Verify rollback preserves user data by fault injection on every Tier 1 machine
justification: 1.0 exit: rollback preserves user data on every Tier 1 machine under a fault-injected failing generation; INS/PKG/BOOT own the generation flip, STO owns the user-data assertion.

title: Implement the save-as grant so an application creates one file without directory access
justification: Implements decide-save-as-flow for the V0.5 Text Editor acceptance scenario.

title: Take scheduled user-data snapshots with a retention policy
justification: Browse-and-restore and Trash need a snapshot history; retention bounded by storage-quotas.

title: Schedule checksum scrubs and report corruption to the user with recovery actions
justification: Second half of EXTRA-035; turns checksum-corruption-errors into a user-facing UX with snapshot-based recovery suggestions.

title: Provide a consent-scoped file content index provider for desktop search
justification: Storage half of desktop search (APP EXTRA-044 owns the service and launcher): indexes only granted Collections, driven by change-notification Operations, with no ambient home access per §9.

title: Expose subtree and system-volume snapshot Operations
justification: V0.5 scope: storage model over a mature CoW filesystem with snapshots; consumed by PKG generations.

title: Measure btrfs, bcachefs and XFS-reflink on snapshots, clones, checksums, dedup and crash safety
justification: Precedes decide-storage-substrate; uses BEN's filesystem harness (INV-0507) and adds crash-consistency runs; ZFS appears only as a licence-excluded reference row.

title: Define and re-evaluate the criteria that would justify a native filesystem or object store
justification: §26 and §57: measured semantic gaps and performance shortfalls recorded against the substrate at each gate; no build task is planned before 1.0.

title: Write L1 conformance tests for File, Directory, Blob and StorageTransaction entry points
justification: V4 exit: every Layer 1 entry point has a conformance test before the freeze ADR; storage objects are L1 surfaces.

title: Close external audit findings in the storage service, store and chooser authority
justification: V4 exit: all High and Critical audit findings fixed and re-verified; storage mediation is in the audit scope.

title: Write the storage user and administrator guides for 1.0
justification: 1.0 documentation exit: user and administrator guides must cover snapshots, quotas, backup, foreign and network volumes and the chooser model; DOC owns the pipeline, STO authors the content.

title: Add `os inspect storage` and trace events for storage Operations and snapshots
justification: V1 exit requires `os trace` export of a session and the debugger to show async Operations; storage Operations and snapshot events must appear in OBS's schema.

title: Add old-client/new-service versioning tests for every storage L2 interface
justification: V1 freezes L2 evolution rules (critique freeze-before-spike); storage interfaces are SDK v1 freeze candidates and need the interface-evolution test the V4 gate later requires.

title: Enumerate and lock storage L2 interface versions for 1.x
justification: V4 exit: Layer 2 interface versions for 1.x are enumerated and locked with the evolution test passing for every core interface.

title: Provide storage quotas per user and per ResourceDomain as typed objects
justification: Critique missing requirement 33; quota objects consumed by APP's settings UI and SCH's ResourceDomain budgets.

title: Add NVMe, SATA and ext4/btrfs/xfs/vfat regression tests to the CI matrix
justification: Second of the two permitted retain-item tasks: boot and I/O tests on virtio and the reference desktop NVMe/SATA plus mount and LTP filesystem subsets for the four retained filesystems, so V0 'Linux compatibility intact' covers storage.

title: Build the user-space storage service mediating capability-scoped access to the substrate
justification: The §4 user-space Storage service; hosts every storage object below and is supervised by SVC.

title: Write the storage threat analysis: chooser spoofing, TOCTOU across snapshots, store poisoning
justification: SEC's V0 threat model (GAP-0540) requires storage designs to cite the threats they address before being fixed; this feeds the V0.5 storage ADRs and the threat register.

title: Add the StorageTransaction Operation kind with commit and abort completion
justification: §18 Operation kind; V0.5 delivers single-volume atomic grouping used by package install and generation build, coordinated with TSK's Operation model and ABI's Operation-kind decision (INV-0357).

title: Complete multi-object StorageTransaction with all-or-nothing commit across trees
justification: §26 transactions backing the §18 Operation; V1 generation updates from the signed repository and `os restore` rely on grouped atomic changes.

title: Add a filesystem-diff test that package install writes nothing outside the store
justification: V0.5 exit criterion 'installing a package adds it to the content-addressed store without writing outside the store; verified by filesystem diff' has no owning item; PKG performs the install, STO owns the diff harness over its volumes.

title: Apply verity to the immutable system store with the root hash in the signed manifest
justification: V1 exit: packages are content-addressed, signed and verified before activation; completes the firmware-to-userspace chain with PKG (manifest), BOOT (measured boot) and REL (signing).

title: Provide the component-scoped temporary-storage Capability granted at launch
justification: §9.1 launch capability set (UI, GPU, temporary-storage); reclaimed with the Component.

title: Decide how user data maps across native, Linux home and Windows profile views
justification: Critique MIG fold: native Collections, POSIX home and C:\Users mapping. STO owns the objects; LNX/WIN present views; INS migrates.

title: Implement Trash and undo-delete on storage snapshots
justification: V2 desktop preview expects a recycle bin; built on snapshot-operations rather than a hidden directory.

title: Deduplicate identical content in user data with an idle-intent reflink pass
justification: §26 deduplication beyond the content store; runs as a Background-intent component within SCH budgets.

title: Implement UserSelected<T> and the chooser grant returning Capability<Image, ReadWrite>
justification: Authority side of the OS-owned chooser (APP INV-0487 owns the UI): mints the narrow capability, records the audit event, returns the typed object to the SDK call.

title: Provide the snapshot catalog and restore Operations behind browse-and-restore UI
justification: V2 exit: snapshots and rollback in the settings UI; APP renders, STO owns the catalog, diff and restore of user data and application state.

title: Benchmark the init-to-session service startup timeline on Tier 1 machines
justification: V3 benchmark gate publishes boot time to login per Tier 1 machine beside mainline Linux; this harness publishes the init and service critical path (dependency waits, readiness latency per service) as the SVC-attributable share of that number, so tuning is measured rather than claimed.

title: Benchmark supervisor death-detection to ready latency for a restarted service
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate 'compositor restart-to-rebound time measured' cites a B-ID owned by BEN (INV-0611); this harness publishes the supervisor-side component (death detection, respawn, readiness) so the BEN number can be decomposed and regressions attributed.

title: Run the compositor and one other service under supervision and pass the restart gate
justification: Verifies the V0.5 gate 'killing the compositor restarts it and rebinds all open windows, 100 consecutive times on QEMU and 20 on hardware' plus a second service (file chooser) as §60 requires; GFX owns the surface rebind, SVC owns the supervision and the CI loop.

title: Decide monotonic versus wall-clock semantics for Operation deadlines across suspend
justification: One decision: which clock Operation deadlines and timers use and whether suspended time counts (CLOCK_MONOTONIC- vs CLOCK_BOOTTIME-like), plus the wall-clock step notification contract. V1 introduces suspend/resume on the Intel laptop; TSK implements the chosen semantics.

title: Decide the default-application registry and open-by-Capability model
justification: Critique folds the SYS default-app registry into SVC as a headless typed service; V0.5 opens files only via the UserSelected chooser, so the decision sits at V1 with daily-driving. One decision: how STO typed kinds and URL schemes map to a handler Package, how user defaults override Package offers, and how open mints a Capability to only that object. Options: user-chosen default per kind/scheme with Package handler candidates; shared MIME/xdg-data database (path-based, rejected by the gap rationale); always-ask chooser with remembered last choice only.

title: Decide native init versus retained initramfs/systemd for early boot
justification: Resolves critique contradiction 2 for V0.5: V0 boots native components beside a retained initramfs (BOOT EXTRA-046); this ADR decides whether native init takes over from the first instruction after the kernel, after root-store unlock, or after a systemd handoff. Blocks init-core.

title: Decide how a service Component reports readiness and liveness to the supervisor
justification: One decision: readiness signalling (explicit ready notification over a supervisor Channel vs interface-advertised-means-ready vs probe-based) and liveness (heartbeat vs kernel death notification only). Dependency-ordered startup and rebind timing in supervisor-core cannot be built without it.

title: Decide restart budgets, strategies, backoff and escalation for supervised services
justification: One decision: the restart policy model (per-service budget window, strategy, exponential backoff bounds, escalation target when the budget is exhausted). The V0.5 compositor-restart gate (100 consecutive restarts) and the V2 safe-mode escalation both depend on it. Options: BEAM-style strategies, systemd StartLimit semantics, Fuchsia eager/lazy restart.

title: Decide the settings storage model: typed schema-versioned objects with history events
