justification: One decision: how settings are stored (typed schema-versioned objects in a settings service vs per-application files vs registry-style store) and how changes become system history events restorable by `os restore`. Needed before the four V0.5 apps invent config formats; PKG INV-0535 forbids registry-style global configuration.

title: Decide whether to retain chrony or build a native NTP/NTS client
justification: The decision named in GAP-0288. Options: chrony hosted as a supervised personality service, a native Rust NTS client Component, or systemd-timesyncd-class minimal client. Must precede time-service in the same rung.

title: Build the default-application registry that opens files by Capability
justification: Implements the default-application ADR: a supervised service that resolves the user-chosen handler for a typed kind or URL scheme from Package handler declarations, persists defaults in the settings store, and launches the handler with a Capability to just that object. APP File Browser and launcher consume the interface; PKG-@manifest-handler-declarations remains the manifest side; Linux xdg-open and portals stay in LNX.

title: Emit typed degraded-recovery events when seamless restart is impossible
justification: §32: where hardware or driver constraints prevent seamless recovery, degraded recovery must still be explicit. Supervisor publishes typed events (service lost, degraded, recovered) into the OBS audit/log path and to subscribed shells; prerequisite for the V2 shell indicators and safe-mode escalation.

title: Write the guide for authoring a supervised service with rebind and restore-state
justification: V1 SDK v1 and IDL guidelines (IPC) need the service-side counterpart: how to declare a manifest, signal readiness, design disconnect/rebind/retry/restore-state per §32, and choose a restart policy; reviewed with DOC and cited by the V3 SDK guide.

title: Host user-space driver Components under supervision with per-device restart
justification: Workstream scope 'user-space driver hosting' and §33: HW INV-0613 builds the driver framework and INV-0626 re-issues device Capabilities; SVC provides the driver host that launches driver Components from packages, supervises each device instance, and escalates exhausted budgets to an explicit degraded-device state.

title: Build the early-boot init stage for verity setup and root-store unlock
justification: The early-userspace ADR rationale names disk unlock and verity setup as early-boot work; V1 allows manually configured encryption and V3 gates FDE in the installer. This stage runs before the content store is available, prompts for unlock through a minimal UI and hands over to init-core.

title: Build the hostname and machine-identity settings service
justification: Workstream scope names hostname; V1 networking (DHCP, DNS) and V2 NET mDNS (GAP-0435) need a typed hostname/pretty-name/machine-id object exposed to native services and to the Linux personality's /etc/hostname view.

title: Build the native init Component that starts the supervisor from a SystemGeneration
justification: Replaces systemd for the native world per the early-userspace ADR: mounts the content store of the selected SystemGeneration, seeds the root Capability set, starts the supervisor, owns reboot/halt. Required by the V0.5 exit criterion 'compositor starts from a system generation' and the generation-rollback boot test.

title: Build the system locale, keyboard-layout and timezone settings service
justification: Workstream scope names locale; TXT GAP-0257 decides locale data (ICU/CLDR) at V1 and V2 gates a localisation framework with three shell languages, so the system-wide typed Locale settings and their projection into personality environments (LANG, /etc/localtime) must exist at V1.

title: Support concurrent per-user session trees with switching that preserves services
justification: V3 exit criterion: two users with separate sessions and separate Capability stores, switching preserves state. Extends session-supervision-tree to multiple concurrent sessions with per-user settings scopes and greeter handoff owned by APP.

title: Supervise Linux-personality daemons as services with the same restart semantics
justification: V1 ships the Linux personality as a product with D-Bus, PipeWire, XWayland and portals; LNX GAP-0506 decides the systemd-emulation level, SVC provides the adapter that runs a personality process as a supervised service with readiness, restart budgets and degraded events so CMP INV-1301 holds for them too.

title: Implement readiness and liveness signalling in the native service runtime
justification: Runtime-side implementation of the readiness ADR: a service reports ready over its supervisor Channel, dependents start only after readiness, liveness loss triggers the restart policy. Shipped as an SDK runtime module jointly with SDK; the supervisor side lives here.

title: Fall back to a text recovery console offering previous-generation boot when safe mode fails
justification: V3 gate: recovery environment restores a system whose current generation is corrupted, and automatic rollback on a failing generation. INS owns the separately booted recovery environment; SVC owns init's last-resort console when no compositor can start, offering rollback and handoff to that environment.

title: Re-advertise interfaces after restart so clients rebind by interface identity
justification: On service death the supervisor restarts the Component and re-registers its interfaces in the IPC service registry (IPC INV-0609) so SDK clients (SDK INV-0601/0602) rebind and retry; defines the disconnect/rebind/retry/restore-state contract of §32 from the supervisor side.

title: Run the §32 restartable-service matrix on every target machine
justification: §32 lists compositor, audio, network, Bluetooth, printing, device-management and GPU userspace services as restartable; V2 gates Bluetooth stack crash recovery without reboot. This task registers each service in a hardware CI matrix that kills it and verifies rebind or explicit degraded recovery, complementing BLD's chaos suite.

title: Escalate exhausted shell or compositor restart budgets to the safe-mode session
justification: Supervisor policy and fault-injection test: when the shell or compositor exhausts its restart budget the session tree is torn down and the safe-mode session starts instead of a restart loop; verified on the three V2 target machines.

title: Build the safe-mode session with settings, log export and `os restore`
justification: Minimal recovery shell running on a minimal compositor configuration, offering settings reset, log bundle export via the system log service, and `os restore` to a previous generation or settings point; the V2 rung named by the critique for the safe-mode session.

title: Expose service control and supervision-tree state via `os service` and `os inspect`
justification: V0.5 gate and BLD GAP-0132 fault injection need a controlled kill/restart/status path for services; the critique moves OBS `os inspect` kinds beyond the six V0 ones to V0.5, so SVC supplies the supervision-tree data (state, restart counts, budget remaining) for `os inspect service`.

title: Lock the service manifest and settings schema versions for 1.x
justification: V4 gate: Layer 2 interface versions for 1.x are enumerated and locked with old-client/new-service tests. The service manifest, settings object schema and supervisor control interface are SVC-owned Layer 2 surfaces that must be listed, tested and locked here.

title: Define the service manifest: capabilities, dependencies, restart policy, readiness
justification: Layer 2 schema declaring a system service as a Component with requested Capabilities, dependency edges, restart policy, readiness kind and ResourceDomain; embedded in the PKG package manifest so no service is configured outside the immutable store (PKG INV-0535/0537). State prototyped; versioning follows IPC L2 rules.

title: Add a CI lint requiring restart/rebind on every service interface
justification: INV-1301 is Principle 10 as a standing invariant, collapsed to a lint rather than a V0 task: services do not exist until V0.5. CI fails when a supervised service's IDL or manifest omits disconnect, rebind, retry and restore-state plus a restart policy. First enforced on the V0.5 compositor, settings and supervisor Interfaces. IPC already owns the client-side guideline (INV-0591); this lint is the service-side gate.

title: Build per-user session supervision trees under the system supervisor
justification: V1 introduces single-user login and session lock (SEC) and V2 APP session management (GAP-0283) needs session-scoped services (shell, panel, agents) that die with the session and restart independently of system services; separates system and session supervision scopes.

title: Provide the per-application settings interface and client crate for the SDK
justification: IDL interface and Rust client for typed, schema-versioned per-application settings with change subscriptions, shipped in SDK v1 so native apps stop inventing config files; SDK owns packaging, SVC owns the interface and service side.

title: Record settings changes as system history events and restore them via `os restore`
justification: V1 exit criterion: `os restore` restores kernel, packages and system configuration; PKG owns `os history` v1 (INV-0587), SVC feeds settings change events and implements the configuration restore path from a history point.

title: Verify by fault injection that rollback and `os restore` preserve and restore settings
justification: 1.0 definition (3): `os history` and `os restore` cover OS, packages and configuration and rollback never loses user data. Adds the configuration leg to the INS/PKG fault-injection run on every Tier 1 machine, with results published in the release notes.

title: Build the settings service storing typed, schema-versioned settings objects
justification: Implements the settings ADR: a supervised service holding per-system and per-application settings as typed objects with schema migration, change notification, and Capability-scoped access (an app reads only its own scope). Emits change events later consumed by PKG system history.

title: Implement ordered shutdown, reboot and generation-switch sequencing in init
justification: V1 exit criteria require reboot into a new generation and `os restore`; init must stop services in reverse dependency order with bounded timeouts, honour inhibitors surfaced by APP GAP-0283, flush storage and hand off to the BOOT generation switch. Nothing else owns the transition.

title: Study BEAM and Fuchsia supervision to shape restart strategies
justification: Report comparing Erlang/BEAM supervision trees, Fuchsia component manager restart policies and systemd restart units; recommends strategy set (one-for-one, rest-for-one, one-for-all), escalation and backoff shapes. Must precede decide-restart-policy; CMP INV-1146 covers the V0 TaskGroup angle, this covers the service angle.

title: Ship the supervision conformance suite run on every Tier 1 machine per RC
justification: V4 gate: every Tier 1 machine passes the full hardware test suite each RC with zero P0/P1. Turns the restartable-service matrix, safe-mode escalation and watchdog escalation into a conformance suite with published per-machine results, exercised in both RC cycles.

title: Build the service supervisor with dependency-ordered start and restart policies
justification: Supervision tree that instantiates services from manifests as Components with declared Capabilities, orders startup by dependencies and readiness, applies the decided restart policy, and records typed exit causes from CMP EXTRA-004. The layer §32 requires and the V0.5 compositor-restart gate exercises.

title: Build the structured log collection service for system and session services
justification: Core system service in workstream scope: collects structured log records from supervised services with per-service retention and Capability-gated read, in the OBS crash-capture/trace format; required by V1 daily-driving debugging and by the V2 safe-mode session's log export (EXTRA-016).

title: Build the time service: NTP/NTS sync, RTC synchronisation, clock-step events
justification: Supervised service implementing the time-sync ADR, syncing the RTC, exposing a Capability-gated set-time interface and broadcasting clock-step events so TLS, package signature verification and deadlines behave; timezone auto-detection is deferred to V2 with the SEC location service.

title: Add timezone auto-detection via the location Capability and the time settings interface
justification: Completes GAP-0288 once SEC GAP-0289 ships the coarse-location Capability at V2: the time service derives the timezone from it with user override, and exposes the typed date/time settings interface the APP Settings date/time panel (GAP-0279) binds to.

title: Wire kernel watchdog and hung-task signals into supervisor escalation
justification: KRN EXTRA-012 retains hardware watchdog, softlockup and hung-task detection and wires them to the service supervisor; SVC side pets the hardware watchdog from init, treats hung-task reports as liveness loss, and escalates repeated failures to reboot into the previous SystemGeneration.

title: Add async-by-default ABI review gate and blocking-syscall lint
justification: Standing rules enforced once: CI lint rejects native entry points whose primary mode blocks, any read()/write() thread-per-call surface, signal-style notification, or runtime async layers bypassing kernel Operations.

title: Publish Operation, deadline and cancellation guidelines for service authors
justification: V1 developer preview: guidelines on when to add an Operation kind versus a Channel method, deadline conventions and the cancellation contract callers may observe, complementing IPC's interface design guidelines.

title: Maintain logical async Task stacks and await chains for debugger and profiler
justification: V1 exit: debugger breaks inside an async Task and shows the logical Task stack; profiler attributes samples to Task and Component; the runtime records parent/await relationships that OBS and SDK tools read.

title: Require an explicit Capability for Tasks that outlive their TaskGroup
justification: §21: persistent background execution requires an explicit capability and no accidental orphans; first needed when native init and SVC-supervised services appear at V0.5; enforces CMP's INV-0392 invariant from the Operation/Task side.

title: Benchmark per-Operation deadline overhead at high submission rates and publish
justification: Makes the spike's measurement a permanent regression harness under BEN's anti-fake-claim policy before the V1 Linux compatibility overhead gate (within 5%) is judged.

title: Benchmark submit-to-completion wake-up latency and publish
justification: Turns the spike's one-off wake-up measurement into a permanent harness (same-core, cross-core, single vs batched) so V0.5/V1 regression gates and the V1 IPC p50 ≤ 2 µs target rest on a registered metric, not a claim.

title: Benchmark native Task handoff against Linux thread switch and publish
justification: V0 benchmark gate 'context-switch behaviour (native Task handoff vs Linux thread switch) measured and published'; publish-only at V0 per critique, registered with BEN methodology.

title: Harden shared submission/completion memory against forgery, TOCTOU and exhaustion
justification: SEC threat model at V0 names shared rings as an attack surface; before external developers submit Operations at V1 the kernel must validate user-writable entries once, bound outstanding work and reject forged completions.

title: Preserve Operation deadlines correctly across suspend and resume
justification: Implements the suspend/resume rule from decide-deadline-representation on the Intel laptop; V1 gate of 200/200 suspend cycles with functional services requires Timers and deadlines to behave predictably after wake.

title: Decide Task cancellation model and resource cleanup
justification: V0 exit cancels a TaskGroup and never delivers a result from a cancelled Operation. Decides cooperative versus forced versus staged-with-grace-deadline cancellation, cleanup of Capabilities, MemoryObjects and partial ownership, and interaction with uninterruptible inherited Linux paths. The ADR report studies Trio nurseries, Kotlin coroutine scopes and Swift task groups (INV-1149) rather than a separate V0 research spike.

title: Decide deadline and timestamp representation in the Operation ABI
justification: Clock domain, resolution, overflow horizon and suspend/resume behaviour of deadlines are stamped into every Operation; must precede operation-kinds-timer-wait and operation-cancel-deadline.

title: Decide whether Operations may complete inline at submit and how the ABI signals it
justification: Cached reads and already-signalled Waits force this ABI-visible choice before submit-complete-path is built.

title: Decide which Operation ABI surfaces become Layer 1 freeze candidates
justification: Critique: L1 freeze candidates at V1 with SDK v1, frozen at V4; names the submission entry, completion record layout, result encoding, deadline representation and kind set that enter the ABI snapshot check.

title: Decide native expression of termination, cancellation and async notification without signals
justification: Signals have no native equivalent; the adr specifies Operation completion, typed Channel messages and Wait-able objects as the notification model and records the rejected signal-like options.

title: Decide how Operation priority relates to ResourceDomain scheduling intent
justification: Whether priority is inherited from the owning domain's intent, per-Operation override bounded by the domain, or independent; needed before the kernel orders I/O and IPC by it and before SCH's Interactive/Background classes land at V0.5.

title: Decide Operation submission/completion transport and batching expression
justification: One decision: rings vs per-Component queues vs syscall-per-Operation vs hybrid, io_uring internals reused or replaced, and how batches are expressed; depends on spike-completion-transport; S-state prototyped, freeze candidate at V1.

title: Decide Operation ownership transfer semantics across Tasks and TaskGroups
justification: operation-object gives every Operation an owner; this decides what transfer means for completion delivery, cancellation and accounting, needed before service-restart-inflight-ops re-owns work during rebind.

title: Decide how personality threads map onto native Tasks
justification: INV-0386 is a V1 question: how Linux and Windows personality threads map onto native Tasks and execution contexts. Needed before V1 daily-driving through LNX and non-gated Wine bring-up. TSK owns the native side of the mapping; LNX and WIN consume it. Personalities are out of V0 scope.

title: Decide whether every Task has kernel-visible identity
justification: Orthogonal to the multiplexing model: every Task is Object<Task>, runtime identity with kernel visibility only for observability and cancellation, or a hybrid. The Task ABI must not embed x86-specific execution-context assumptions (§38). Depends on spike-task-multiplexing; freeze candidate at V1.

title: Decide Task mapping onto kernel execution contexts
justification: Required V0 architectural ADR: replace the thread model with Task/TaskGroup (INV-0071) and fix the kernel/runtime split (INV-0380). Options are complete models that each state how unexpected kernel blocking is compensated (GAP-0493): kernel-managed Tasks, UMCG-style activations with compensating workers, or pure userspace async syscalls. Surface prototyped, not frozen.

title: Implement a native Event object signalled by user space and consumed via Wait
justification: Realises decide-native-notification: the replacement for futex/eventfd/signal wake-ups that the toolkit, compositor and Wayland bridge need for cross-Task synchronisation without ambient signals.

title: Verify cancellation state machine against NVMe, GPU and Wi-Fi on all target machines
justification: The V0 spike covered one NVMe path on one desktop; V2's three target machines add laptops, Wi-Fi and GPUs, so the committed-work contract must be exercised per hardware class in CI.

title: Write Layer 1 reference pages for every Operation kind, result and completion record
justification: V3 exit requires 100% Layer 1 reference documentation; DOC generates from IDL but the Operation semantics, result codes and cancellation observability text are TSK-authored.

title: Implement batched submission and linked Operation chains
justification: decide-operation-transport fixes how batches are expressed; this implements batch submit and io_uring-style links (Read then Send, Timer-bounded chains) that the compositor frame loop and File Browser need at V0.5.

title: Implement Operation cancellation and deadline expiry with Cancelled and DeadlineExceeded results
justification: Owner cancel and deadline expiry deliver through the normal completion path, cancelling a TaskGroup cancels every Operation it owns, and the committed-hardware state machine from spike-uncancellable-operations is implemented for the NVMe path; V0 exit: a cancelled Operation never delivers a result.

title: Build Layer 1 conformance suite for the frozen Operation ABI
justification: V4 exit: L1 frozen with conformance suite; covers every kind, inline-completion signalling, deadline representation and cancellation results named by decide-l1-freeze-candidates.

title: Build continuous fuzzing harness for Operation submission and completion
justification: V3 exit: continuous syscall and IPC fuzzing; TSK supplies the grammar and oracle for submit, batch, link, cancel and deadline paths on BLD's fuzzing infrastructure.

title: Implement DeviceOperation kind for Object<Device> including user-space drivers
justification: Asynchronous requests to devices backed by kernel or SVC-hosted user-space drivers; the V0.5 compositor drives DRM/KMS through it.

title: Implement GPUDispatch Operation kind with committed-work cancellation
justification: §18 lists GPUDispatch and the V2 ComputeDevice demo dispatches to CPU and GPU; extends the uncancellable-work state machine to submitted GPU work with HET owning ComputeDevice semantics.

title: Implement StorageTransaction Operation kind over the storage durability contract
justification: §18 lists StorageTransaction; STO's durability contract lands at V1 with system history and os env snapshots, and the async transaction kind is the TSK-owned plumbing for it.

title: Implement Connect and Accept Operation kinds
justification: Connection establishment to services and listening objects needed by compositor clients and service rebind; NetworkConnection objects arrive with NET at V1 over the same kinds.

title: Implement Read, Write, Send and Receive Operation kinds
justification: Read/Write against File, Channel and MemoryObject-backed objects plus typed Send/Receive on Channel<T> in coordination with IPC's fast path; required by the V0 §59 demo and exit criteria.

title: Implement Timer and Wait Operation kinds
justification: Timer completes at or after an absolute or relative deadline in the representation decided by decide-deadline-representation; Wait completes when a referenced object or set reaches a signalled state; both are V0 exit kinds.

title: Implement Operation<Result> kernel object with owner, typed result, priority and trace points
justification: The first-class unit of outstanding work: owner Task or TaskGroup for structural cancellation, typed Result or failure, priority field carried for later ordering, tracing hooks consumed by OBS; identity/handle encoding comes from ABI INV-0373.

title: Order I/O, IPC and wake-up by Operation priority
justification: Plumbs the carried priority into block I/O ordering, Channel queueing and completion wake ordering per decide-operation-priority-model so the compositor's Operations preempt Background work (V0.5 zero-dropped-frames gate).

title: Charge outstanding Operations and completion queue memory to the owning ResourceDomain
justification: §19 lists resource accounting as an Operation property; in-flight Operations and ring slots must count against SCH's kernel-object limits so a runaway component cannot exhaust kernel memory once multiple apps run at V0.5.

title: Audit Operation surfaces for the 1.0 ABI stability statement
justification: 1.0 definition item (1): confirms every Operation kind and result code is in the frozen L1 statement or a versioned L2 interface with deprecation policy, and lists async non-promises (no distributed Operations).

title: Document how language runtimes bind to kernel Operations
justification: SDK v1 and C bindings ship at V1; the guide specifies waker, completion record and cancellation contracts so Rust, C and later runtimes bind to Operations rather than reinventing async I/O.

title: Complete in-flight Operations against a restarted service with typed Disconnected results
justification: V0.5 exit: killing the compositor rebinds all windows with no application exit; outstanding Send/Receive/DeviceOperation work against the dead instance must fail typed and be resubmittable, coordinated with SVC supervision and IPC rebind.

title: Prototype Operation submission/completion transports and measure wake-up latency
justification: Studies io_uring rings, linked operations and cancellation, then prototypes shared ring, per-Task wait object and hybrid completion delivery on QEMU and the reference desktop with wake-up latency measured for each; feeds decide-operation-transport (critique: L1 spikes explicit in V0, freeze nothing).

title: Prototype in-kernel deadline enforcement and measure per-Operation overhead
justification: Timer wheel vs hrtimer per Operation measured at high submission rates before the Timer kind and deadline path are built.

title: Prototype Task multiplexing models and measure hidden blocking
justification: Critique keeps the UMCG/scheduler-activations study among the six V0 spikes that inform L1 surfaces. Prototypes kernel-notified user scheduling, a pure userspace runtime with async syscalls only, and kernel-managed lightweight Tasks at the §20 live-Task scale, and measures how page faults and synchronous driver paths stall a worker. Feeds decide-task-mapping; freeze nothing.

title: Prototype cancellation state machine for hardware-committed Operations on NVMe
justification: Answers whether cancel waits, fails or is best-effort for in-flight DMA/GPU/network work and how partial results are reported, prototyped against a real NVMe read on the reference desktop; feeds operation-cancel-deadline.

title: Implement submit(Operation), completion delivery and poll/wait in the native ABI
justification: Builds the transport chosen by decide-operation-transport and decide-inline-completion; submit returns without waiting and completions report results back to the submitting Task (V0 exit: async submission/completion works).

title: Tune Task multiplexing with per-core completion affinity and work distribution
justification: V1 targets IPC p50 ≤ 2 µs same-core and ≤ 5 µs cross-core and V0 benchmarks must not regress; completion affinity, wake batching and idle-Task memory footprint are the TSK levers, measured by bench-operation-completion and bench-task-handoff.

title: Implement Task multiplexing across bounded execution contexts
justification: §20: kernel and runtime multiplex Tasks across a bounded set of execution contexts so native software can create enormous numbers of Tasks without kernel threads. Implements the model chosen by decide-task-mapping, including hidden-blocking compensation. Existing task-multiplexing-wake then wires Operation completion onto this multiplexer; V1 task-multiplexer-tuning is out of scope.

title: Integrate Operation completion with Task suspension and wake on execution contexts
justification: §18 completion integrates directly with Task scheduling and §20 requires 500,000 Tasks without 500,000 kernel threads; the kernel records which Operation a suspended Task awaits and wakes it on completion so the native runtime binds to kernel Operations rather than reinventing async I/O; BEN INV-1020 measures 500k Tasks at V0 and needs this.

title: Implement Task as the native concurrency abstraction
justification: §59 V0 goal: create a native Task. Implements Task per decide-task-identity and the Tasks half of the Native Platform layer. Threads are not a native API; this object is what native software runs.

title: Propagate cancellation through the TaskGroup hierarchy
justification: V0 exit and cancellation demo: cancelling a TaskGroup cancels owned Tasks, child groups and outstanding Operations; app.cancel waits until every owned Task has terminated; a regression proves no Task survives group cancel or application exit. Operation Cancelled results remain operation-cancel-deadline; the background-execution Capability exception is V0.5.

title: Inherit TaskGroup deadlines and outstanding-Operation limits by owned Operations
justification: §21 structured concurrency: Operations submitted inside a TaskGroup take the minimum of their own and the group's deadline and share the group's outstanding budget, so cancelling or timing out a group tears down in-flight work deterministically (V0 cancellation demo hardened for real apps).

title: Implement Object<TaskGroup> with ownership hierarchy
justification: §7 Object<TaskGroup> and §21 ownership: Application owns TaskGroups, TaskGroups own Tasks and child TaskGroups, each Component owns a TaskGroup. Capability-referenced kernel object. V0 scope and the §59 create-TaskGroup exit.

title: Add slack and coalescing to Timer Operations for energy efficiency
justification: V1 idle power and battery runtime gate; Timer Operations carry slack derived from EnergyEfficient/Background intent so idle desktops coalesce wake-ups instead of ticking per component.

title: Build V0 Operation acceptance suite for six kinds, deadline and cancellation
justification: Verifies the V0 exit criterion: Read, Write, Send, Receive, Timer, Wait complete; a deadline yields a Timeout result; a cancelled Operation never delivers a result; runs on QEMU and the reference desktop in CI.

title: Benchmark per-Component text memory and shaping CPU with shared versus private caches
justification: The shared atlas exists on a memory and startup claim; §54 and BEN policy forbid unmeasured claims, so the harness publishes memory and shaping cost for N Components with private caches and with the shared read-only atlas.

title: Benchmark text stack initialisation and first-glyph time inside application startup
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate measures warm startup (target p50 ≤ 20 ms for the smallest app) and font loading, matcher resolution and first shaping are on that path; harness plus publish-only measurement so later text stack claims have a baseline per §54.

title: Verify CJK input methods in native and Linux-personality applications on Tier 1
justification: V4 exit criterion: CJK input methods functional in native and Linux-personality applications (tested); scripted typing scenarios for Chinese, Japanese and Korean run on every Tier 1 machine each RC.

title: Ship CLDR, tzdata and Unicode data as a Package updating independently of SystemGenerations
justification: Locale and time zone data change faster than the OS; a content-addressed data Package with hot reload in the text and locale services (coordinated with PKG for independent update and SVC for time settings) prevents stale time zones between generations.

title: Render emoji ZWJ sequences and COLRv1 colour glyphs
justification: Emoji presentation selectors, modifier and ZWJ sequences and COLRv1 rasterisation into the shared atlas using the emoji font selected in the font set decision; V2 desktop shell and messaging-class L3 apps expose emoji everywhere.

title: Decide the default system font set and publish its script coverage matrix
justification: Selects licensed fonts covering Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai, CJK, monospace and COLRv1 colour emoji, including metric-compatible substitutes for Windows core fonts instead of Microsoft fonts, with the coverage matrix recorded in the decision; fonts ship in the first immutable V0.5 image.

title: Decide the cross-Component glyph atlas and shaped-text cache sharing model
justification: Decides one thing: per-Component caches, a read-only atlas minted by the text service, or a shared writable atlas (rejected per critique #7 and §67 principle 3); depends on the font threat model and SEC's side-channel statement.

title: Decide hosting existing IME engines versus native engines and the 1.0 language list
justification: Decides one thing: sandboxed hosting of librime, libpinyin, anthy, libhangul and m17n versus native engines, with the 1.0 input-language list; §67 principle 15 argues against rewrites and the V4 CJK gate needs engines from V2.

title: Decide the locale data source between ICU/CLDR and an ICU4X port
justification: Decides one thing: which CLDR-backed implementation supplies formatting, collation, plural rules and time zones; must precede the V2 Locale object, localisation pipeline and CLDR/tzdata package.

title: Decide the message catalog format between Fluent and gettext
justification: First-party apps accumulate string sites from V0.5; deciding the catalog format and SDK string API alongside SDK v1 prevents rewriting every UI string site before the V2 localisation framework, per the GAP-0258 rationale.

title: Decide the shaping and rasterisation libraries for the native text stack
justification: Decides one thing: retained HarfBuzz+FreeType versus Rust-native shaping and rasterisation (options with §67 principle 15 applied), using the spike report; every V0.5 app renders text through the chosen stack.

title: Decide hinting, subpixel positioning and gamma policy across scale factors
justification: Decides one thing: the rendering policy so native and Linux-personality text render identically at every fractional scale; V2 introduces fractional and per-display scaling and §49 forbids visibly non-native compatibility windows.

title: Decide whether shaping runs in-Component or in a shared text service Component
justification: Decides one thing: in-component library, shared system text service, or hybrid (library shaping with a service minting read-only caches); depends on the font threat model because the answer changes the isolation and latency model for every UI Component.

title: Bring the shell and native applications to five languages via the translation platform
justification: V3 scope caps localisation at five languages; reaching five through the public platform validates community translation flow before the V4 ten-language gate and the V3 public documentation.

title: Audit and record licences of every shipped font with redistribution terms
justification: Records licence, source and redistribution terms for each shipped font under GOV's licensing policy and feeds the BLD licence/SBOM CI gate; must exist before the first immutable V0.5 image redistributes fonts.

title: Build the typed FontMatcher interface with family, weight, script fallback chains
justification: Typed Layer 2 interface resolving family/weight/width/style/script requests to fallback chains over installed font Packages, replacing fontconfig for native applications; the V0.5 toolkit and four apps resolve fonts through it.

title: Ship fonts as immutable content-addressed Packages with per-user installation
justification: Fonts become Package objects in the content-addressed store (system set in the generation, user fonts installed per user without writing outside the store), satisfying the V0.5 immutable-package exit criterion for the text stack.

title: Parse untrusted fonts in an isolated Component before atlas admission
justification: Implements the threat model mitigation: user-installed and personality-supplied fonts are parsed and sanity-checked in a capability-scoped Component with no display or file authority beyond the font object, so the text service that mints shared atlases never parses untrusted bytes in its own address space.

title: Write the font parsing and text service threat model
justification: Critique contradiction #7 makes a shared glyph atlas a font-parsing attack surface and cross-domain channel; the V0.5 apps parse fonts from packages and user files, so the attack surface, trust boundaries and the dependency on SEC's side-channel statement must be written before the service-placement and atlas decisions.

title: Expose the native font store to the Linux personality through fontconfig
justification: V1 L2 integration check scores correct scaling and §49 requires compatibility windows to feel native; generating fontconfig configuration and font directories from the native store gives browser, IDE and Wine (consumed by WIN) the same fonts and fallback chains as native apps.

title: Build the text service minting read-only glyph atlas and shaped-run MemoryObjects
justification: Text service rasterises and shapes once per system and hands Components read-only MemoryObject atlas pages and shaped-run cache entries with an eviction and generation protocol; V1 daily-driving runs many more text-rendering Components under cheap isolation.

title: Ship the first hosted IME engine for Chinese pinyin input
justification: First engine through the host proves the protocol, capability routing and candidate window end to end at V2, leaving V3 for the remaining 1.0 language list ahead of the V4 CJK gate.

title: Ship hosted IME engines for Japanese, Korean and the rest of the 1.0 language list
justification: Completes the engine list from the IME strategy decision (anthy, libhangul, m17n-based Vietnamese and Indic) so the V4 gate can test CJK input on Tier 1 machines with a full milestone of soak.

title: Route Capability<TextInputFocus> to the IME Component for the focused field only
justification: Coordinated with UIP input routing: the compositor mints a per-focus Capability<TextInputFocus> and an IME Component without it receives no key events; a permanent denial test proves no global key stream exists, satisfying the capability model that forbids ambient key logging.

title: Build the sandboxed IME host Component with candidate window presentation
justification: IME host Component holding only Capability<TextInputFocus> and dictionary Package access, engine lifecycle and per-session switching, and a candidate window placed at the protocol's cursor rectangle; the V2 localisation framework and V4 CJK gate depend on it.

title: Implement the native input-method protocol in the toolkit text fields
justification: Preedit rendering, commit, surrounding text, cursor rectangle and candidate placement implemented against the registered Layer 2 surface so the protocol is exercised by real fields before the V1 freeze candidate; engines arrive at V2.

title: Bridge text-input-v3 and input-method-v2 in the Wayland bridge to the native IME
justification: Linux GUI apps type through the native IME host via the Wayland text-input protocols implemented inside LNX's bridge (TXT owns the IME mapping); §47 integration and the V4 gate that CJK input works in Linux-personality applications.

title: Build the typed Locale object with per-application override and formatting APIs
justification: Locale as a typed SDK object (numbers, dates, plurals, collation, measurement) with per-application override and session default from SVC settings storage; required by the V2 localisation framework and §41 locale formatting.

title: Build the SDK localisation pipeline with catalog extraction and packaged resources
justification: Build-time string extraction, catalogs shipped as Package resources, runtime lookup with plural and bidi-aware formatting through the Locale object, and the SDK API; the V2 exit requires the localisation framework in place.

title: Lock 1.x versions of FontMatcher, TextInput, Locale and SpellCheck interfaces
justification: V4 exit requires Layer 2 interface versions enumerated and locked with the old-client/new-service and new-client/old-service evolution test passing for every core interface; the IME surface registered at V0.5 is frozen here, never earlier.

title: Build the monospace grid text fast path for the Terminal
justification: The V0.5 Terminal needs cell-width metrics and a no-reshape glyph grid path so it meets its scripted acceptance scenario and keeps text stack cost off the warm-startup path measured by the V0.5 and V1 application startup gates.

title: Register the input-method protocol shape as a Layer 2 surface in UI protocol v0
justification: Critique ordering fix: preedit, commit, surrounding text, cursor rectangle and candidate placement must be an S-entry before the UI protocol becomes a V1 freeze candidate; reserving the optional messages while protocol v0 is designed and version-bumped at V0.5 avoids an incompatible V1 revision.

title: Re-verify the localisation and IME gates on the 1.0 release build
justification: 1.0 exit criterion: accessibility and localisation gates from V4 hold on the release build (10 languages ≥ 95%, CJK input tested); re-runs coverage, conformance and IME scenarios on the final release candidate across Tier 1.

title: Translate the shell and four native applications into three languages
justification: V2 scope requires the shell translated into at least three languages; includes one RTL language to exercise bidi, a coverage test in CI and screenshot review of layout under translated strings.

title: Build the spell-checking and hyphenation service with dictionary Packages
justification: Typed interface over Hunspell dictionaries and hyphenation patterns installed as per-language Packages, consumed by toolkit text fields (underlines, suggestions, per-field opt-out for secrets); a V2 polished desktop needs it in every text field.

title: Prototype HarfBuzz+FreeType against Rust shaping and raster stacks on a script corpus
justification: Builds both candidate stacks (HarfBuzz+FreeType; rustybuzz/swash/cosmic-text) behind one shaping trait, measures shaping correctness on a multi-script corpus, throughput, binary size, startup cost and unsafe surface, and rules options out before the two stack decisions; answers the V0.5 risk that a minimal text path hardens into the permanent design.

title: Reach ten languages at 95% string coverage with a CI coverage gate
justification: V4 exit criterion: 10 languages at ≥ 95% string coverage for shell and native apps; adds the coverage measurement as a blocking CI gate and closes translation gaps before feature freeze.

title: Build the toolkit text editing model with cursor, selection and surrounding text
justification: Editing primitives (caret movement by grapheme, selection, undo, surrounding-text access, reserved preedit span) used by the Text Editor and every text field at V0.5, shaped so the IME protocol can attach without redesign.

title: Write the SDK guide for fonts, text layout, input methods and localisation
justification: V3 exit requires the SDK guide published and reviewed; the text, FontMatcher, IME protocol, Locale and catalog APIs need developer guidance so third-party packages localise correctly (coordinated with DOC's generated references).

title: Apply the text rendering policy natively and in the Linux personality with pixel parity tests
justification: Implements subpixel positioning and fractional-scale rasterisation in the toolkit, propagates the same hinting, gamma and scale settings into personality fontconfig and FreeType properties, and adds a pixel-compare test at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x and 2x that scores in the L3 integration check.

title: Make the text service restartable with client rebind and cache regeneration
justification: SVC supervision semantics from V0.5 require every shared service to restart and rebind; a crashed text service must not blank text in running applications during V1 daily driving, so clients rebind, revalidate atlas generations and re-request evicted runs (tested by kill loop in CI).

title: Integrate shaping and rasterisation into the toolkit retained text layout
justification: Delivers shaped, rasterised, high-DPI-aware text runs as retained render nodes for declarative widgets (Latin and simple scripts, wrapping, alignment) on the decided stack; required by the V0.5 exit criterion that a native application renders declarative UI and by all four apps.

title: Stand up the public translation platform and catalog sync for first-party apps
justification: Public translation platform with automated catalog round-trip into first-party repositories and per-language coverage reporting; community translation is how the V3 five-language and V4 ten-language targets are reached.

title: Run Unicode and text-rendering conformance suites as a CI gate
justification: BidiTest, BidiCharacterTest, LineBreakTest, GraphemeBreakTest, WordBreakTest and the text-rendering-tests corpus run in BLD CI against the layout engine and shaping stack, making GAP-0249's 'verified against the Unicode conformance test suites' a permanent gate.

title: Implement UAX #29 segmentation, UAX #9 bidi and UAX #14 line breaking in layout
justification: Grapheme and word segmentation, bidirectional resolution and reordering, and line breaking in the toolkit layout engine; required for the V2 three-language shell (including an RTL script) and the §41 localization requirement of bidi.

title: Support variable font axes and OpenType feature selection end to end
justification: Variation axes and feature tags flow from FontMatcher requests through shaping, the atlas key and rasterisation; the V2 polished shell relies on weight axes for typography and the toolkit must expose features to applications.

title: Support vertical CJK text layout and orientation features in the toolkit
justification: Vertical writing mode with vert/vrt2 features and upright/rotated Latin runs in the layout engine, needed for CJK text fidelity before the V4 CJK gate and the 10-language target.

title: Emit role, name and state for every widget and expose via os inspect
justification: V0.5 exit criterion 'every UI widget emits accessibility metadata inspectable via os inspect; tree dump test on each of the four apps'; critique pulls emission to V0.5 with the ACC tree-model adr as dependency.

title: Support adaptive layouts for desktop, laptop and external display in toolkit
justification: INV-0776; V2 laptop day demo plugs an external HDR display at a different scale and the shell UX script includes external display and scaling change.

title: Build animation API with frame-scheduled transitions and reduced-motion
justification: INV-0769 animation with frame-scheduled updates as a toolkit API (implicit and explicit animations) on top of frame-scheduled-redraw.

title: Expose light/dark, accent, icon, cursor, wallpaper and font scale as typed settings
justification: GAP-0281; V2 desktop UX script covers settings and scaling change. LNX projects the same typed settings through the settings portal and GTK/Qt hints.

title: Build scripted UI frame-time benchmark and publish p99 against frame interval
justification: V0.5 exit criterion 'frame-time p99 below the frame interval in a scripted UI benchmark'; harness plus published measurement, re-run at every later rung for the regression gates.

title: Build clipboard service as Capability with typed lazy MemoryObject transfer
justification: INV-0773 and INV-0208; V0.5 exit criterion 'an application without the clipboard capability cannot read clipboard contents; a test confirms the denial', and the Wayland demo needs copy-paste between native and Linux apps.

title: Gate clipboard reads on paste gesture and add ClipboardRead for managers
justification: GAP-0233 and INV-0773: paste-gesture-gated reads, explicit Capability<ClipboardRead> for the privileged shell clipboard manager, and the V1 L2 integration check 'clipboard both directions' for Linux windows.

title: Expose decoration, clipboard, drop and scale hooks for compatibility bridges
justification: V1 L2 integration check for every GUI application (clipboard both directions, correct scaling, native chrome); LNX owns the Wayland/XWayland bridge, UIP owns the protocol hooks it plugs into.

title: Decide clipboard authority policy: paste gesture or Capability, no ambient read
justification: GAP-0274 and GAP-0233 are the same decision (reads gated by paste gesture or explicit Capability<ClipboardRead>, writes allowed, history is a privileged shell feature, typed negotiation with lazy MemoryObject transfer); INV-0208 is the invariant it enforces. Pulled to V0.5 because clipboard-capability-v0 depends on it.

title: Decide global shortcut model: named actions bound in Settings, no key grabs
justification: GAP-0286 pulled from V2 to V1 because shortcut-focus-model (INV-0787, V1) depends on it.

title: Decide input routing and focus arbitration model for focused surfaces
justification: One decision: how pointer, keyboard, touch, pen and gamepad events reach only the focused surface and how focus is arbitrated between compositor, shell and applications without grabs. Precedes input-routing-service.

title: Decide UI protocol model: retained scene tree, client Buffers, or hybrid
justification: INV-0778 ADR; V0.5 exit requires an accepted ADR for UI protocol transport. Depends on spike-protocol-shape.

title: Decide new Rust toolkit versus adapting an existing toolkit and renderer
justification: INV-0779 and GAP-0517: toolkit build-vs-adopt with an evaluation matrix covering accessibility tree output and declarative fit, decided before the four demo apps start.

title: Decide server-side versus client-side decorations for native and compat windows
justification: INV-0786 ADR; needed before protocol-core-idl fixes the window surface roles and before the Wayland bridge shows compat windows at V0.5.

title: Document input-stack ownership split between HW and UIP
justification: EXTRA-042: device enablement (libinput/evdev/HID, layouts, gestures) in HW; routing and focus in UIP, recorded in both workstream files and the protocol spec.

title: Write UI protocol reference and toolkit SDK guide from IDL at V1
justification: V1 scope 'SDK v1 published'; DOC provides IDL-to-docs generation at V1, UIP writes the protocol reference and toolkit guide content that V3 documentation coverage relies on.

title: Implement drag and drop where a drop transfers a Capability to the target
justification: INV-0772; V1 daily-driving and the capability demo (chooser grants exactly one file) rely on drops granting object capabilities, not paths.

title: Drive toolkit redraw from compositor frame callbacks at display refresh
justification: INV-0769 frame-scheduled updates; V0.5 exit requires a native application to animate at the display refresh rate with frame-time p99 below the frame interval.

title: Fuzz UI protocol decoders and compositor-facing endpoints continuously
justification: V3 exit 'continuous fuzzing' and the UI threat review: the protocol decoder is the largest untrusted-input surface between applications and the compositor.

title: Implement named-action global shortcuts bound by the user in Settings
justification: GAP-0286 implementation after decide-global-shortcuts; push-to-talk, screenshot and media keys are needed by V2 screen-sharing, video conferencing (L3) and gaming.

title: Add high-contrast themes and reduced-motion mode across all toolkit widgets
justification: V4 scope 'high contrast across shell and native apps' and the a11y script; built at V3 so V4 conformance can be verified rather than started.

title: Support per-surface high-DPI and mixed-DPI scale across displays in toolkit
justification: INV-0777; V1 L2 integration check scores 'correct scaling' and the Intel laptop internal plus external display differ in DPI.

title: Instrument input pipeline stages with trace timestamps for latency measurement
justification: V0.5 benchmark gate 'input-to-photon latency measured with a photodiode rig' needs the routing and toolkit stages timestamped so the LAB rig result can be decomposed; OBS tracing format is reused.

title: Route pointer, keyboard and touch input only to focused surfaces
justification: INV-0770 and INV-1180; V0.5 exit requires a native application to receive keyboard and mouse input through the protocol and no unfocused surface may observe it (tested).

title: Park on-screen keyboard, tablet mode and convertible form-factor UI
justification: GAP-0287 excludes these from 1.0 and INV-0776 names 'future tablet'; parked here so adaptive-form-factors is not stretched into them before 1.0.

title: Declare Layer 4 UI toolkit evolution under semantic versioning
justification: Layer 4 is the UI toolkit and app frameworks; UIP owns it. SDK remains Layer 3 only.

title: Provide locale-aware date, number, currency and collation APIs to native apps
justification: GAP-0259 typed formatting and collation APIs consumed by the toolkit and native apps; the translated-language set and percent gate are TXT's V4 localisation gate.

title: Handle per-display scale and refresh changes and hot-plug without window loss
justification: V2 exit 'two displays with different scale factors and refresh rates, hot-plug 100 times without window loss'; GFX owns the compositor side, UIP the surface migration and toolkit relayout.

title: Publish UI protocol conformance suite for third-party toolkits and bridges
justification: V3 gate 'public repo with third-party packages' means non-core toolkits talk the protocol; the suite is also the precondition for the V4 L2 version lock.

title: Define UI protocol v0 IDL: surfaces, frames and Buffers over Channel
justification: INV-0762 and INV-0108: the native protocol between applications and the compositor is a user-space service above Channel and MemoryObject; V0.5 exit requires a native app to open a window through it.

title: Add CI lint rejecting X11, Wayland and primary-selection concepts in native IDL
justification: Standing non-goals enforced once: the native UI protocol IDL and toolkit API may not reference X11 or Wayland objects, and primary selection is emulated only inside the Linux personality bridge (critique contradiction 9, decided once here).

title: Publish UI protocol v1 as L2 freeze candidate with client compatibility suite
justification: V1 exit 'SDK v1 with L2 evolution rules frozen'; critique: L1 not frozen before V4, L2 rules frozen at V1. Suite proves v0/v0.1 clients run on v1.

title: Lock UI protocol L2 version for 1.x and remove deprecated messages
justification: V4 exit 'versioned Layer 2 interfaces locked for 1.x'; compatibility suite proves V1-era clients run on the locked version.

title: Version UI protocol under §12 rules and bump v0 to v0.1 with old clients running
justification: INV-0783; V0.5 exit criterion 'interface versioning exercised end to end: UI protocol v0 bumped to v0.1 with an added optional method, old clients still run, regression test retained permanently'.

title: Implement right-to-left layout mirroring as a toolkit property
justification: GAP-0259: RTL mirroring is architectural and must land with the V2 localization framework, not as a translation later.

title: Add semantic actions (activate, expand, scroll-to) to the a11y tree in protocol
justification: §41 requirement 'semantic actions'; V2 exit 'screen reader prototype reads and activates every widget' and SEM's Terminal.run/Editor.open proof need actionable nodes on the tree emitted at V0.5.

title: Add privileged shell surface roles to protocol v0 for panel and launcher
justification: V0.5 demo 'cold boot to native desktop showing the four native applications' needs a minimal launcher; APP builds the shell, UIP provides the layer-surface roles gated by a shell Capability.

title: Implement shortcut and focus model forbidding global interception without Capability
justification: INV-0787; test that a Component cannot register a global key grab and that focus follows the routing model.

title: Prototype UI protocol as scene graph, client buffers and hybrid; measure
justification: GAP-0516: the protocol shape is nearly as permanent as the kernel ABI and gates the V0.5 transport ADR; measured latency, memory and toolkit ergonomics over Channel plus MemoryObject buffers must exist before the V0.5 adr. Started in V0 so the largest V0.5 body of new userspace code is not blocked on its own spike.

title: Study Flutter, SwiftUI, Compose, Slint and Xilem declarative models
justification: INV-0784 research study; per the critique non-V0 studies sit at V0.5. Report feeds decide-toolkit-architecture and toolkit-core.

title: Build theming and styling system with tokens and runtime theme switch
justification: INV-0785 theming and styling for native applications, the base the V2 appearance model builds on.

title: Write UI protocol threat review: focus stealing, input injection, exfiltration
justification: Critique ordering fix: threat analysis precedes the design it constrains. Feeds decide-input-routing-model, decide-clipboard-policy and ui-capability-definition, citing the SEC V0 threat model; clickjacking, focus stealing, synthetic input and screen-content leaks are the protocol's own threats.

title: Build toolkit core: declarative element tree with retained render tree
justification: INV-0763, INV-0764, INV-1181: declarative UI with retained-mode rendering sufficient for the four V0.5 demo applications.

title: Build keyboard focus traversal, focus ring and access keys across all widgets
justification: V4 gate 'keyboard-only operation of the entire shell verified' and the V2 screen-reader prototype both need every toolkit widget reachable and activatable by keyboard; ACC owns the AT client, UIP the widget traversal.

title: Build GPU renderer drawing toolkit render tree into MemoryObject Buffers
justification: INV-0768 GPU rendering; V0.5 exit requires GPU-accelerated composition of application windows rendered into Buffers owned by the application.

title: Build responsive layout engine with constraints and reflow on resize
justification: INV-0767 responsive layout; the four apps must reflow on window resize in their scripted scenarios.

title: Integrate TXT shaping into toolkit text display and editing widgets
justification: V0.5 scope 'basic text' in the UI protocol and toolkit; TXT owns shaping and the glyph atlas service, UIP owns the text widget consuming them. Editor and Terminal cannot pass acceptance without it.

title: Build widget set sufficient for Terminal, File Browser, Editor and Viewer
justification: INV-1181: buttons, lists, text fields, scroll views, menus, dialogs, splitters and image views needed by the four APP demo applications.

title: Ship basic touchscreen and touchpad gestures in toolkit and routing
justification: GAP-0287 scope-in half: tap, scroll, pinch and swipe on the V2 target laptops' touchpads and touchscreens; HW owns libinput gesture recognition, UIP routing and widget handling.

title: Add touch, pen and gamepad event types to the UI protocol
justification: INV-0770 lists touch, pen and gamepad; the protocol surface must exist before the V1 L2 freeze-candidate review, and V2 gaming and target laptops consume it.

title: Define Capability<UI> granted at launch: window creation without screen contents
justification: INV-0213; V0.5 exit requires the Image Viewer to start with UI and GPU capabilities only, and a test that a UI-only Component cannot read screen contents.

title: Publish UI protocol and toolkit API stability statement for 1.x
justification: 1.0 exit 'ABI stability statement' and 'explicit non-promises listed': states the locked protocol version, toolkit semver policy, and that on-screen keyboard, tablet mode and convertible UI are not in 1.0 (GAP-0287 scope-out half).

title: Build UI test driver that scripts widgets through the a11y tree and actions
justification: §41 'automation interfaces' at toolkit level; the V0.5 app acceptance scenarios, the V2 40-scenario desktop UX script and the V4 50-task a11y script all need a driver that is not GUI pixel automation.

title: Unify drag-and-drop and clipboard content types across native, Wayland and OLE
justification: GAP-0276; V2 exit requires Windows applications to use the native clipboard and file chooser, and drops grant a Capability to the dropped object in every personality.

title: Automate V0.5 UI gates: window, input, animation, clipboard denial, a11y dump
justification: V0.5 exit criteria owned by UIP wired into CI on QEMU and the reference desktop so the gates are verified by tasks, not prose.

title: Automate V1 UI gates: L2 integration scoring and frame-time regression
justification: V1 compatibility gate integration check (clipboard, scaling) and benchmark gate 'no regression greater than 10%' for bench-ui-frame-time on both V1 machines.

title: Automate V2 desktop UX script and appearance consistency on three machines
justification: V2 exit '40-scenario desktop UX script on all three target machines with zero P0/P1 defects' driven through ui-test-driver; APP owns the shell scenarios, UIP the toolkit-level harness and theming consistency checks.

title: Verify every shipped widget passes a11y metadata and keyboard conformance
justification: V4 exit '50-task assistive-technology script completes 100%' and 'keyboard-only operation verified'; ACC runs the script, UIP fixes the widget-level defects it surfaces.

title: Publish guest GPU frame-time against host and Proton
justification: §54/§57: no performance claim without a benchmark. V2 gaming gates already publish FPS vs Linux+Proton; the VM fallback needs the same published comparison on the path spike-guest-gpu selects. Harness reused by V4 passthrough. Publish-only at V3; no numeric target in the task.

title: Decide the fallback virtualization product and 1.0 scope
justification: GAP-0443: personalities never cover 100% of software, and the 1.0 non-goal of kernel anti-cheat leaves the VM fallback as the only honest answer (§56.2, §69). Options must include a native KVM Component manager, a libvirt/virt-manager personality app, qemu launched with Capability-wrapped fds, and no host VM product. KRN-@adr-kvm-native-exposure owns kernel Capability<VirtualMachine>; WIN GAP-0510 owns whether the personality promise includes a VM fallback.

title: Decide guest-window integration depth and agent protocol
justification: GAP-0445 is listed at V4 but its rationale says seamless mode fixes the guest-agent protocol that guest tools must ship against; critique ordering puts decisions no later than dependents. Options: one virtio-gpu Surface per VM, per-application guest windows as native Surfaces with clipboard/drag/drop/chooser/notification bridging (§49), or single-display default with opt-in seamless. Pulled to V2 so linux-guest-tools and windows-guest-tools do not freeze a protocol by accident. GFX-@vm-guest-surfaces remains the compositor remote-Surface work at V3.

title: Implement SR-IOV and GPU passthrough for VM guests
justification: Remaining GAP-0446 path after virtio-gpu: SR-IOV and full passthrough on the V4 multi-GPU/NVIDIA Tier 1 set, which is the 1.0 answer for GPU-bound software the Windows personality cannot run. Size L: IOMMU, VFIO and host GPU sharing with GFX/HW. Host driver stack stays Linux DRM; this is not a native GPU rewrite (§57).

title: Implement virtio-gpu acceleration for Linux and Windows guests
justification: Critique missing-workstream line names guest GPU as VIRT scope; V3 experimental gamers need a 3D path before VFIO passthrough. Builds the virtio-gpu Venus/virgl option spike-guest-gpu recommends. Not a native GPU stack (§56.1, §57).

title: Provide OVMF firmware and TPM emulation for Windows guests
justification: 1.0 VM fallback must run Windows 11 guests the personalities cannot, which need UEFI and TPM 2.0. Workstreams.md 1.0 feature scope of the GAP-0443 product. BLD GAP-0111 OVMF/TPM is the CI matrix for hosting JakeOS, not guest firmware inside the VM manager.

title: Bridge guest windows, clipboard, drag/drop and notifications
justification: Remaining EXTRA-054 seamless path after V2 guest tools. Implements the GAP-0445 choice so guests meet §49 (taskbar, clipboard, chooser, notifications) instead of an obvious VM. V3 because GFX-@vm-guest-surfaces (INV-0746) lands then. Crosses UIP clipboard/drag/drop and GFX Surfaces; size L.

title: Grant VM host access through inspectable Capabilities
justification: GAP-0444 invariant collapsed into an enforcing build: folders, devices, network and clipboard reach a guest only as granted Capabilities, each visible in os inspect with revoke taking effect on the next Operation. Collapses the ambient-authority constraint rather than a standalone rule task. USB/PCI passthrough uses these grants; GPU passthrough is a later task.

title: Ship Linux guest tools for folders, clipboard and display
justification: EXTRA-054/GAP-0448: a fallback VM is unusable without shared folders, clipboard, time sync, display resize and a guest agent. Linux guests first, using the protocol chosen by decide-guest-window-depth. Per-window Surfaces stay in guest-window-integration. IPC-@vm-transport-prototype is native-guest-to-host Channels, not this agent.

title: Offer the VM fallback from compatibility triage
justification: EXTRA-056 and workstreams.md 'offer the VM' flow: when an ELF or PE fails under a Personality, the OS offers to run it in a granted VM. REL GAP-0450 owns the explanation text and public compatibility database; this task is the VM-offer action and handoff into the manager. Needed for V3 enthusiasts facing anti-cheat and other personality misses (§49).

title: Boot an existing Windows dual-boot partition as a VM guest
justification: Implements spike-physical-win-guest if the report recommends a supported path; otherwise dropped with reason infeasible. 1.0 migration bridge from the GAP-0447 rationale and V3 dual-boot installer. INS owns partition layout; STO owns NTFS; VIRT owns attaching the volume as a VirtualMachine disk with TPM/BitLocker caveats recorded.

title: Publish JakeOS guest images for common hypervisors
justification: EXTRA-055 and workstreams.md give VIRT the JakeOS-as-guest image product so V1 developers can onboard without bare metal. Ships signed qcow2/vmdk/vhd/UTM artifacts for QEMU/KVM, VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V and UTM. INS GAP-0449 owns virtio, guest agent and dynamic resolution inside those guests; BLD/REL own the image builder and channel.

title: Evaluate guest GPU paths for a VM gaming fallback
justification: GAP-0446 research: virtio-gpu Venus/virgl, SR-IOV and full passthrough with multi-GPU, plus viability for titles that keep a Windows partition. Jsonl says V4; pulled to V2 so guest-gpu-virtio (V3) and guest-gpu-passthrough (V4) have a report. No FPS number in prose; bench-guest-gpu publishes the comparison.

title: Evaluate booting a physical Windows partition as a VM
justification: GAP-0447: activation, TPM and BitLocker implications of attaching the dual-boot Windows partition as a guest. Jsonl says V4; pulled to V3 so it runs once the V3 installer dual-boot path exists and can inform physical-win-guest. Options the report must rule in or out: unsupported, hibernate-and-attach, and both-ways dual boot.

title: Verify the VM fallback on Tier 1 without shipping Windows images
justification: 1.0 completeness check for the VIRT product: manager, guest tools, triage offer and GPU path run on every Tier 1 machine; release artifacts contain no Windows ISO or key (GAP-0448). Anchors the workstream to the 1.0 compatibility-guide and anti-cheat-non-promise exits.

title: Snapshot and clone VM disks via the content-addressed store
justification: 1.0 feature scope of the GAP-0443 product and workstreams.md VM manager: a broken guest must be restorable the same way a SystemGeneration is. STO owns CoW/snapshots; VIRT owns VM disk objects that snapshot, clone and roll back without a second storage model. Needed before 1.0, after the V2 manager exists.

title: Publish the VM fallback chapter of the compatibility guide
justification: V3 documentation exit and 1.0 compatibility guide need an honest VM-fallback chapter: how to offer a VM, which guests are supported, and the GAP-0448 ban on redistributing Windows images or keys. DOC owns IDL→docs; VIRT owns this product chapter.

title: Implement the KVM VM manager as a capability-scoped Component
justification: EXTRA-053 is the V2 product: a KVM-based manager with typed VirtualMachine objects. GAP-0444 requires each VM to be a Component in a ResourceDomain (§10, §23) so virtualization does not reopen ambient authority (§9.1). Userspace only; depends on KRN-@kvm-virtual-machine-object. Out of scope: kernel KVM retention, nested-virt CI, IPC VM transport.

title: Build the native VM manager UI with capability review
justification: GAP-0443 product includes a native UI; V3 public-alpha strangers cannot be asked to drive VMs from a CLI. Create/start/stop, disk and firmware pickers, and review/deny of host-access Capability requests. APP owns shell/store/consent chrome; this UI is the VIRT product surface. V2 manager may be CLI-only.

title: Ship Windows guest tools without redistributing Windows images
justification: GAP-0448 Windows half plus the licensing boundary: guest agent, virtio-win, clipboard, folders, time and display resize for user-supplied Windows ISOs. CI fails if a Windows image or license key is in tree or release artifacts. Same protocol as linux-guest-tools so the V2 agent is not Linux-only.

title: AOT-compile Wasm Components into Package artefacts
justification: §34 and PKG precompiled-artefact storage (INV-0633). WASM produces content-addressed AOT images so V1 plugin instantiation can use verified-once mapped pages. PKG stores; WASM compiles.

title: Host Wasm automation modules over typed Interface
justification: §13/§45 first-class automation modules at V2 with the semantic-automation gate. SEM owns the rules ADR and registry; WASM hosts modules that hold only delegated Capability. Not an AI broker.

title: Measure Wasm instantiation and Channel round trip
justification: V1 publish-only gate for B-047 (bench:wasm-component). Critique forbids benchmark gates without a harness. No numeric claim; targets live in the register.

title: Debug Wasm Components with source-level breakpoints
justification: V3 TypeScript/Wasm SDK bindings (SDK) need a guest debug path. Native debugger is V1; this adds DWARF/name-section breaks inside a Wasm Component without exposing POSIX ptrace as a native API.

title: Decide the userspace Wasm runtime and host placement
justification: V1 gate: runtime ADR plus prototype. Chooses Wasmtime, Wasmer, WAMR or custom, and in-Component versus shared service. License forces userspace-only; in-kernel embed is rejected on GPLv2 incompatibility.

title: Decide WASI imports bound to native Capability
justification: V1 Channel prototype and capabilities-as-WASI-resources mapping need a Decision listing which WASI worlds bind to Capability (clocks, random, UserSelected, NetworkConnection) and which ambient Preview1 imports are forbidden.

title: Decide Wasm role versus native machine-code Components
justification: V0 allows a Wasm ADR and V1 requires a Wasm-role Decision. Collapses the no-duplicate-WIT/WASI invariant and the do-not-force-every-app nongoal. Options must keep native machine code first-class and reject Wasm as the Native ABI.

title: Instantiate downloaded Wasm Components from the store
justification: §13 downloaded Components once the V2 store client and signed repository exist. Unsigned or undeclared-Capability modules are refused; grants match Package requested Capability. REL/APP own store UX; WASM instantiates.

title: Load a sandboxed Wasm plugin with declared Capability rights
justification: V1 demo: Wasm plugin in the editor holding only declared Capability. Collapses plugins and sandboxed extensions. APP owns editor chrome; WASM owns the plugin host and denial tests.

title: Evaluate userspace Wasm runtimes for host selection
justification: Spike must precede the V1 runtime Decision. Measures instantiation latency, footprint and Capability binding on Wasmtime, WAMR, Wasmer and a custom option. Not V0: hard cap and no integration yet.

title: Fuzz the Wasm host ABI and Capability import table
justification: The Wasm host is a trust boundary the moment the V1 prototype exists. Harness mutates WIT canonical ABI and import tables; panics and Capability forgeries fail closed. Feeds the V3 continuous-fuzzing gate.

title: Transfer MemoryObjects into Wasm guest resources
justification: §13 participation in the object ecosystem plus §16 ownership transfer. Large Channel payloads must move as MemoryObject resources rather than copies through linear memory. MEM owns MemoryObject; WASM maps the guest resource.

title: Run portable services as supervised Wasm Components
justification: §13 first-class portable services. A long-running Wasm Component is SVC-supervised with crash-rebind of Channel clients, matching the V0.5 compositor pattern. SVC owns supervision; WASM owns the service Component kind.

title: Host Wasm Components in userspace beside machine code
justification: V1 scope: portable WebAssembly Components as a Component kind next to machine code. Instantiates from Package, charges ResourceDomain, maps traps to typed disconnect, and CI-rejects linking the runtime into the kernel.

title: Lock Wasm host Interface versions with a conformance suite
justification: V4 Layer 2 versions locked. Wasm host imports are Layer 2, not Layer 1, so this is not an L1 freeze. Conformance suite proves binaries against the lock candidate still instantiate on later V4 builds.

title: Map WASI resources and WIT worlds onto Capability
justification: V1 exit: a Wasm Component exchanges typed messages over Channel with a machine-code Component. Implements capabilities as WASI resources and WIT interfaces as Channel after IPC's IDL/WIT Decision.

title: Ship architecture-independent Wasm Component Packages
justification: §13 cross-architecture workloads as a portable format on every V2 x86-64 machine without per-arch native binaries. ARM64 native remains LATER; this does not port the kernel.

title: Publish Wasm instantiation metrics against Linux Wasmtime
justification: 1.0 requires every §54 metric published versus Linux/Windows/macOS with no unmeasured claim. Re-runs B-047 on Tier 1 against the register baselines. Harness landed at V1.

title: Reproduce Wasm AOT artefacts bit-for-bit
justification: V4 reproducible-builds gate applied to Wasm AOT images in Package. Two independent builders emit identical content-addressed artefacts for the same WIT world and module.

title: Specify Wasm Component artefact layout in Package
justification: V0.5 Package format and the critique to reserve kind fields before the first immutable install. WASM names the Component-kind artefact (module, WIT world, requested Capability); PKG owns the manifest schema.

title: Study Component Model and WASI as native-model inputs
justification: V0 L1-informing spike in the FIDL class: WIT, resources, interface versioning and WASI capability interfaces feed the V0 IDL and Component Decisions. V0 scope-out bars Wasm integration beyond an ADR, not this study.

title: Version WIT worlds across native Channel endpoints
justification: V1 freezes Layer 2 evolution rules. Wasm Components must honor the same forward/backward Channel compatibility tests as machine-code endpoints so WIT is not a second versioning story. IPC owns the rules; WASM exercises them on the host.

title: Publish WASI subset conformance for third-party Components
justification: V3 public repository and third-party packages. A documented WASI/WIT subset with a runnable suite so external Wasm Components instantiate under the host import Decision.

title: Document Wasm Component authoring against native Interface
justification: V3 documentation gate for strangers shipping packages. Layer 2/3 authoring guide for WIT worlds, Capability requests and Package artefacts. DOC owns L1 ABI pages; WASM owns this host guide.

title: Adopt existing Steam, Wine, Proton and Bottles libraries in place
justification: Detect Steam libraries, Wine prefixes, Proton compatdata and Bottles/Lutris configs on attached volumes and adopt them without re-download.

title: Decide the kernel-level anti-cheat policy
justification: Critique: V1 anti-cheat adr. Options: refuse kernel-level anti-cheat; offer VIRT fallback; vendor engagement. Bypass is an explicit nongoal. Vendor contracts are anticheat-vendors at V3.

title: Study kernel-level anti-cheat feasibility under the Capability model
justification: Critique pulls the anti-cheat study to V1 so the policy adr is not a V2 cliff. Per-vendor (EAC, BattlEye, kernel-mode) compatibility and which systems cannot work under capabilities.

title: Decide anti-cheat vendor engagement and required legal agreements
justification: EAC/BattlEye agreements and whether the project entity can sign them (GOV GAP-0040 is the entity). Options: no vendor deals in 1.0; userspace-only titles; pursue contracts. Does not relax anticheat-policy.

title: Close High and Critical Windows personality findings from the audit
justification: V4 exit: external security audit of personalities; all High/Critical fixed and re-verified. WIN owns Windows personality findings.

title: Publish titles blocked by kernel-level anti-cheat as a nongoal
justification: Public list of games blocked by kernel-level anti-cheat; bypass remains a nongoal. V2 users judging the milestone by those titles need the honest page.

title: Decide the case-insensitive view for Windows personality storage
justification: Case-insensitive, case-preserving semantics must not leak into native or Linux views. Options: Wine lookup; per-prefix overlay; filesystem casefold in the personality view only (STO personality-view-api).

title: Route Windows open and save dialogs through the native file chooser
justification: Pulled from V3: V2 exit names the native file chooser. GetOpenFileName/IFileDialog return UserSelected capabilities, not ambient paths.

title: Lint the tree against the Windows personality clean-room policy
justification: Invariant collapsed to CI: fail the build on disassembly artefacts, leaked-source contributor markers, and bundled Microsoft fonts or unsigned redistributables.

title: Decide a clean-room policy for the Windows personality
justification: Must precede Wine bring-up. Options: Wine's rules as-is; stricter contributor affidavits; allow per-prefix redistributables that EXTRA-029 needs versus a ban on all Microsoft binaries. Resolves the GAP-0025 versus EXTRA-029 tension.

title: Bridge the Windows clipboard onto the native clipboard Capability
justification: V2 exit: Windows applications use the native clipboard. UIP owns clipboard policy and unified types; WIN implements the Wine/OLE side.

title: Provide COM and OLE for W1 productivity applications
justification: W1 corpus includes 15 productivity applications that require COM/OLE (Office-class, installers, shell links). Wine COM enabled inside the prefix, not as a native API.

title: Write the Windows personality chapters of the compatibility guide
justification: 1.0 documentation gate: compatibility guide complete. DOC owns the book; WIN authors Windows personality chapters, W3 how-to and the unsupported matrix.

title: Deliver native keyboard, mouse and pointer input to Windows applications
